to keep you away.  The path south is open for you to take.

Exits.Description: The path thickens.

rooms.Name: On a gradually sloping hill
rooms.Description:
Surrounded by thorn bushes to the north and south, the forest seems
to be pushing you down the hill to the east.  Moving west would require 
a hard climb.  To the east, however, the stench of sulfur and fire seems
stronger.

Exits.Description: The hill slopes gently east.
It's uphill all the way.

rooms.Name: Faint sounds of merriment
rooms.Description:
From the north you can hear faint but unmistakable noises of
laughter and singing.  The path north heads up a steep slope.  The main 
path runs east-west here.

Exits.Description: The wide path continues.
Sounds of laughter and music.
Sure looks dark down there.

rooms.Name: Downhill from fun
rooms.Description:
The path through the trees has narrowed once again.  Uphill from
here, you hear voices singing and the thrumm of a tambourine, the click 
of finger cymbals.  Downhill, you can see a more well-defined, wider 
path.  The small path you are on also branches west.

Exits.Description: The faint path becomes fainter as you head west.
You hear the sounds of an elven encampment.
A broad path makes its way through the forest.

rooms.Name: Amidst the maples
rooms.Description:
You follow the faint path between tall maple trees.  The unusual
clustering of these trees gives the impression they were planted by a
hand more orderly than nature's.  The path continues north for a short
distance and to the east the path looks a bit more traveled.

Exits.Description: A small glade.
A path up a steep hill

rooms.Name: A small glade
rooms.Description:
A small but lovely break in the trees has been created here by the
woodcutter's axe.  This borders of this area are formed by different
varieties of maple.  It is a lovely place to be in the fall.  The only
path out leads south.

Exits.Description: The path takes a sharp turn

rooms.Name: Elven encampment
rooms.Description:
A small group of wood elves have set up camp here recently.  Known
for their great joy in life and fondness for good song and good stories,
the wood elves are more relaxed than many of their more noble-seeming
cousins.  The encampment continues to the north and east of here.

Exits.Description: The elven encampment
The elven encampment
Down the steep hill towards a broader path

rooms.Name: A circle of fire
rooms.Description:
An enticing circle of flame invites you to sit and relax.  What
could be dangerous in the deep forests of Tynstri?  The elves have told 
you stories of large numbers of dragons who live near here, but surely
those are just stories.  When you finish your stay at this encampment,
you can return by the path to the west.

Exits.Description: The western way

rooms.Name: A merry time was had by all
rooms.Description:
Surrounded by maple and birch, the wood elves have extended their
camp in this lovely clear space in the woods.  The forest floor is hard
beneath your feet, and there is a chill in the air that is not entirely
due to the weather or the general forest gloom.  You may leave this
spot by heading south down the hill.

Exits.Description: It's all downhill from here!

rooms.Name: White birch path
rooms.Description:
White birch and blue spruce line this part of the path, alternating
like some strange flag.  The stench of dragon breath and the heat of
dragon fires are strong here.  You must be near the source.  The path
westwards is uphill, and you are looking for a cave entrance.  The path
east looks promising, as the trees seem to have been thinned.  The path
south leads steeply down, though, to a cave mouth.  That must be it!

Exits.Description: The birch and spruce seem thinner
A broad path, well-trampled
The path down and south leads to a dark cave.  Do you have a lantern?

rooms.Name: Neatly cut stumps
rooms.Description:
From the neatly cut stumps of oak and maple, it's clear that a band
of woodcutters have been through here.  The critters who used to dwell 
in the branches of those trees have been evicted to find shelter
elsewhere.  The path continues north and west from here.

Exits.Description: The stumps continue
A gloom seems to settle over the path

rooms.Name: Stumping along
rooms.Description:
A stack of logs lies here waiting to be carted off to a sawmill.
For quite a distance in all directions there is nothing but short tree
stumps, a few of which still bleed.  You may leave this sad place to
the south.

Exits.Description: A faint path through thinning woods.

rooms.Name: The Mouth
rooms.Description:
You are standing at the mouth of a long tunnel leading deep into the
earth.  It is very dark and forbidding.  The air is fetid, damp, with a
faint sulphurous odor.  You may descend into who-knows-what, head west
to reconnoiter, or head up the hill.

Exits.Description: A small area to sit and think
Up the hill to deep forest
A long, dark, forbidding tunnel

rooms.Name: A place to think
rooms.Description:
A quiet little space to the west of the entrance to a very large
(and very dark and smelly) cave is a good place for a picnic, or to 
simply stop and think about your options.  Are you safer facing the 
gobble-uns of the forest or the dragons who surely must populate the 
cave?

Exits.Description: The cavemouth is ready to eat you up.

rooms.Name: Dragon exit tunnel
rooms.Description:
A long tunnel leads steadily upwards into fresh air.  To the west, a
rough passage slopes rapidly down a long passageway.  It is difficult
to see anything in any direction due to the slant of the tunnel.

Exits.Description: Fresh air seems to be coming to you from a distance
There is too much of an angle to see much of anything.

rooms.Name: Kerbumpety thump
rooms.Description:
As you bump your way down the slope you begin to worry you will be
unable to scramble back up again should you need to leave in a hurry.
Your nostrils fill with the definite, clear stench of dragon breath.
Lots of dragons.  You can TRY to head up the sloping tunnel or you can
kerbumpety thump your way west.

Exits.Description: Can't see much
Can't see much

rooms.Name: All growed up
rooms.Description:
Or almost all growed up dragons find their way out this exit and the
larger one which is up the slope from here.  From this spot you catch a
whiff of werewolf up a very small tunnel, but it's difficult to sort
that odor out over the overwhelming scent of dragon.

Exits.Description: The narrow tunnel continues up
The scent of wolf is faintly discernible.
A well lit corridor

rooms.Name: Dragon Queen's doorstep
rooms.Description:
Standing at the northern end of the long north-south hallway that
forms a large part of the dragon living quarters, you are awed by the 
size and grandeur of the caverns.  Although the roof towers high above 
you, it has been beautifully smoothed, and it glows of its own accord,
bathing the quarters in a soft light.  A sign on the gilt door to the
north reads, "Dragin Kween's hom"

Exits.Description: There is an elaborate gilt door
The well-lit corridor continues.
A dark and narrow tunnel.  Looks forbidding.

rooms.Name: Dragon Kitchen
rooms.Description:
Neatly kept and well-stocked, the elf slaves who work here have made
the best of their captivity.  The excellence of their cooking has made
them favorites of the dragon children as well as the queen, and their
every wish is granted.  Every one except for freedom.  The entrance to
the QueEn's quarters is east of here.

Exits.Description: QueEn's quarters' entrance

rooms.Name: Entrance to the DraGoN QueEn's home
rooms.Description:
An expensively furnished (if somewhat tacky) entrance room, this is
where visitors to her majesty must wait to be heard. The carpet is a
deep crimson, and the walls a deep violet.  There are two massive plush
velvet sofas placed facing each other in the center of the room.  One
is fuchsia, the other a deep purple. There is a wide space between the
seat of the sofa and the backrest, presumably to allow dragging tails
room to hang over the back edge.  Round stools of plush velvet are
scattered like bright pink polka dots around the room.

Exits.Description: The room of consorts
A gilt door leads into the hatchlings area
A heavy oak swinging door leads west to the kitchen

rooms.Name: The room of consorts
rooms.Description:
The queen's many consorts sit in this lovely room, waiting on her
pleasure.  They preen in the many mirrors and play games amongst
themselves to prove individual superiority.  They are always listening
for a call from their queen, whose rooms are west of here.

Exits.Description: A waiting room
QueEn's chambers

rooms.Name: The lair of the DraGon QueEn
rooms.Description:
Red velvet softens the walls and dims the magic glow, which is quite
strong here.  The queen is not fond of being closely observed.  She
rarely leaves her lair, preferring for her subjects to be brought to
her.

Exits.Description: The consort room

rooms.Name: Spider Webs
rooms.Description:
For some reason these huge spider webs have remained clustered on
the walls here.  They partially obstruct the passage, which leads
north-south with a short jaunt west.  The dragons are not particularly
adept at housekeeping, but fragile stuff like spider webs is usually
burned away by one of the hatchlings' practicing.

Exits.Description: The cave continues
The cave continues
A small alcove

rooms.Name: A small alcove
rooms.Description:
Eeeeeeeeuuuuuuuwwwww!  The cave floor of this tiny alcove in the
cavern is covered with bat droppings!  The dragons call this their
"batting range".

Exits.Description: A large cave corridor

rooms.Name: A nursery corner
rooms.Description:
This whole area of the great underground dragon caves is devoted to
raising the next generation of fire breathers.  The walls are marked
randomly with scorch marks.  Young dragons have little control over
their fiery breath.  It is something they must learn in dragon school.
From here the nursery continues east, and the corridor runs
north-south.

Exits.Description: Cobwebs!
Soft pastels
A playground for small dragons

rooms.Name: Soft pastel colors
rooms.Description:
Before they become accustomed to the bright jewel tones favored by
adult dragons, young dragons are raised in soft, calming colors of
mint, pink, powder blue, cream and sunshine.  The cavern floor is
covered with soft sand to protect baby dragon feet.  The nursery
continues east, or you may find older dragons to the west.

Exits.Description: More of the nursery
The main north south corridor of the living quarters

rooms.Name: Between nursery and schoolroom
rooms.Description:
Standing outside the dragon schoolroom you hear the sleep-inducing
monotone of the dragon master, dragging on about emergency measures -
how to extinguish fires you didn't mean to start.  How extremely dull!
You might peek in at the schoolroom to the east, or head towards the
baby cries to the south.

Exits.Description: You hear the dragon master's boring voice.
You hear baby dragon cries.
The soft pastels of a dragon nursery

rooms.Name: Dragon schoolroom
rooms.Description:
Little round dragon stools dot the floor in an orderly pattern.
Small dragons sit on many of them, little tails draping over the 
edge.  From the number of empty stools it looks like not all the 
little dragons can be talked into going to school.

Exits.Description: The nursery corridor

rooms.Name: Nursery west
rooms.Description:
Newly hatched dragons spend some time in this enormous room.  The
adult dragons have smoothed out the walls and covered the floor with 
a soft white sand, but that has been their only concession to the 
necessities of dragon infancy.  Adult dragons meddle very little in 
the affairs of their offspring.

Exits.Description: A hallway
The nursery continues

rooms.Name: Nursery east
rooms.Description:
Remnants of nursery meals - bits of bugs, wingtips from bats - lie
on the sandy nursery floor beside forgotten or discarded toys.  The room
is bathed in a warm soft glow without any obvious source.  The nursery
is very roomy, fortunately so, as some of the clutches of eggs lately
have been much larger than usual. The egg hatchery is south of here,
and the infant nursery continues to the west.

Exits.Description: Sounds of eggs breaking
The nursery continues

rooms.Name: Hatchery
rooms.Description:
Bits of shell from dragon eggs litter the floor.  A few large eggs
lie dormant in the center, under a stream of pure white light coming 
from a small crack in the ceiling. Listening closely, you can barely 
hear the chanting of wiccan monks pouring through the crack with the 
light.

Exits.Description: You hear childish dragon voices

rooms.Name: Southern end of a long dragon hallway
rooms.Description:
The hallway here stretches from the practice room just south of here
all the way to the queen's quarters far to the north.  Although the
walls have been smoothed and well lit, the floor remains hard.  Perhaps
it serves to toughen little dragon feet before they pad out into the
forest.

Exits.Description: The hallway continues
Looks like a practice range
The molting area

rooms.Name: Practice Range
rooms.Description:
Here, at a dead end of the hallway, in the part of the cavern at
once furthest away from queen and from hatchlings, the young dragons 
have a spot to test their skills.  The southern, western and eastern 
walls are covered with scorch marks and deep gouges into the wall.  
The trainees look like they'd love to practice with a live target!

Exits.Description: The grand hallway of dragondom begins

rooms.Name: Molting area
rooms.Description:
This simple room in the dragon quarters leads south to the
entranceway and east to the grand hallway.  Here, the walls are plain, 
the young dragons have tracked some sand from the nursery onto the cave 
floor.  Young dragons molting out of their first skins have used a large 
rough area on the northern wall as a large scratching post.  Small 
patches of dragon skin have been left where they were caught by the rock.

Exits.Description: The grand hallway
The entranceway

rooms.Name: A small space with a large sign
rooms.Description:
A relatively small cave within the underground network, you find
your voice echoes eerily off the solid rock walls.  The sound of 
trickling water comes from through the crack in the south wall, and 
there is a very large sign here presumably to catch the attention of 
adventurers entering the caves from that direction.

Exits.Description: The passageway continues north.
You hear trickling water.
The cave gets darker.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
In very large, clumsily written letters you read:

                       Dragin Homland and Stomping Ground
                                Du Not Dysterb!

rooms.Name: Small crypt in a large catacomb
rooms.Description:
A large polished archway leads northwards.  The archway has been
smoothed, and the walls are filled with paintings of dragons enjoying
themselves in a hundred different pleasures.  There is some lettering
over the archway identifying this area, and a small sign at eye level.

Exits.Description: The crypt
A very small cave

ExtraDescriptions.Description: The lettering reads, "Dragon Catacombs"

The sign consists of a huge arrow pointing north and the following
crude lettering:
 
                              Dragin Treshur

rooms.Name: A dark and lonely place
rooms.Description:
Tis written that the grave is "a dark and lonely place".  Dragons 
don't spend much time reading, however.  North of you lies a large 
memorial to the Great Undead Dragon (GUD), and to the west the 
brightly-lit Trail of the Undead begins.  This one little room is quiet 
and dark.

Exits.Description: A GUD memorial
An arched entrance
On the trail of the undead

rooms.Name: A GUD memorial
rooms.Description:
This enormous cavern is covered floor to ceiling in bright colors.
Murals depicting stories from the legendary Great Dragon cover every
surface.  In the center of the floor there are two huge depressions the
exact size of the Great Dragon's footprints.  Every so often one of
this dragon generation will sneak in here to see how he or she is
measuring up, and wonder what happened to the GUD treasure hoard.
There is a small sign on one wall.

Exits.Description: The catacombs entrance

ExtraDescriptions.Description: He was GUD to all us draginz

rooms.Name: Southern end of the Trail of the Undead
rooms.Description:
This area of the great underground caves is colorfully known as the
Trail of the Undead.  Those dragons who, dying, fail to make the great
flight wander these halls.  Here they play some of the same games and
pranks they enjoyed when alive.  The corridor leads north for a ways,
or you may head east towards the entrance to the Dragon Catacombs.

Exits.Description: The Trail of the Undead
A dark and lonely waiting place

rooms.Name: The Trail of the Undead
rooms.Description:
The cavern walls are covered with murals depicting great dragons and
their treasures.  The light flooding the corridor appears to make the
painted jewels glow.  There is something about this light that makes
your skin crawl.

Exits.Description: The northern end of the corridor
A brightly lit corridor of rock

rooms.Name: Northern end of the corridor
rooms.Description:
The cave walls have been elaborately painted in the jewel tones the
dragons love - ruby, topaz, sapphire, emerald, amethyst.  Dragons are
very fond of collecting and hoarding treasures and over a long lifetime
can build up a huge store of riches.  Nobody is entirely certain what
happens to the treasure when a dragon dies.  Some say they take it with
them.

Exits.Description: The murals continue
The murals continue

rooms.Name: An intersection in the dragon catacombs
rooms.Description:
To the south and west are large crypts lined with shelves.  There is
a long corridor leading north from here and this room continues east.
The room is brightly lit, and you begin to FEEL the magic saturating
the air.

There is a large sign hanging from the ceiling.

Exits.Description: A corridor leading north
The room continues east
A small room in the catacombs
A small room in the catacombs

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
A large arrow points north, and the sign reads:

                           Enormuss Pile of Golld and Jules!

rooms.Name: A small crypt in the catacombs
rooms.Description:
This is a very small crypt, lined with shelves.  The shelves are
lined with jars made from volcanic glass.  The jars are filled with the 
ashes of those dragons whose remains could be captured before they were 
blown away by the winds of fate.  Some of the jars have been opened, 
perhaps by greedy adventurers in search of treasure.

Exits.Description: The trail through the catacombs

rooms.Name: Yet another small crypt
rooms.Description:
You are in a small, brightly lit room, again saturated with magic
light.  The walls are painted with pictures of the great dragon
treasures amassed by famous dragons of long ago.  There is a small
trail of ashes from an urn which has spilled.

Exits.Description: Another small crypt
The corridor through the catacombs

rooms.Name: Following the Catacomb Path
rooms.Description:
The rock of the cavern floor is hard against your feet, but the
ground is fairly level as you follow the clearly marked path through the
dragon burial grounds.  The catacombs are fairly thickly populated with
departed dragons who have yet to learn the meaning of "eternal rest".

Exits.Description: The catacombs continue
The catacombs continue
A small crypt lies to the west

rooms.Name: A large dark vault
rooms.Description:
Unlike the rest of the catacombs that you have seen so far, this
vault is painted in dark, gloomy colors, the colors of night and mud and 
the dark side.  There are vaults in the wall containing glass coffins.
Some of the coffins contain dragon bodies with large wooden stakes
protruding from them.  Looking around for some understanding of what
you see, you spot a small sign.

Exits.Description: The catacomb corridor
A small crypt

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Here lie the bodies of those few dragons who were truly evil.  We have
skewered them to their coffins in hopes that they will thus not arise
against us, and we have enclosed them in glass that we may look upon
them and revile them.  And keep an eye on them just in case.

rooms.Name: Serpentine corridor
rooms.Description:
The catacomb path curves sharply here.  The walls as well as the
ceiling glow with a creepy magic light.  You wonder at the effect of
this magic on growing young things.  You may follow the path of
increasing light to the west or head down the corridor to the south.
There is a large sign here to help you decide.

Exits.Description: A catacomb corridor, ending in a small crypt
A brighter glow

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
There is a large arrow pointing west, and the words:
 
               Hed West to the Lejenderry Dragin Treshur!

rooms.Name: More catacombic twists
rooms.Description:
The catacomb path continues to twist here, curving from north to
east.  The walls are glowing with a soft topaz light, reminding you of 
the dragons' love for that gem.  The ceiling is glowing with the 
dazzling white light of a thousand diamonds.  The glow continues to the 
north and decreases slightly to the east.

Exits.Description: Dazzling
A softer glow

rooms.Name: Near the source
rooms.Description:
Walls, ceiling and floor all glow with bright jewel colors.  Could
the amassed treasure of all the dragons who have passed away be the 
source of this light and color?  Could you possibly grab some of the 
fabulous fortune for yourself?  If it is as large as is rumored, they 
could easily spare you a few small jewels!  

There is another sign here.

Exits.Description: A bright glow
A softer glow

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It points east.
 
                 Fabulus Jules!  Dragin Treshur for them with Kerage!

rooms.Name: Near the Glowing Light
rooms.Description:
The light and heat coming from the east is overpowering.  You feel
drawn there, compelled almost against your will as you have all along
this long journey through the caves.  You are frightened at the
outpouring of magic from the room.  It will take enormous resolve to
turn back the way you came, but that is by far the safer route.  Is
this next room truly the storehouse of dragon treasure?  or a trap set
by canny dragons?  There is a large sign here which may offer you some
advice.

Exits.Description: Dragon Crematorium
A turn in the catacombs

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Like others in the catacombs, this sign features a gigantic arrow (this
one is glowing and flashing and pointing east) and some writing:
 
                         Huge Heap uv Dragin Treshur!

rooms.Name: The Great Dragon Crematorium
rooms.Description:
You have stepped into the crematorium and been burned to ashes.
What did you expect to happen in a crematorium?

rooms.Name: The cave tunnel
rooms.Description:
An endless tunnel drops rapidly down into the cool stone walls of an
underground cave.  Although most cave passages are formed by the
actions of water over millenia, this particular passageway appears to
have been formed by a blasting heat.  You try to remember what little
you once knew about volcanoes.

Exits.Description: Fresh air
The perils of a network of underground caves.

rooms.Name: On The Swift Flowing River
rooms.Description:
The deep river flows east and west through a dense forest.  Over the
ages, the river has cut through the bedrock to form a particularly deep
channel for itself.  The banks of the river are very steep, and appear to
be very slippery, so it would be quite impossible to leave the river and
enter the forest.

rooms.Name: The Riverbank
rooms.Description:
The river is deep, and runs swiftly in an east-west direction.  To 
the north the river eddies and enters a backwash where a small bank 
extends down from a dark, thick stand of trees.  However, it doesn't 
look particularly inviting.

rooms.Name: The Twisty Part Of The River
rooms.Description:
The river twists and turns and nearly tosses you out of your boat.
The water is dark, cold, almost reptilian in sheen.  It seems almost
alive.  The river runs east and south.

rooms.Name: The Scenic Route
rooms.Description:
The dark forest of Haon-Dor recedes behind you to the northeast.
The river continues in a westerly direction toward the river delta,
where you can just make out a large island.

rooms.Name: The Swift River Delta
rooms.Description:
You are at the edge of the river delta, where the river empties
out on its way to the sea.  The water here is Black.  Deep.  Dark.
Deadly.  The tidal waves sweep you around and around up and down.

rooms.Name: Near The Rocks
rooms.Description:
You bob up and down in the waves, coming dangerously close to some
large, jagged rocks on the eastern shore of an unusual looking island.
There is no way you could possibly land there without getting killed.

rooms.Name: The South River Delta
rooms.Description:
You are making your way along a channel in the river delta between
the island to the west and the shore to the south and east.  To the
south an aging, run down looking pier juts out from land. Toward the 
west the channel works it way close to the island as it moves around
its southern tip.

rooms.Name: The Pier
rooms.Description:
You float next to a crumbling pier long since neglected. To the west 
the water gets sluggish and there are many weeds and some seaweed 
floating about.

rooms.Name: Mired In Seaweed
rooms.Description:
The going is rough here.  The tide struggles with the normal flow
of the river and here near the edge of the sea there is a large
amount of growth.  To the west the channel passes the southern tip of
the island and heads for open waters.

rooms.Name: The Last Stop
rooms.Description:
The delta meets the sea here.  To the west you see nothing but
ocean on the horizon.  Sea birds squawk noisily at your approach
and take flight from a nearby beach head on the island.  It looks
as though this could be the last stop for those heading out to sea.

rooms.Name: The Beach Head
rooms.Description:
This is a secluded looking beach on the southern tip of the island.
There isn't much to see here and there is no way to cross the steep
rocky cliffs that wall in this place.

rooms.Name: The North Channel
rooms.Description:
The river splits and runs up against the island and a navigable
channel slips off to the north and west.

rooms.Name: The North Channel
rooms.Description:
The river current carries you swiftly westward as the channel
begins to narrow as it squeezes past the north end of the island.

rooms.Name: Near The Isle
rooms.Description:
You are sitting just off a small landing on the island that 
appears to be nothing more than a short path that leads to the
side of a hill.

rooms.Name: The Lane Of The Lying
rooms.Description:
Bodies lie everywhere.  Commoner, peasant, duke, duchess.  The Gods
will not hear your call here, hence they will not answer you.  To the
south the path ends at a dark cave entrance.
A sign has been posted beside the entrance.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
A sign beside the dark cave opening reads:

   WARNING! Only fools and dead people pass this way.
   The tests of Crete, our glorious ruler, await.

rooms.Name: The First Trial Of Crete
rooms.Description:
Ah... you find yourself in Crete's battlefield playground.  Crete 
loves to torture his people through these places.  He collects the 
monsters of the world and puts them here.

rooms.Name: The Second Trial Of Crete
rooms.Description:
Crete's voice reverberates from the four walls of this room:
'Get some rest and make sure you're healed.  You'll need it for
the next monster in my playground.  Or are you strong enough?'
To the south is the entrance to the next challenge of Crete's
stronghold.

rooms.Name: The Third Trial Of Crete
rooms.Description:
You go inside a red room.  Very red.  As if the Crete King used
them to disembowel his guests.  The path continues eastward.  You
see blue lights in that direction.

rooms.Name: The Fourth Trial Of Crete
rooms.Description:
Crete must be a monster hacking machine.  You see a blue light
flicker on and off.  A voice crackles, 'WHY ARE YOU HERE!'

rooms.Name: The Fifth Trial Of Crete
rooms.Description:
This is General Woundwort's quarters.  Hraka abound.  The frayed
corpses of rabbits lie scattered about this hell-hole.  The General
is not a very neat person as you can tell.

rooms.Name: The Sixth Trial Of Crete
rooms.Description:
Dare we surmise how many more rooms Crete has?  The paths appear to 
be endless.  You shudder as the sounds of death cries from the east.  
A loud voice bellows another warning: 'Leave now or face my wrath!' 
There is a crawlway leading upwards at the far end of the room and 
there is a fresh breeze coming from there.

rooms.Name: The Final Trial Of Crete
rooms.Description:
This is Minos' room.  What else did you expect?  The room is lavishly
decorated for this bovine king.  Everything is so opulent that it makes
your eyes bulge.  Survive and reap his fortune!  The only exit is a 
large oak door in the east wall.

Exits.Description: You see a rather large oak door bound with iron and securely locked.

rooms.Name: The Royal Chamber
rooms.Description:
The treasure room of Crete is dark save for your lantern.  
Hopefully it has not been looted yet by the many legendary 
thieves of Midgaard. A clever looking secret passage leads 
upward from here.

rooms.Name: Above, On The Beach
rooms.Description:
You sit amongst the rocks above a small beach at the southern end 
of the island.  You could clamber down easy enough, but getting back 
up would be another story.

rooms.Name: At the Mouth of the Xynarr River
rooms.Description:
As the brownish waters of the Xynarr River meet the crystal blue waters
of the vast ocean, they mix to form a cloudlike haze.  The mighty river
empties the debris and silt that it has carried from the north into the
ocean, thankful to be rid of its burden.  The river continues into a large
forest to the north, and to the south is an enormous ocean.  At the eastern
edge of the river's mouth is a peacful beach, created from the very debris 
left by the river.

rooms.Name: At the Edge of the Xynarr River
rooms.Description:
The mighty Xynarr River flows into the ocean just west of here.  Its
brownish waters churn as they reluctantly greet the warm blue waters of the
ocean.  A large forest extends to the north, but the density of the
underbrush makes it impossible to head in that direction.  A small beach
extends to the east and south, and the river lies to the west.

rooms.Name: The Edge of the Forest
rooms.Description:
A large forest of fragrant pine meets the edge of the peaceful beach.
The tall trees stand majestically, guarding their smaller brothers from the
onslaught of wind and salt from the ocean.  The dense underbrush that grows
between them makes it impossible to venture into the forest to the north,
but the beach continues in every other direction.

rooms.Name: The Edge of the Forest
rooms.Description:
A large forest of fragrant pine meets the edge of the peaceful beach.
The tall trees stand majestically, guarding their smaller brothers from the
onslaught of wind and salt from the ocean.  The dense underbrush that grows
between them makes it impossible to venture into the forest to the north,
but the beach continues to the west and south.

rooms.Name: The Aquatic Meeting Place
rooms.Description:
The hazy waters churn as the Xynarr River empties itself into the vast
ocean.  A small beach lies east of here, covered with debris from both the
river and ocean.  To the south the ocean extends as far as you can see.

rooms.Name: A Peaceful Beach
rooms.Description:
The sandy beach is covered with debris left from the last high tide.
Bits of driftwood and seaweed litter the sand, and create wonderful hiding
places for the tiny creatures that inhabit the beach.  A vast ocean extends
to the south for as far as you can see.  The beach continues to the east
and north, and to the west is a hazy mix of marine and fresh waters where
the Xynarr River meets the ocean.

rooms.Name: A Peaceful Beach
rooms.Description:
The sandy beach is covered with debris left from the last high tide.    
Bits of driftwood and seaweed litter the sand, and create wonderful hiding
places for the tiny creatures that inhabit the beach.  A vast ocean extends
to the south for as far as you can see.  The beach continues in every other
direction, and not far to the north is a large forest.

Bits of driftwood and seaweed litter the sand, and create wonderful hiding
places for the tiny creatures that inhabit the beach.  A vast ocean extends

direction, and not far to the north is a large forest.

Bits of driftwood and seaweed litter the sand, and create wonderful hiding
places for the tiny creatures that inhabit the beach.  A vast ocean extends
to the south for as far as you can see.  The beach continues to the west,
and not far to the north is a large forest.

rooms.Name: In the Shallows
rooms.Description:
The crystal blue waters have all but erased every trace of the large
river that flows into the ocean from the north.  The shallow waters
continue to the east and west, and the vast ocean continues for as far as
you can see to the south.

rooms.Name: In the Shallows
rooms.Description:
The shallow waters of the vast ocean are only waist deep here.  The 
gently rolling waves don't seem to be in any great hurry as they move past
you.  A peaceful beach is just north of here, and the ocean continues in   
every other direction.

you.  A small beach is just north of here, but the jagged rocks are too
treacherous to traverse.  The vast ocean continues to the south for as far
as you can see.

rooms.Name: On the Vast Ocean
rooms.Description:
The salty air and gently rolling waves of the ocean are making you just
a little seasick.  The ocean continues in every direction, but it appears
to become more shallow to the north.  In the distance you see a peaceful
beach, and beyond that a large forest.

rooms.Name: On the Vast Ocean
rooms.Description:
The salty air and gently rolling waves of the ocean are making you just
a little seasick.  The ocean continues in every direction for as far as you
can see, and not even a hint of land is anywhere to be found.  As you gaze
into the crystal blue waters, you can see that the ocean below you teems
with life.  Flashes of silver streak through the water, away from the
gaping mouths of unseen predators.  The vast ocean is a beautiful but
deadly place.

can see, and not even a hint of land is anywhere to be found.  As you gaze
into the crystal blue waters, you can see that the ocean below you teems
with life.  Flashes of silver streak through the water, away from the
gaping mouths of unseen predators.  The vast ocean is a beautiful but
deadly place.

a little seasick.  The ocean continues in every direction, but it appears
to become more shallow to the south.  In the distance you see a sandy
beach, and beyond that a vast jungle.

rooms.Name: In the Shallows
rooms.Description:
The shallow waters are only about waist deep on this part of the ocean.
The warm water feels quite soothing, and the gently rolling waves are
almost hypnotic.  To the south there is a sandy beach, but a terrible 
riptide makes passage in that direction very dangerous, if not impossible.

rooms.Name: On a Sandy Beach
rooms.Description:
The warm white sand of this beach has been meticulously groomed by the
forces of time and nature.  Waves gently lap at the edge of the beach as
they greet the land, only to be taken back out to sea by those behind them.
The vast waters of the ocean extend to the north for as far as you can see.
To the south is an tropical forest filled with all sorts of jungle life.

rooms.Name: At the Edge of the Jungle
rooms.Description:
As you near the edge of the jungle, the humidity nearly overwhelms your
senses.  The emerald curtain of trees hides a plethora of exotic life.  You
feel as if the eyes of the jungle are upon you as you near their tropical
home.

rooms.Name: Caught in the Riptide
rooms.Description:
As you struggle to break free from the riptide, you wish that you hadn't
attempted to pass through it!  You see a sandy beach to the south, but no
matter how hard you try to move towards it, the riptide insists upon
carrying you back out to sea.  You begin to grow quite tired from your
struggles.  You better think of a way out, fast!

rooms.Name: Gate to Tynstri
rooms.Description:
Tall, lacy ironwork gates painted a gleaming white are flanked by
guards in bright white uniforms.  The gates of Tynstri are open wide to
welcome all those who come in good faith to visit, to hunt or to shop
here.  The elves are always on the watch for evil, however, so better
watch your step!!

Exits.Description:
North of here you see a very tall circular white tower made of gleaming
white stone.
The road to town continues east.

South of here you see a very tall circular white tower made of gleaming
white stone.
Off to the west you see the rest of the world.

rooms.Name: Ground level of North Tower
rooms.Description:
You enter a dark, circular room, the only light filtering in from
the open door and from far up in the tower.  A narrow stone staircase
spirals clockwise around the stone wall.  You may leave by the door to
the city gate, or you may climb the spiral staircase leading up the
tower.

Exits.Description: Looking south you see the lacy white ironwork of the gates to Tynstri.
The top of the tower shines dimly above you.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Looks pretty rough and narrow to me.

rooms.Name: Spiraling around inside the North Tower
rooms.Description:
The spiral staircase seems to circle endlessly around and around the
stone staircase.  You are in almost total darkness.  The tower door is
far beneath you and the end of the staircase is nowhere in sight.  You
are tempted to cling to the stone walls as the stairs were made for
sure footed elves.

Exits.Description: Dim light filters through from above.
F-a-a-a-r below you lies the stone floor of the tower.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
They are old, and rough.  They tear at your clothes where you brush
against them.

rooms.Name: Atop the North Gate Tower
rooms.Description:
You emerge at the top of the tower, and the tower's purpose becomes
immediately obvious.  This tower faces eastward, toward the treetop
kingdom of the elves.    A fire here would be unthinkable, and you
understand the use of the large horn to the right of the watcher.

Exits.Description: You see an endlessly spiraling staircase leading down.

rooms.Name: Bottom of South Tower
rooms.Description:
This large, dark, circular room smells of mold and old moss.  The
bare stone walls support a large staircase, which circles 
counterclockwise up the tower.  The stone staircase looks sturdy and 
well kept, if perhaps a bit rough.  There is no handrail.  You may 
leave by the door to the gate or try your luck up the staircase.

Exits.Description: A heavy oaken door leads north.
Above you a staircase spirals endlessly.

rooms.Name: Part of the way up the South Tower of Tynstri
rooms.Description:
You circle endlessly between the hard stone floor far beneath you
and the dim light from above.  The watchtower really towers, you tell
yourself, as your legs grow tired.  You contemplate resting on one of
the steps, but they are REALLY narrow and VERY hard.

Exits.Description:
Looking up, all you can see is a small opening at the top of the
stairway far away.

W-a-a-a-y down, you see the stone floor of the tower and the large oak
door.

rooms.Name: Atop the South Gate Tower
rooms.Description:
During the day and on moonlit nights, the top of the tower is filled
with light from the large open area looking west.  From this watch
station a keen-sighted elf can see far into the forest surrounding
Tynstri.  The room is barren and comfortless.  The stone walls and
stone floor bespeak a hard life for the Watcher.

Exits.Description:
You see the wide expanse of forest and a narrow dirt road leading up to
the gates far below.
You see the beginnings of a long, spiraling staircase.  You feel dizzy.

rooms.Name: Near the Gates
rooms.Description:
A broad dirt road is well rutted from traffic coming to and from the
elven village of Tynstri.  Although a main thoroughfare for the town,
it retains a woodsy charm.  The trees grow thickly on both sides of the
road, and are hung with strong vines.

Exits.Description: More shops ...
The gates of Tynstri glow whitely.
The ladder appears to go up into the tree.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: You see a ladder dangling from a branch that is out of sight.

You see a sturdy ladder woven of thick vines of ivy.  You hope it's not
poisonous.

rooms.Name: Climbing a tree
rooms.Description:
You are pleased you practiced that silly climb-a-rope-ladder game at
the fair so many times, because it's not easy to traverse a ladder made
only of rope.  Your feet and hands scrape against the rough bark.   The
tree is about as big around as an elephant's leg, but looks sturdy
enough to hold your weight.  The bark is rough and deeply grooved and
seems loose in places.  The ladder continues up to a ledge of sorts and
down to the ground.  Better go up or down!

Exits.Description: Uh oh!  Is that bird droppings you feel on your face?
Down always looks safer, if more boring.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: It looks loose!

rooms.Name: On a wide branch
rooms.Description:
This not-very-thick tree has a surprisingly large branch.  It is
unfortunately rather covered with bird goo from the huge nest directly
above you.  You could reach up and gather the eggs if you were really
hungry, but the very large bird sitting on the nest looks like she
wants them more than you do.  Escape from this sticky situation is
either down the shaky rope ladder at your feet or taking a strong hold
of the vine at hand and swinging over to the tree north of here.

Exits.Description: A small platform awaits the brave.  There seem to be scorch marks ...
Back down the ladder.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It looks like a vulture.  A mother vulture.  A mother vulture with
several mouths to feed.  She's looking at you, sizing you up as food!

Hmm ... seems easy enough to swing over to that platform.  Remember not
to release the vine so you can get back!

rooms.Name: Broad Path into Town
rooms.Description:
The deep ruts in the hard packed dirt road bear evidence to the
numbers going to and from the fair town of Tynstri.  To the east you can 
see the first shops.  To the west, in the distance you see the tall iron 
gates, and above you, you hear the shouts and laughter of elven children
playing.

Exits.Description: The shops appear to be open.

The gates far to the west are tall, white, and enchanted with a
blessing to protect from evil.

rooms.Name: Tynstri Proper - Main Road
rooms.Description:
Tynstri is a local center for the healing arts, traffic in herbal
remedies, and a meeting place for elves.  The street here continues to
be well shaded with trees known for their magic properties.  From the
north come music and laughter and the sounds of a rowdy bunch having a
bit of fun.  To the south is a small storefront organization recruiting
hardy young elves over the age of 100 to ... well, perhaps you should
take a look and see.

Exits.Description:
A blue-black cloud of smoke emerges from the establishment north of
here.
The road continues east toward the center of town.
A brightly painted sign reads, "Free the Elves!"
You look back towards the entrance to town.

rooms.Name: A Sleazy Tavern
rooms.Description:
You have wandered into a sleazy tavern on the outskirts of Tynstri.
The bartender is a dainty elf wearing a skimpy top, a short leather 
skirt and high heeled boots.  She smiles at you as you walk in.  Just 
inside the door, two burly bouncers eye you with surly suspicion.  From 
the north, a cloud of dark gray cigar smoke streams through a curtain of
garishly colored purple, green and yellow beads.  There is a small sign
on the counter.

Exits.Description: This is a REALLY ugly curtain!
The street will be there when you decide to leave.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It reads:
     say    LIST         - to learn what you can buy here
            BUY   <item> - to buy something
            SELL  <item> - to sell something
            VALUE <item> - to find out how much I will pay for
            something that you wish to sell.

rooms.Name: Back Room
rooms.Description:
The boys in the back room are having a friendly game of poker.  This
is their home away from home, and you can see they've made it to their
liking.  The chairs evenly spaced around the center table are large and
sturdily made from solid oak.  The walls are covered with elven pinups
and racing ponies.

Exits.Description: A garish bead curtain in yellow, purple and green.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
You see quite a few pictures of scantily clad girl elves with names
like "Buttercup" and "Melody".

Lying in a field of yellow buttercups, wearing nothing but the flowers,
Buttercup's picture is enough to distract the most determined of poker
players.
Melody winks at you saucily.

rooms.Name: Elven underground
rooms.Description:
Free the Elven slaves!!! The wall is full of posters of famous elven
chefs, kidnapped and kept as slaves for the evil forces of the assassin
Gontran.  Eager young recruits to this cause will tell you the
assassins ate some of the more reluctant slaves.

Exits.Description:
You are so caught up with enthusiasm for the quest that you don't
notice the street is still outside!
One of the posters looks like it is falling off the wall.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
This is a particularly sad poster of Chef Boyardee, who was
mysteriously stolen right from his kitchen.  The chef's eyes seem to
follow you suspiciously around the room.

rooms.Name: Upstairs from the Free the Elves Foundation
rooms.Description:
Here's where the real radicals gather to train and to plot a serious
attempt on Gontran and his evil minions.  The room is bare except for a
table under the harsh light of a single lantern and a small practice
area along the opposite wall.  In a place of prominence, over the
table, there is a framed picture of the Foundation's hero, #bDazzlin'
Hambone#N, General in Chief of the Elven Armies.  He has been painted in
his full battle uniform with all his many decorations for valor.

Exits.Description: Down the secret stairs

rooms.Name: Shopping in Tynstri
rooms.Description:
As you wander slowly down the street, you are amazed at the number
and variety of shops. To the south you see the bright colors and sweet
scents of Flowers & Sweets, while north of you is Tynstri's fashion
spot, Second Hand Rose.

Exits.Description:
Looks intriguing.  Knights, monks, magicians ... all sorts appear to be
heading for Rose's.
To the east lie a couple of odd looking stores.
Mmmm, looks like a tasty kind of gift shop ...
You see a sleazy tavern and the Elf Foundation to the west.

rooms.Name: Second Hand Rose
rooms.Description:
Rose loves to collect new and used clothing and armor of all sorts.
The shop is alive with color and movement.  Battle hardened warriors
argue loudly about the best kits, and there is always a group looking
for something unique to just "hang" in.  The south wall of the shop is
covered with racks of social attire, from hats to shoes.  The eastern
and western walls hold more serious gear - armor for those eager to
fight and not die!  There is a small embroidered sign hanging over one
of the tables.

Exits.Description: The street beckons as if to say, "stop your dawdling and get busy!"

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It reads:
     say    LIST         - to learn what you can buy here
            BUY   <item> - to buy something
            SELL  <item> - to sell something
            VALUE <item> - to find out how much I will pay for
            something that you wish to sell.

rooms.Name: Flowers & Sweets
rooms.Description:
This is an all-occasion gift shop.  You can feed that sweet tooth of
yours, buy a funeral wreath in fond memory of your recently dead uncle
or a baby's breath bouquet to celebrate an adoption.  You might even
find some enchanted flowers or sweets in the collection.  Flora is,
after all, married to Seymour, the magic herbalist.  Seymour studied
with Henrietta for many years - until his love potions started to rock
and Flora told him he'd better stay closer to home!  There is a small
sign on the wall, hand embroidered by Flora herself.

Exits.Description: The street is still there.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Roses are red
Violets are blue
Sugar is sweet
So buy some of that too.
 
It continues:
     say    LIST         - to learn what you can buy here
            BUY   <item> - to buy something
            SELL  <item> - to sell something
            VALUE <item> - to find out how much I will pay for
            something that you wish to sell.

rooms.Name: Wandering through Tynstri
rooms.Description:
Trees with long branches and fingerlike leaves beautifully shade the
road through the center of town.  Are they moving with the breeze? or
are they waving at you?  There are many cheerful flowers planted at the
base of the trees, adding a touch of color to the natural greens and
browns of town and trees.  The sign on the store north of you is
peeling and not easily read, but it _looks_ like it once read "Elmer's
Oddities".  To the south, Barns & Nibble invites you to sit awhile,
read, nibble and chat with your friends.

Exits.Description: It looks like a curio shop, how curious!
Small explosions and noxious odors come from the east.

Barns & Nibble looks like a great place to while away an afternoon
amicably.
More street!

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
You're not sure of the variety, but there is a strangely sentient look
about these.  You are glad you are not expected to chop one down!
Colorful pansies  are planted around the base of each tree.

rooms.Name: Elmer's Oddities
rooms.Description:
Elmer's store is crammed with strange and unusual artifacts from all
corners of the kingdom.  This is a favorite haunt for those who delight
in the unusual, the arcane, the utterly useless.  Elmer looks as odd as
his store.  He mutters to himself as he sorts through his clutter.

Exits.Description: Back to the street.

rooms.Name: Barns & Nibble Café
rooms.Description:
This cafe feels like the living room of your great aunt right down
to the odd cats wandering through, brushing against your legs.
Comfortable chairs and tables fill the room, but the large plants and
screens provide an atmosphere of privacy where you can sit and chat.
The walls are lined with ancient books containing the wisdom of the
elder Elves.  This would be a cozy place to rest a while.  You notice a
sign hanging at the end of one of the shelves of books.

Exits.Description: The street is still north of here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It reads:
     say    LIST         - to learn what you can buy here
            BUY   <item> - to buy something
            SELL  <item> - to sell something
            VALUE <item> - to find out how much I will pay for
            something that you wish to sell.

"Nature in all Her Glory", by Brother Russ
"How to Prevent Forest Fires", by Crash, M.R.
"Mysteries of Magic", by Henrietta, M.H.

rooms.Name: Wandering through Tynstri
rooms.Description:
As you stroll down the dirt road that forms the main path through
Tynstri, you see to the east of you a beautiful green park. From the
north, the pungent scents of the herb shop intrigue and repulse you.
To the south you see a shop with the sign of a powerful arm flexing,
and from the crowd of adventurers heading into the store you can
suppose some sort of adventuring equipment must be sold there.

Exits.Description: A twin cloud of bright magenta and saffron yellow billows forth.
What a lovely park!
You see knights and soldiers coming out with shiny new weapons.
There is the oddest shop off west of here.

rooms.Name: Little Shop of Seymour's
rooms.Description:
Seymour has stocked his store with the best that nature has to
offer. He does the distilling himself, and frequent small explosions and
noxious odors come from the room you can glimpse through the partially
open door at the back of the shop.  The walls behind the counter are
lined floor to ceiling with beakers, bottles and boxes of all sizes and
shapes.  Suddenly from the back you hear a deep, petulant voice
screaming, "Feed Me!" and Seymour asks if you'd like to step on back to
his greenhouse and feed his plant.  There is a small unobtrusive sign
on the counter.

Exits.Description: Seymour's greenhouse lies north of here.
You can (and probably should) go back out to the street this way.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It reads:
     Be sure to visit my special pet, Audreyii, in my greenhouse!
     say    LIST         - to learn what you can buy here
            BUY   <item> - to buy something
            SELL  <item> - to sell something
            VALUE <item> - to find out how much I will pay for
            something that you wish to sell.

rooms.Name: Greenhouse
rooms.Description:
The back room of the herb and potion shop is a combination
greenhouse/distillery. Seymour grows some truly rare and unusual plants
here.  Some are huge, and reputed to be carnivorous.  The scents and
the warm humid air combine to overwhelm your senses, making you feel
drowsy.

Exits.Description: The main part of the store is south of here.
Hmm ... looks awfully ... _DARK_ down there!

rooms.Name: Myconoid Hangout
rooms.Description:
This earth cellar smells musty and dank, and with good reason.  This
is where Seymour cultivates his special mushrooms.  These are VERY 
special fungi, and don't take kindly to strangers intruding on them, 
bringing light and fresh air with them.

Exits.Description:
Relative safety, i.e. the myconoids have no relatives up there ... you
hope!

rooms.Name: Elven Arms
rooms.Description:
Horatio, the shopkeeper of the Elven Arms, doubles as a blacksmith
on non-market days, and his burly physique clearly is a reflection of
long, hot days spent over his forge.  He has a reputation for selling
only the sharpest of swords and knives, the heaviest of hammers and the
snappiest of whips in his shop.  He tells you, "You can buy with
confidence here."  Should you lose your confidence (or have not enough
gold) you can leave by the door to the street.  A small sign is sitting
on the counter.

Exits.Description: The street!

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It reads:
     Courtesy Tynstri Chamber of Commerce
     say    LIST         - to learn what you can buy here
            BUY   <item> - to buy something
            SELL  <item> - to sell something
            VALUE <item> - to find out how much I will pay for
            something that you wish to sell.

rooms.Name: Village Park
rooms.Description:
This small park lies at the end of the shopping area.  Other than
the Barns & Nibble store this is the gathering place for elves of 
Tynstri, a meeting place of sorts.  The park is, of course, surrounded 
by and filled with tall trees and small animals and birds.  The focal
point of the park is a small spring fed fountain.  Its source lies 
deep in the earth.

Exits.Description: The park is rather dimly lit north of here.
A shining stairway leads east and up.
The forest begins south of here.
The stores and village gathering places are to the west.

The small spring feeding the beautiful fountain has it's roots deep
underneath the earth's surface.  You might be able to swim into
the small cave from where the water bubbles.

rooms.Name: Northern End of the Park
rooms.Description:
You are at the northern boundary of the town park.  This end is
apparently more of a gathering for elven lowlife, and you feel
distinctly uneasy as you look about you.  Did you just see a furtive
movement over there by that tree?  And what about those seedy
characters sitting on the bench?  Accosted by the unwashed, you decide
quickly to head east up the hill towards the pair of buildings you see
or south towards the better-lit section of the park.

Exits.Description: The beautiful forests of Tynstri lie north of here
Looks like a pretty steep hill!
Very green.

rooms.Name: Forest path
rooms.Description:
This narrow path leads north to a small but inviting park, and south
into the darkness of a forest of tall trees and long, dangling vines.
The mass of branches overhead has blocked sunlight from the forest
floor to the extent that it is fairly clear of debris, making walking
easy.

Exits.Description: You see the happy sights and sounds of a city park.
It's getting d-a-a-r-r-r-k-k-e-r .....

rooms.Name: Creepy Forest
rooms.Description:
This path gives you a creepy feeling that something is vastly amiss.
The forest is gloomy.  The vines that once appeared to you like a
lovely green waterfall are now more menacing and dangerous.  The small
sounds of the forest are more sinister than cheerful.  The park is a
long ways off to the north, and the clearing to the south looks closer.
A rustle in the bushes makes you scurry on to your next destination.

Exits.Description: The forest looks clearer to the north.
This exit goes somewhere.
Whatever you see to the south, it's gotta feel safer than it does here!

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Looks like someone must be hiding there.
They are reaching out to you, grasping at you.

rooms.Name: Across a Creek
rooms.Description:
The dirt path abruptly stops at a narrow creek that appears quite
deep. The water looks cool, clear and just looking at it seems to make 
you thirsty.  You are disappointed that you will have to turn back to 
town so soon, then you notice a series of large flat rocks irregularly
spaced across the creek.  Some look a bit slippery and wet, but you
could cross the stream on the stones, or follow the creek to the east.

Exits.Description: It's too dark to see much ... a shadowed forest ...
The creek sounds louder to the east.

The forest continues, the trees growing larger and thicker to the
south.

rooms.Name: The Big Trees
rooms.Description:
The trees are all very very old here, their circumferences so wide
that a small band of rogues or a den of tigers could easily hide behind
them.  What was that noise?  Should you race off to the clearing north
of here?  Would you be safer plunging still deeper into the forest
further south?  Either way, you don't feel safe standing still!  Do
something!

Exits.Description: You smell a faint scent of water.
The trees all look so very ... BENT up ahead.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It is huge.  Yes.  And there is a head peeking out at you from behind
it.

rooms.Name: Faint Echoes of Music
rooms.Description:
From the south some faint music enraptures you, leaves you without
will to resist coming closer to its source.  The forest is very still 
here and you sense that even the forest listens to the beautiful melody
drifting this way.   The fir and rowan, yew and thistle all seem to bow
to the music coming from the south, behind that small thicket.

Exits.Description: You see some VERY LARGE trees.
The path stops at a large thicket.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Looks like you could easily move it aside, although at some cost to
your hands!

rooms.Name: Circle of Joy
rooms.Description:
You enter a large forest glade filled with incredibly beautiful
music. The glade is circular in shape.  The floor is covered with the 
softest green moss that you have ever seen, and you are sorely tempted 
to remove your shoes and run barefoot, letting the tiny tendrils tickle
your toes.  Planted around this part of the glade are herbs of joy:
catnip, morning glory, witchgrass and meadowsweet.  You may continue to
explore the glade to the east and south, or head north from here into
the gloom of the forest.

Exits.Description: Looks like a pretty thick thicket.
The circle continues to purify you.
The dryad's circle continues to be friendly.

rooms.Name: Circle of Purity
rooms.Description:
The dryads who care for this peaceful setting have planted herbs of
purification here - copal and iris, thistle, vervain and sage.  If you
are very lucky and very quiet, you may see the nymphs dancing here.
The nymphs are elves who do not mingle much with the rest of the world.
Very shy, they fade into the trees when confronted with the mundane.

Exits.Description: The dryad's circle continues to heal you.
An enormous tree beckons to you.
The dryad's circle continues joyfully.

rooms.Name: Circle of Healing
rooms.Description:
The beautiful glade continues south and west.   You see the patterns
of many feet on the soft moss floor, and know that this glade is sacred to
the dryads of this forest - the wood nymphs.  They come to this spot to
dance and celebrate the forest magic.  This section of the glade is
planted with many herbs of healing: viper's bugloss, whose prickly
hairs tickle your feet, and coltsfoot to make a tea for coughs.  At
your feet you find adder's tongue and fennel, burdock and garlic, and
this portion of the ring is made up of cedar trees.

Exits.Description: A cloud of color.
The circle continues purely.

rooms.Name: Circle of Friendship
rooms.Description:
You are standing in the western most part of a beautiful forest
glade, encircled with the dark green of the yew tree and silver-gray of the
rowan.  The bright red berries on the yew add a touch of brightness to
this misty green/gray world.  The music of the dryads, heard throughout
the clearing, is haunting.  This area is planted with herbs of
friendship: lemongrass, sweetpea and passionflower, and bordered with
pink tourmaline and turquoise.

Exits.Description: The circle continues joyfully.
Looks like a tree, something you've seen in a tapestry.
The circle continues with honor.

rooms.Name: Center of the circle
rooms.Description:
An enormous tree fills the center of the circle, tall and graceful,
its branches brushing the sky.  The tree is full as well as tall, 
branches spread wide over you, each covered with deep green leaves and 
soft pink and white blossoms.  The bark of the tree resembles a deeply 
rippled river of chocolate - smooth and dark, with deep ridges and 
swirls.

Exits.Description: The pure circle continues.
The circle continues in a comradely manner.
The dryad's circle continues strongly.
You see a moving cloud of color.

rooms.Name: A cloud of butterflies
rooms.Description:
You have walked into a cloud of moving color.  Soft flashes of
green, mauve, yellow, gold, aqua and lavender brush against you, 
bewildering you until one alights on your arm and you see that 
butterflies surround you.  You look about you and see the circle 
continues north and south, and the center of the circle beckons 
to you from the west.  There are several large vitex plants here 
attracting the butterflies.

Exits.Description: The dryad's circle continues joyfully.
The dryad's circle continues in good health.
There appears to be something white under an enormous tree.

rooms.Name: Circle of Honor
rooms.Description:
This southernmost point of the circle honors courage, divination and
spirituality, and it has been planted with camphor, orris, mugwort and
dragon's blood, thyme and yarrow, frankincense and gardenia.  The
circle is sweet and pungent, colorful against the deep brown bark of
the trees.

Exits.Description: The circle continues in a friendly fashion.
The circle continues strongly.

rooms.Name: Circle of Strength
rooms.Description:
This part of the circle is planted with herbs of strength and
wisdom.  Carnations of all colors are blooming next to pennyroyal and 
saffron.  Sage and iris grow side by side with bodhi.  You may continue 
around the circle west or north or east.

Exits.Description: An enormous tree beckons to you gracefully.
The circle continues in good health.
The circle continues with honor.

rooms.Name: Circle of Health
rooms.Description:
The stones placed here, like the herbs that grow amongst them, are
the source of the dryads' glowing good health.  Here grows the sweet,
strong magic of caraway, juniper, marjoram, nutmeg, rue, sassafras and
tansy.  You are tempted to take some and crush it between your fingers.
Agate, jade and coral stones make small borders around them.

Exits.Description: You see a moving cloud of color.
The circle continues strongly.

rooms.Name: A cold, clear lake
rooms.Description:
This cold clear lake is fed by the creek whose bank you followed.
From the temperature of the water you can guess that the source lies up 
in the mountains.  Your teeth chatter, although you are not sure whether
that is because your toes are turning blue or because of the very LARGE
fish you see swimming around.
The lake continues in all directions but up.

Exits.Description: The lake continues.
The lake continues.
The lake continues.
The lake continues.
The lake bottom is dark.

rooms.Name: The Forest Lake or Who's the Prey Now?
rooms.Description:
The clear water is shallower here, not enough that you could rest
your feet on the bottom and still keep your nose above water, though.   The
pond is much larger than it originally looked, and you hope you can
find your way back to shore before you drown.

Exits.Description: The lake continues.
The lake continues.
The lake looks bottomless.

rooms.Name: Drowning in the Lake!
rooms.Description:
The cold clear waters of the pool would be refreshing if they didn't
make your teeth chatter.  And perhaps you'd rather just not know about
those funny looking fish with the fangs.  A lazy frog floats by on a
lilypad.  At least ... you THINK it's a frog.

Exits.Description: Yet more lake!
This is a really vast lake.
What a lake!
Will it ever end?
Murky depths of the lake ...

rooms.Name: Off the bank
rooms.Description:
The bottom suddenly drops out from under your toes and you are
treading water and swimming with the fish.  Some of them look rather 
nasty, with long sharp teeth and a lean hungry look in their eyes.  
Others look remarkably like the waybread your Auntie used to bake up 
for you, and you remember how long it's been since you last ate.

Exits.Description: The lake continues endlessly northwards.
The lake continues in the direction of the rising sun.
The lake continues as far as you can see.
The waterfall keeps needlessly pouring more water into the lake.
The lake looks deep.

rooms.Name: Deep and Cold
rooms.Description:
The water is cold and deep, and your body is working hard to stay
warm and to breathe.  All around you fish of differing sizes and colors 
swim lazily about, looking for food.  You hope you don't look tasty to 
them. Far to the west you hear a waterfall.

Exits.Description: The lake continues endlessly.
The lake continues endlessly.
The lake continues endlessly.
The lake continues endlessly.
The lake looks bottomless.

rooms.Name: On the Lake
rooms.Description:
Ripples of cold water splash at your face.  You begin to wonder if
you've somehow tumbled into the deep blue sea, but the water is fresh,
not salty.  You watch a frog float by on a lilypad, and wish you had a
boat.

Exits.Description: The lake continues endlessly.
The lake continues endlessly.
The lake continues endlessly.
The lake continues endlessly.
The lake appears to be bottomless.

rooms.Name: Treading water
rooms.Description:
As your legs keep cycling beneath you, tiredly you wonder why this
lake seems to keep growing around you, and you remember all the magic in
this forest.  You look hard to the north, south, east and west, looking
for someplace to crawl out and rest your cold, weary body.

Exits.Description: The lake continues endlessly.
The lake continues endlessly.
The lake continues endlessly.
The lake continues endlessly.
The lake looks bottomless.

rooms.Name: Dreading water
rooms.Description:
The lake waters are calm, the water faintly rippling in an easterly
direction.  If it wasn't so cold and so vast you would probably enjoy
your swim more, but you are tiring, and you begin to think a watery
grave might be peaceful.  Then a fish takes a small *bite* out of you
and you decide it's time to move on!

Exits.Description: The lake continues endlessly.
The lake continues endlessly.
The lake continues endlessly.
The lake continues endlessly.
The lake appears to be bottomless.

rooms.Name: Swimming with the fish
rooms.Description:
The lake appears well stocked with fish, both of known and unknown
varieties.   It is much larger than it first appeared, the waters calm
despite a slight breeze.  You can swim in just about any direction but
up from here.

Exits.Description: The lake continues endlessly.
The lake continues endlessly.
The lake continues endlessly.
The lake continues endlessly.
The lake appears bottomless.

rooms.Name: Deep in the Lake
rooms.Description:
You are deep beneath the surface of the cold lake waters. You have
lost all sense of direction in the watery world, and your body is 
beginning to feel numb.    Fish of all sizes and varieties swim around 
you.  None of them is smiling, except for the big one in the distance 
who is looking at you with a hungry, toothy grin.

Exits.Description: More water, more fish.
More water, more fish.
More water, more fish.
More water, more fish.
More water, more fish.

rooms.Description:
