rooms.Description:
You are in a dark room, where most of your biggest light source is
the metal light from several weapons and armor's that are layed around
in the room. There isnt much to see, just pick and take it.

Exits.Description: There is starway leading up.

rooms.Name: #C[ #yT#whe Esoteric Shop #C]#N
rooms.Description:
You stand in dark room, the only source of light is a couple of
blowtorch's in the walls. You can see a vast exposition of weird items,
most of them come from the uncharted lands of Elite. A old woman with the
looks of a wizard stands near to a cabinet cleaning some dusty old 
items, though she is not looking at you, you sense one thousand eyes
penetrating your soul and you feel very unconfortable as you notice
that you are being watched and measured.

Exits.Description: You see an orange road leading to the village.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It's made of black marble, within this cabinet you can see a huge
collection of potions of all kinds and colors... Maybe this is what
took you to this place.

rooms.Name: #C[ #yT#whe hall of the past glories #C]#N
rooms.Description:
You are in a huge hall full of statues, the glories of the past.
The entire hall is made of dark marble covering the walls, the light
is provided by torch's in grey marble altars scatered through the
hall. Ahead of you lies for all eternity the statues of those who
served Izumo in the best way they could. Bow before the #yL#wegends #Nof
the past, for their spirits protect this sacred place.

Exits.Description: The hall continues west.
This path leads you to Izumo village.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
They are made of grey marble, on top of them is a golden container
in the form of a helmet upside down with the 'oil of life' burning,
giving the room a mystic atmosphere and purifying the air.

rooms.Name: #C[ #yT#womb of #yA#wtiel, The Dragon #C]#N
rooms.Description:
In this sacred place lies #rAtiel #Nthe #GDragon #NKnight. In
distant times, Atiel's fate crossed with 2 mighty warriors, Shandrala
and Mystasia, they both regreted their fate when they were defeated
at Atiel's feet. The room is covered with a green mist, the mist that
remains when a Dragon's corpse is down, some say that the Mighty Dragon
Lord's spirit keeps an eye on his followers and that by his power, a
corpse can regain life and answer to the call of his Master.
You see a huge #yT#womb #Nmade of white marble, on the sides there are
carvings with the story of #rAtiel#N's life written in ancient runes.
On the top of the Tomb there is a statue of Atiel wielding is weapons,
with a raged expression it appears that he wants to charge over you.

Exits.Description: This path leads you to the entrance hall of the shrine.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
This runes state:

"Those who can not remember the past, are condemned to repeat it."

"Here lies Atiel, the Dragon, slayer of evil in ancient times, when
the elders were young, this mighty Dragon wielded the sword of Justice,
a Sword forged in fire and ice, a Sword to battle and take life, a
Sword to bring Peace and Justice in troubled times."

"Here lies the Slayer of Shandrala and Mystasia, bow before this great
warrior who awaits for the call of his Master."

rooms.Name: #C[ #yA#wbhorsen's Green House #C]#N
rooms.Description:
Here is Abhorsen's refuge in days of peace. The mighty Avatar rests
here when there's no more fights to be fought. He choose to live in his
greenhouse where he has his plantation of Cannabis and Marijuana, and,
of course he Bong colletion. Abhorsen has a strong nervous problem and
seeks refuge and peace on his medical treatment with the "wild plants".
Some say, he is the leader of a strange cult known as the #bRasta#N
#bWarriors#N. You see some plants growing in vases all over the place.
The house stays outside of Izumo because he likes peace and doesnt like
to be disturbed when enjoying his trips.

Exits.Description: To the east you can see the road wich leads to Izumo.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
What a huge plantation, no man can smoke all of this, though Abhorsen
surely tries to... This might be just enough for the entire cult wich he
leads, known as #bRasta Warriors#N.
They do smell nice.

rooms.Name: Cursed Den of Frogeaters
rooms.Description:
Down in the wet cellar of the Ni-Knights clan house (well, House can
be discussed, but still) the frogeaters hang out chatting about their
glorious deeds. To their help they have one of the Clans Minstrels,
Kami, whos voice can stand up to the glorious mushysinger Hulio, anyday.

Exits.Description: The constant turmoil of the Ni Throne room.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Even if Kami is not here you can still here some of his chantings
eminating from the damp walls of the Den.

Placing your ear to the wet wall the chanting comes clearer to you.
   ...   ni   ...    ni   ...   ni   ...   ni   ...
You stand there for a long time completely hexed and looking awfully
silly with your ears sticked to the fungicovered wall.
So impregnated with the chanting of NI (ni ni) the walls are that they
seem to reverberate it for all eternity

                                        ni   ...   ni   ...   ni

Hulio has a standing act at Ma Globs Dancing Parlor in Stanneg. Go
there if you want to have a peek at him.

rooms.Name: Hall of Ni
rooms.Description:
This is the clan house of the #RKnights #Ywho say #GNi#N. There is
almost no light at all, but you can still distinguish some statues of the
clan founders. At the end on the wall you can see a picture showing the
holy grail and a cross marking a spot. Some intricate carvings can also
be found next to the picture. They read: "Here may be found the last
words of Joseph of Arimathea. He who is valiant and pure of spirit, may
find the #YHoly Grail#N in the Castle of Aaahh..."

Exits.Description: The clan regeneration, or is it degeneration?, room open up before you.
Back to the cold unfriendly Outside...
The soup kitchen smell invitingly.
The Herring passage takes you further inside the clan house.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Reading the stones on the statues you see engraved the names of: Kidd,
Sadsam, Eladamri, Trilion, Tungtor, Wildthing, Achilles, Gloin, Bofur,
Kami, GOAG, Legasi, Champion, Bedevere, Juvenile, Midas, Maynard,
Cerbaro, Ephex, Vombat, Zolgorath, Fatbob, Planeswalker.
A real mighty bunch of people set out to bring NI to everyone.
Over and over again.    Ni      Ni      Ni      Ni      Ni      Ni.

rooms.Name: Clan Regeneration Room
rooms.Description:
You enter a round room in which you can see portraits of the fellow
clan members. From some sort of device in the roof dim lights stream
down unto you. Along the walls several beds are lined up together with a
small table. In the middle of the room a small pond filled with cold
water and nets filled with delicate beer. Beverage for true heroes!
 An unseen servant tucks you into bed as fast as you lay down on the
beds and you really feel at home.

Exits.Description: The Hall of Ni.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Some all mighty Ni-Knight have bonded a big block of shining true magic
in the centre of the roof, so that it can radiate down on the clan
members when they relax after a hard day of old crone taunting. A fact
that cause some to believe it is not magic after all, but just a piece
very high consentrated essence of 'wicked'.

Brought to you courtesy of #BGlob Inc.#N

(Binding magic that way could not been accomplished by someone else.)

Some of the main contributors to the creation of the clan and the
clanhouse has their pics here. The current pictures show the faces off
Kidd, Egba Glob, DJMC, SadSam, Eladamri and Beleg.

rooms.Name: The Soup Kitchen
rooms.Description:
You enter what appears to be an anbandon warehouse, you realise, you
found the Ni's Soup Kitchen. You see stockpiles of slighty used
equipment ranging in levels, styles and types. There are several
clannies roaming through the stuff, looking for that particular jem to
their collection, that missing piece, that would make there kit
complete. So have a look about, see what you can use. All is at your
disposal. We just ask that you don't put stuff in there that one would
consider junk, you know what I mean that stuff that is just usless to
all that would desire. These rules are also stated on a big sign on the
rear wall.

Exits.Description: The Hall of Ni.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The sign of Rules reads as follows :
Do not place junk here.
Do not donate stuff from ON your field trips, bring it here and drop it.
If you find something worth equiping yourself with, drop the thingie you
 were wearing(unless its complete junk:) so that the younger clannies
 can get it.
Do say Ni to everyone you see, every time. Ni.
Never sell anything from the Soup Kitchen.
 (unless its junk and they are really stooopid)
If you have or find stuff that are too junky for this place that you
 still want to make available to the rest of the clan for a while drop
 them in the Old Crone Quarters.

rooms.Name: Herring Passage
rooms.Description:
Again the strange crowned knight and a multitude of people
gathering. There is a strange conversation going on:

King Arthur: Oh, Knights of Ni, we have brought you your shrubbery. May
  we go now?
Knights of "Ni" Leader: It is a good shrubbery. I like the laurels
  particularly. But there is one small problem.
King Arthur: What is that?
Knights of "Ni" Leader: We are now...no longer the Knights Who Say Ni.
Random Knight of "Ni" (thats us bringing chaos): Ni!
Knights of "Ni" Leader: Shh shh. We are now the Knights Who Say Ecky-
  ecky-ecky-ecky-pikang-zoom-boing-mumble-mumble.
Random Knight of "Ni"(ooops, we again:) : Ni!
Knights of "Ni" Leader: Therefore, we must give you a test.
King Arthur: What is this test, Oh, Knights of...Knights who 'til
  recently said "Ni"?
Knights of "Ni" Leader: Firstly, you must find...another shrubbery!
King Arthur: Not another shrubbery!
Knights of "Ni" Leader: Then, when you have found the shrubbery, you
  must place it here beside this shrubbery, only slightly higher so you
  get a two-level effect with a little path running down the middle.
Knights of "Ni": A path! A path! Ni!
Knights of "Ni" Leader: Then, when you have found the shrubbery, you
  must cut down the mightiest tree in the forest with...a herring!

Exits.Description: The Hall of Ni.
The Ni Throne Room.

rooms.Name: The Ni Throne Room.
rooms.Description:
In a little clearing within the group of trees a mighty throne is set
up for the Head of the #RKnights #Ywho say #GNi#N Clan. In this very room
a daily court is held where kinds of subjects are taken up for
discussion. The topic range from 'How to spread the knowledge of the
correct intonation of NI amongst the unbelievers' to 'Spanking 101' via
'Optimum distance between two shrubberies to fit a path suitable for two
Knights dragging a Old Crone behind them tied up in a rope made of
raspberry twigs' and 'The current pricing of herrings'. The Clan leader
do have a real cumbersome duty, eased up only by the frequent uttering
of the sacred words 'Ni Ni Ni'.

Exits.Description: The Old Crone Quarters.
The Herring Passage.
The Shrubbery Tunnel.
The Forest of Mighty Trees (Bring your own herring!)
The den below smells of frog leftovers. Bleh !

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The throne is huge, a necessity if one want to dangle ones leg over the
edge of the throne seat. It is wooden and all black. Some small carvings
can be seen in the wood, apart from that there is no other decorations
present. Well a gigantic reindeer horn set is placed on top of the
throne spreading its pointy horns in all directions.

The multidirectional spreading of the horn edges show a clear influence
in the current ruling and decitionmaking in the clan.

rooms.Name: Old Crone Mud Quarters
rooms.Description:
Covered in mud you continue along the path watching an Old Crone
talking with a guy with a Crown on his head you listen in:

King Arthur: Old crone! Is there anywhere in this town where we could
  buy a shrubbery?
Crone: Who sent you?
King Arthur: The #RKnights #Ywho say #GNi#N.
Crone: Agh! No! Never! We have no shrubberies here.
King Arthur: If you do not tell us where we can buy a
  shrubbery, my friend and I will say...we will say...Ni!
Crone: Agh! Do your worst!
King Arthur: Very well! If you will not assist us voluntarily... Ni!

Haaaa... by the terrible sound of the very word Ni the Old Crone is
terrified and runs away in a flash!!!

Exits.Description: Vombats Collector Studio.
A room for a prominent Kniggit is about to be excavated from this wall.
The Ni Throne Room.
A room for the champion, Champion.

rooms.Name: Shrubbery Tunnel
rooms.Description:
You find yourself in a very long Tunnel. A splendid tunnel filled
with... Shrubbery!
Shrubberies of all sizes and colours and on the floor deep green moss in
which you quickly throw yourself into. Mmmm, nice...
And from within the walls faint soothing voices chant:
"ni..ni..ni..ni...".
Soothing, relaxing...and you feel you could lay here forever...as long
as you keep track on the white killer rabbit that is...After all, you
are not very far from the very cave of Caer Bannog!

Exits.Description: The Ni Throne Room.
A room for a prominent Kniggit is about to be excavated from this wall.
A room for a prominent Kniggit is about to be excavated from this wall.
A room for a prominent Kniggit is about to be excavated from this wall.

rooms.Name: Mighty Trees Forest
rooms.Description:
As you walk along the path, you start to enter a great and very old
forest, with trees so high and mighty you could get scared just by
looking at it. Suddenly you notice a huge stone with some carvings in
it. Carvings well worth reading.

Exits.Description: The Ni Throne Room.
The Shrubbery Shrine.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The carvings read the following :

King Arthur: Who are you?
Knights of "Ni" Leader: We are the knights who say..."Ni". Ni!
Ni! Ni!
King Arthur: No! Not the knights who say "Ni"!
Knights of "Ni" Leader: The same.
Sir Bedevere: Who are these?
Knights of "Ni" Leader: We are the keepers of the sacred words
Ni Peng and Ni Wom!
(Echo): Ny Wom...
King Arthur: Those who here them seldom live to tell the tale.
Knights of "Ni" Leader: The knights who say "Ni" demand a
sacrifice!
King Arthur: Knights of "Ni", we are but simple travellers, who
seek the enchanter who lives beyond these woods.
Knights of "Ni" Leader: Ni! Ni!
Knights of "Ni": Ni! Ni! Ni!
King Arthur, Sir Bedevere and their company: Ah! No! Aie! No!
Knights of "Ni" Leader: We shall say "´Ni" again to you, if you
do not appease us.
King Arthur: Well, what is it you want?
Knights of "Ni" Leader: We want...a shrubbery!
King Arthur: A what?
Knights of "Ni": Ni! Ni! Ni! Ni!
King Arthur: Aah! No! No, please, please! No more! We will find
you a shrubbery.
Knights of "Ni" Leader: You must return here with a shrubbery,
or else you will never pass through these woods...alive.
King Arthur: Oh, Knights of Ni, you are just and fair. And we
will return here with a shrubbery.
Knights of "Ni" Leader: One that looks nice!
King Arthur: Of course.
Knights of "Ni" Leader: And not too expensive.
King Arthur: Yes!
Knights of "Ni" Leader: Now...go!

rooms.Name: The Shrubbery Shrine
rooms.Description:
The shrine of Shrubberies is fully devoted to the art of arranging
shrubberies in perfect order so that the maximum effect can be reached
with a minimum of shrubberies. We all know that Shrubberies is very
sought of all over the land as the availability is somewhat limited.
Everyday new constellations can be found here as the Knights are very
keen on rearranging them to fit the task of the day.

Exits.Description: The Secret Order of Holy Shrubbery most secret hideout.
A Foretst of Mighty Trees.
Kidds Secret Hideout - Do not tell anyone...

rooms.Name: Secret Order of Holy Shrubbery
rooms.Description:
The bright and fantastic look of the walls of the room of the holy
order makes you a bit dizzy, now you are feeling even more silly than
the usual. Around you gather the other members of this sacred and
hermetic order, they also look pale,maybe they are on dope, who knows.
You never felt so strange, yet is sooooo good to be in the mud most
secret place!!! A old man comes forth, he tells you to move forward, he
speaks:

Stop! Who approaches the Bridge of Death must answer me these questions
three, 'ere the other side he see.

Exits.Description: The Shrubbery Shrine.
On the other side of the Bridge of Death is The Grail !!!

You Really answer the questions correctly ???
   Lucky you to still be alive - and inside the Ni Clan House !

Knights might gather
when they want to draft some new plans in privacy. Their long and very
dangerous path finally led them to their ultimate goal.
                      #RThe #YHoly #GGrail#N.
No mortal may ever enter this room as it most certainly would cause
certain death to those still unworthy.

rooms.Name: KIDDs Secret Hideout
rooms.Description:
This room is more like a cave or hummm, a cavern maybe. It sure it a
good place to mud when you are alone. Kidd spent long memorable nights
here and you can see loads of memorabilia scattered around, like some
pictures from dear friends like Hath, Angulion, Egba, Therold, Icestorm
and Demona.
Some Monty Python movies lies dumped in the corner and a bed made
directly on the floor, shows a bit KIDD tastes on sleeping.

Exits.Description: The shrubbery Shrine

rooms.Name: #R CHAMPION#N OF THE #RKNIGHTS #YWHO SAY #GNI#N
rooms.Description:
The room appears quite spartan. The only items adorning the walls is
a broadsword and a shield. There is also a table, chair, bed and closet.
Sparse accomodations for one such as Champion. Perhaps he likes it that
way.

Exits.Description: The Old Crone Qaurters.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
This broadsword is huge! Obviously too large for any normal man. The
hilt is wrapped in sharkskin for the perfect grip. A single sapphire the
size of an egg adorns the pommel. The silvery blades is etched with what
appears to be magical symbols. When you look closer the blade appears to
emit an ethereal flow. Better to not touch this weapon!
You see a normal ordinary bed. Looks to be quite uncomfortable really.

Your cursory examination show some letters which seem to be for someone
named Demona.

Reading the letters you find thaty Champion seems to worship a lady
whose name is Demona. It seem, however, that clan affiliations have
doomed any real relationship.

Opening the closet you find a complete set of plate armor. Shining
gold, it is emblazoned with the insignia of the Knight of Ni.

The shield seems to glow with a fire of it's own.The emblem of the
Knight of Ni is burnished into it's surface. Looks dangerous! Better
leave it alone.
Just a chair. What?! Did you expect more?

rooms.Name: #R Vombat#N Collectors Studio
rooms.Description:
There are several shelves full of old and new books and albums. A big
desk in the middle of the room with a magnifying glass and some nippers
on it. It also seems to be full of very small pieces of paper. Stamps!!
Please, take caution upon your breathing!
This is a very quiet and very relaxing place, where Vombat usually spend
his time collecting stamps, searching for perfection on his beautiful
thematic Ships Collection. This walls still echoing the word he said
when he finally found a new rare specimen.

Exits.Description: The Old Crone Quarters.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
You see a stamp with an image of a fabulous sailing ship! If you want
to see more of this, please ask Vombat and he shows you his secret
exhibition, somewhere in the web space.

You see some albums full of complete stamp sets, arranged by sub-themes
like Sailing ships, Sport ships, Fishing Ships, War Ships ! If you
really want to see more, please ask Vombat and he shows you the place
where he have his secret exhibition, somewhere in the web space.

rooms.Name: Beginning of the Marsh
rooms.Description:
The humming of insects fills the air, which is heavy with moisture 
and difficult to breathe. The ground is soft underfoot, with water 
seeping upwards and mud sucking at booted feet. To the north, the ground 
seems higher, and there are even some tufts of grass visible. To the east
and south the marsh becomes more misty and there are pools of water 
visible close by. Strangely, a rickety wooden ladder is suspended here, 
but it is too misty to see what lies at the top of it.

Exits.Description: There are grassy tufts to the north.
The marsh continues to the east.
The marsh continues to the south.
To the west, a path disappears into the forest.
A rickety wooden ladder leads up.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The ladder is made from long knobbly lengths of bamboo, lashed together
with lengths of a rope-like grass. The ladder disappears up into the mist
above, and whatever lies at the top remains out of sight.

rooms.Name: Marshy Ground
rooms.Description:
The marshy ground is totally waterlogged here and appears to get 
worse to the east. To the north thick tufts of grass are visible, waving
gently in the slight breeze. Further east the marsh becomes more foggy
and damp. A tall and extremely thick oak with very pale bark stands to 
the south.

Exits.Description: The ground looks firmer to the north.
The marsh to the east is clouded in thick fog.
The edge of the marsh is just visible to the west.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The oak is ancient - much older than any of the other trees nearby. The
bark is ghostly pale and almost luminous in the faint light.

rooms.Name: In the Fog
rooms.Description:
It is eerie and quiet in this part of the marshland. Thick mist
muffles all sounds, yet at the same times makes far-off noises seem 
close by. At least - you hope the chewing and crunching sounds are 
coming from far off! The ground is saturated with water and small 
pools gather in amongst the tufts of moss and expanses of muddy green 
slime. To the north and west the marsh seems less ominous, while to the 
south it becomes darker and altogether more treacherous. The smell of a 
stagnant pool comes from the east.

Exits.Description: You can see nothing through the thick fog.
You can see nothing through the thick fog.
You can see nothing through the thick fog.
You can see nothing through the thick fog.

rooms.Name: Dark Bog
rooms.Description:
Deep in the dark bog it is difficult to both see and move. The 
dark murky mist clings to the ground and swirls around your ankles. 
The slimy marsh tries to grab your feet as you attempt to move. 
Although it is easy to get confused in these conditions, it appears to
be less murky to the north. The dark bog continues to the east, 
west and south.

Exits.Description: A thick fog obscures the view to the north.
The dark bog continues to the east.
The dark bog continues to the south.
The dark bog continues to the west.

rooms.Name: Dark Bog
rooms.Description:
Puddles of clinging slimy mud are found amongst the pools of unclean 
water and tufts of saturated moss. Tiny insects, almost too small to 
see, swarm around you and the dark mist gathers around you ominously. The
bog continues in all directions.

Exits.Description: The dark bog continues to the north.
The dark bog continues to the east.
The dark bog continues to the south.
The dark bog continues to the west.

rooms.Name: Lair of the Bog-Goblin King
rooms.Description:
The lair is brightly lit by a number of sputtering yellowy torches 
placed around this grove hidden deep within the dark bog. The smell is 
pretty unpleasant - rotting flesh and stagnant water mostly and the 
filthy nests of lesser ranked bog-goblins. The bog-goblin King 
has a wide wooden platform all to himself, keeping him off the boggy 
ground.

Exits.Description: The dark bog continues to the north.
The dark bog continues to the east.
The dark bog continues to the south.
The dark bog continues to the west.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Bog-goblins are semi-amphibious and so are quite comfortable sleeping
in shallow boggy pools. The nests are really just patches of flattened
reeds with a mucky puddle of brackish water in the center.

rooms.Name: Dark Bog
rooms.Description:
The clammy air makes it difficult to breathe in this part of the bog.
The dark murky fog is thick all around, and it is impossible to see very
far in any direction. The mossy ground is saturated with brownish 
water, ready to trap the foot of any unwary adventurer. From somewhere 
out in the murky bog comes the sound of harsh cackling laughter. Better
watch your step!

Exits.Description: The dark bog continues to the north.
The dark bog continues to the east.
The dark bog continues to the south.
The dark bog continues to the west.

rooms.Name: Dark Bog
rooms.Description:
The dark bog is sparsely populated with tall stands of greyish reeds. 
The reeds rub against each other in the breeze, making an ominous 
creaking scratching noise which echoes around. Squelching sounds close
by indicate that there is something living out there - but what could
it be?

Exits.Description: The dark bog continues to the north.
The dark bog continues to the east.
The dark bog continues to the south.
The dark bog continues to the west.

rooms.Name: Dark Bog
rooms.Description:
Squelching noises echo all around this part of the dark bog. Long 
reeds whisper sibilantly in the slightest air currents, and every so 
often a subdued splashing can be heard. The bog continues to the east, 
south and west, but to the north, the way is blocked by an enormous
oak tree, which disappears into the murky fog above.

Exits.Description: The dark bog continues to the east.
The dark bog continues to the south.
The dark bog continues to the west.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The oak is ancient - much older than any of the other trees nearby. The
bark is blackened as if burned, but the tree appears otherwise healthy.

rooms.Name: Dark Bog
rooms.Description:
The feeling of being watched cannot be escaped in this dark and
sinister bog. The slightest movement in the air makes the reeds and
rushes rub together, making sounds like slow breathing. There is an
occasional splash close by, although the damping effect of the lingering
fog makes it impossible to determine which direction the noises come 
from. The dark bog continues in all directions.

Exits.Description: The dark bog continues to the north.
The dark bog continues to the east.
The dark bog continues to the south.
The dark bog continues to the west.

rooms.Name: Dark Bog
rooms.Description:
An unpleasant smell emanates from the scattered puddles of brackish
water and rotting vegetation. A murky black mist clings to the ground, 
swirling around your feet as you move. Eerie noises echo strangely in
the darkness around you. The bog looks the same to the north, east and
west, but to the south a squelchy trail can be seen.

Exits.Description: The dark bog continues to the north.
The dark bog continues to the east.
A squelchy trail leads south through the bog.
The dark bog continues to the west.

rooms.Name: Dark Bog
rooms.Description:
Tall reeds loom out of the eerie darkness of the bog. The ground is
soft and slimy, stagnant water has collected into small puddles all
around. The bog continues in all directions.

Exits.Description: The dark bog continues to the north.
The dark bog continues to the east.
The dark bog continues to the south.
The dark bog continues to the west.

rooms.Name: Beneath the Platforms
rooms.Description:
The rushes and mosses in this area of the bog are trampled flat, and
the ground seems less waterlogged. A dark clinging mist lurks over the 
ground and crawls about your feet. A strange rickety wooden ladder leads 
upwards into to the mist.

Exits.Description: The dark bog continues to the north.
The dark bog continues to the west.
A rickety wooden ladder leads up to the platforms.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The ladder is made from long knobbly lengths of bamboo, lashed together
with lengths of a rope-like grass. The ladder disappears up into the mist
above, and whatever lies at the top remains out of sight.

rooms.Name: Squelchy Trail
rooms.Description:
This waterlogged trail winds its way north-south through the dark
murk of the bog. To the east and west, the damp shuffling noises are
louder, as if something lurks out there in the mist. From the south
comes a foul stench, and to the north the air is fresher, but still
oppressive.

Exits.Description: The dark bog continues to the north.
The dark bog lies to the east, away from the trail.
The trail continues south, where it becomes progressively smellier.
The dark bog lies to the west, away from the trail.

rooms.Name: Stinking Bog
rooms.Description:
The fetid puddles of stagnant water in this part of the bog reek of
rotting vegetation and perhaps worse. A trail leads northwards through
the murk, or you could abandon the trail and head west or south into
the depths of the dark bog. To the east is a small cave, from which the
foulest smell emanates.

Exits.Description: A squelchy trail leads north, through the dark bog.
A foul stench emanates from a dark cave to the east.
The dark bog lies south, away from the trail.
The dark bog lies west, away from the trail.

rooms.Name: The Caves of Stench
rooms.Description:
Eeew! The air is thick with the rancid stench of open graves and 
rotting food. The cave walls are daubed with goblin blood and several
goblin corpses lie dismembered on the cave-floor. The corpses have 
been rent and torn by some vicious clawed creature. The relative 
safety of the bog lies to the west.

Exits.Description: The relative safety of the dark bog beckons from the west.

rooms.Name: Grassy Tufts
rooms.Description:
Large tufts of stiff yellowy-green grass wave gently in the breeze. 
In between the tufts is water-soaked moss, waiting to snare careless 
feet. By carefully moving from tuft to tuft, it is possible to continue
further to the north, or south.

Exits.Description: There are more grassy tufts to the north.
The marsh lies to the south.

rooms.Name: Stagnant Pool
rooms.Description:
A few mossy rocks surround this horrible little pool in the marsh. 
The water is clogged with slimy green weeds, and frog spawn. The marsh 
is far too soggy to be traversed in any direction except north, where 
a rivulet of the foul stagnant waters cuts through firmer ground.

Exits.Description: To the north lies an expanse of squelchy moss.

rooms.Name: The Pixie Throne
rooms.Description:
A pixie-throne, made entirely of buttercups and spidersilk, almost 
floats above the dew-laden grass. Phosphorescent lights glow throughout 
the grove, lighting up the green grass, and sleek-limbed willow trees.
To the east, there appears to be some sort of celebration among the
pixie folk!

Exits.Description: There is pixie dancing to the east.

rooms.Name: The Pixie Feast
rooms.Description:
Rows of tables, decorated with bluebells, snowdrops, and ribbons of 
all colours, are covered with exuberant pixie foods - sweets and peculiar
fruits for the most part. Tiny prancing figures skip between the tables
helping themselves to the delicious treats before springing off to the
east to dance, or to the west to visit the pixie-queen.

Exits.Description: The magic pixie circle lies to the east.
The magical pixie throne glows to the west.

rooms.Name: Pixie Circle
rooms.Description:
Within a circle of giant redcap toadstools the grass is flattened by
by the light but numerous feet of the dancing pixies. Pixies like 
nothing more than joyous dancing and will happily prance around their
pixie groves at any time of night. To the west lies the glow of the
pixie throne and the merry noises of the pixie feast! To the east, a 
narrow path leads through the darkness.

Exits.Description: A dark path leads away from the pixie circle.
The festive sound of pixie dancing comes from the west.

rooms.Name: Among the Truffla Stumps
rooms.Description:
The reason for the boggy ground soon becomes clear. All the trees in
this region (and as far as the eye can see) have been chopped down, 
leaving only the stumps behind. Without the trees drinking up the water,
the ground has quickly become waterlogged and boggy. To the east, there
are only tufts of grass, but at least it is possible to travel there. 
In the other directions, the ground is too waterlogged, and the stumps
too few and far between.

Exits.Description: There are no trufflas to the east, only tufts of grass.

rooms.Name: Tufts of Grass
rooms.Description:
This area is populated by thick tufts of grass, which rise up out of
the soggy ground. By hopping from tuft to tuft it is possible to cross
this part of the marsh without getting wet. To the east, the ground 
becomes more boggy, while to the south there are more of the grassy 
outcrops. To the west, a forest of tree stumps is just visible.

Exits.Description: To the west, the ground becomes more boggy.
There are more grassy tufts to the south.
To the west, is a glen of tree stumps.

rooms.Name: Squelching Moss
rooms.Description:
Thick wet moss covers the ground, both here and further to the north
and south. The ground almost looks solid, but a closer look reveals the
brackish water beneath the fronds of moss, waiting to snare careless 
feet.

Exits.Description: A mossy path leads north.
The ground becomes more waterlogged to the south.
The ground to the west is covered in thick tufts of grass.

rooms.Name: Pixie Circle
rooms.Description:
The light barely penetrates the canopy of the dense will trees into
this glade. The area is surrounded by a circle of giant red mushrooms - 
so this must be a magical pixie circle! Shame, it must be their day off
because there are no pixies to be found.

Exits.Description: A dark path leads away from the pixie circle.

rooms.Name: Dark Path
rooms.Description:
A dark path weaves between the trees and rocky outcrops. There is a 
dark fogginess to this place, and it appears as if light never truly
reaches the forest floor. The dark path continues both east and west.

Exits.Description: A dark path leads east.
A dark path leads west, opening out into a little glade.

rooms.Name: Dark Path
rooms.Description:
The dark path turns sharply here, avoiding a steep outcrop of rock
to the south and east. To the south, the rocks are covered by a 
sprawling holly bush, with spiky leaves and flame red berries. Gnarled 
willow limbs reach down out of the darkness, trying to trip and trap 
you. The dark path continues to the north and west.

Exits.Description: The dark path leads north.
The way south is blocked by a thick bush.
The dark path leads west.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Behind the sharp leaves and twisted branches, you can make out some
kind of cave!

rooms.Name: Damp Cave
rooms.Description:
Water drips from the ceiling and down the walls of this dark dank
cave. The air smells musty and mouldy and the floor is strewn with
old bones and bits of furry skin. The only way out is to the north.

Exits.Description: Outside the cave is a dark path.

rooms.Name: Boggy Path
rooms.Description:
Squelchy puddles of water ooze up between tufts of soggy moss beneath
unwary feet. To stop moving is to risk becoming trapped by the shlurping
marsh. It is possible to head in any direction, although there seems to
be some kind of route through the bog to the north and west. From the
south comes the dank smell of stagnant water.

Exits.Description: You think you can see a safe route through the bog to the north.
The boggy ground extends further to the east.
The boggy ground extends further to the south.
The boggy ground extends further to the west.

rooms.Name: Marshy Trail
rooms.Description:
An oak tree climbs majestically out of the bog to the west, its 
deep roots giving it some stability in the soft, waterlogged ground. 
The marshy trail continues to the east and south.

Exits.Description: A faint trail leads north through the marsh.
A faint trail leads east through the marsh.
A faint trail leads south through the marsh.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The oak is ancient - much older than any of the other trees nearby. Despite
its age and girth, the tree sways gently in the breeze as its might roots
claw at the boggy ground.

rooms.Name: Marshy Trail
rooms.Description:
A watery trail runs east-west through this part of the marsh, 
although it is possible to go in any direction. The humidity is 
oppressive, but it seems to grow less further to the east. Far to 
the west is a tall oak tree.

Exits.Description: A faint trail leads north through the marsh.
A faint trail leads east through the marsh.
A faint trail leads south through the marsh.
A faint trail leads west through the marsh.

rooms.Name: Marshy Trail
rooms.Description:
The ground here is a little firmer, although puddles of water still
peek up between tufts of thick marsh-grass and moss. There is a muddy
grove and another large oak tree, surrounded by reeds, to the south.
The marsh continues to the north, east and west.

Exits.Description: A faint trail leads north through the marsh.
To the east is a wide boggy area.
A muddy trail leads south, towards a large oak tree.
A faint trail leads west through the marsh.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: There is an oak standing in the grove to the south.

rooms.Name: Beneath the Oak
rooms.Description:
The muddy ground beneath the oak has been well trampled recently. 
It looks like the rocks around this place have been turned over and the
bark of the nearby oak tree has been scraped clean of the parasitic
vines which infest this area.

Exits.Description: A narrow trail leads north into the marsh.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The footprints are about the same size as those of a halfling, but 
three-toed and webbed.

The oak is ancient - much older than any of the other trees nearby. The
bark is pitted (possibly by some bird or other animal) and rivulets of 
sap run down the trunk like tears.

rooms.Name: Boggy Ground
rooms.Description:
Soggy fronds of moss squelch unsteadily under foot. Between patches 
of soft moss are areas of mud. The ground appears slightly firmer 
further to the east and continues much the same northwards. A thick 
mist clings to the ground making it difficult to see much further.

Exits.Description: There is more boggy ground to the north.
The ground looks firmer to the east.
There a misty glade to the south.
A trail leads west through the marsh.

rooms.Name: Firmer Ground
rooms.Description:
The ground around this area is damp, but not too muddy. The ground
has been heavily trampled, and there are many webbed footprints 
surrounding a rickety wooden ladder, which disappears up in the wispy
mist that lingers around this area. The marsh continues in all 
directions.

Exits.Description: The ground to the north looks very muddy.
The ground to the east looks very muddy.
There is a misty glade to the south.
The ground to the west looks very boggy.
A rickety ladder ascends through the mist.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The ladder is made from long knobbly lengths of bamboo, lashed together
with lengths of a rope-like grass. The ladder disappears up into the mist
above, and whatever lies at the top remains out of sight.

rooms.Name: Misty Glade
rooms.Description:
Thin strands of wispy fog cling to the ground in this sheltered 
glade. The ground is bare of moss, but not muddy - more of a rich damp 
peat. A number of large rocks are strewn around here and show signs of
having been recently moved. To the east, south and west, dark-leaved
bushes grow, glistening with red berries. The mist and the marsh 
continue to the north.

Exits.Description: The ground looks firmer to the north.

rooms.Name: Dark Path
rooms.Description:
Craggy rocks, overrun with prickly bushes, crowd in from all sides, 
and with the ground waterlogged and squelching with sodden moss there is
an oppressive feel to this path. A dark mist crawls over the ground, 
hiding stagnant pools and wicked quicksands. A gap in the rocky wall
opens up to the east, although it is even darker in there. The path 
continues to the south, while the north it opens out and becomes much
lighter.

Exits.Description: The ground looks to get much softer to the north.
A musty smell carries on the breeze from the east.
The dark path continues south.

rooms.Name: Rocky Passage
rooms.Description:
The narrow trail winds between high rocky walls, twisting and turning
in almost complete darkness. To the east, a huge oak tree is just 
visible, while to the west is a dark narrow trail, with claws of fog
gripping and tripping at passing feet.

Exits.Description: A HUGE oak tree rises from the ground a little way to the east.
A dark path lies to the west.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The oak is by far the largest and most ancient tree in the whole realm. The
bark is dark and mossy and the roots gnarled and twisted eons of growth.

rooms.Name: Beneath the Sacred Oak
rooms.Description:
This particular oak is one of the oldest and largest in the land. Its
bark is dark and rough, and covered with thick moss growths and clinging
parasitic vines. The oak is so tall that it quickly disappears into the
fog without narrowing - not even branches are visible from here and the
trunk must be twenty paces across. The gnarled roots look strange and 
may be worth investigating.

Exits.Description: To the west, you can make out a rocky passage leading west.
There is a narrow tunnel between the tree roots.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Some of the roots are less firmly anchored in the soil than others, and
may be moved aside to reveal a narrow tunnel, leading below the tree!

The oak is by far the largest and most ancient tree in the whole realm. The
bark is dark and mossy and the roots gnarled and twisted eons of growth.

rooms.Name: Underneath the Roots
rooms.Description:
Thick oak roots form columns in this cramped cavern beneath the great
tree. Masses of smaller vessels form curtains of growth, which must be
pushed aside to allow further movement. To the east, there is a dark
cavern visible between the dangling roots. A hole just to the west leads
upwards through the roots to ground level.

Exits.Description: A mass of roots obscures the entrance to a small underground cave.
From above comes the smell of fresher air.

rooms.Name: The Den of the Judderman
rooms.Description:
This finely decorated cave is completely out of place from its 
surroundings. The walls of the cave are perfectly flat and smooth, the
midnight black stone polished to a mirror finish. Incense burns in 
the corners of the room, and in the centre is a circle of oak leaves
about five feet across. Around the perimeter of the circle of warding
burn six candles, with the seventh candle extinguished by the breeze
caused by your entry - oh dear!

Exits.Description: To the west, you can see the roots of the great oak dangling down.

rooms.Name: Boggy Ground
rooms.Description:
Tufts of moss hide croaking frogs and chirping insects and in 
between are concealed puddles of brackish water. A pale mist drifts 
through the marsh which continues to the west, south and north. 
Eastwards, the boggy ground becomes less waterlogged but much muddier.

Exits.Description: There is more boggy ground to the north.
The ground become more muddy to the east.
There is more boggy ground to the south.
A trail disappears into the marsh to the west.

rooms.Name: In the Mud
rooms.Description:
The sodden moss and thick sticky mud mingle together here, making 
it difficult to progress. A thin veil of mist drifts around, carried by
the gentle air currents. To the west and north the ground becomes more
marshy and waterlogged, while to the east it is much muddier. The
ground to the south is a little firmer, and what appears to be a wooden
ladder is just visible through the mist.

Exits.Description: There is some boggy ground to the north.
There is more mud visible to the east.
There is some firmer ground to the south.
There is some boggy ground visible to the west.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The ladder is further south from here - and climbs up into the mist
above the marsh.

rooms.Name: In the Mud
rooms.Description:
Some patches of mud almost writhe with concealed squirming creatures
all busily burrowing and clusters of webbed footprints suggest that this
is some kind of hunting ground. Wisps of mist drift over the mudpatch, 
which extends in all directions.

Exits.Description: There is more mud to the north.
There is more mud to the east.
There is more mud to the south.
There is more mud to the west.

rooms.Name: In the Mud
rooms.Description:
Smelly yellow-green mud covers this entire area to a depth of several
inches. Bubbles and tiny piles of dried mud indicate that this place is
rich with worms and other burrowing mud dwellers. The expanse of mud 
continues to the east and north, while the ground becomes firmer to the
west. A dark trail leads south between gnarly trees and rocky outcrops.

Exits.Description: There is more mud to the north.
There is more mud to the east.
A dark path leads south away from the muddy area.
There is firmer ground to the west.

rooms.Name: Main Platform
rooms.Description:
A wide circular platform made of long thin strips of flexible wood 
hangs suspended from the mighty limbs of the great oak tree. Braces 
and struts help to keep the platform stable, although it sways gently 
along with the tree. The top of a rickety wooden ladder pokes through 
a hole in the centre of the platform. Although this area is uncovered 
and open to the sky, a second platform immediately to the east is 
sheltered by a greenish awning. Unsteady wooden walkways lead north 
and south.

Exits.Description: A swaying walkway leads north.
A large meeting hall lies to the east.
A walkway to the south is firmly anchored to a pale oak tree.
A rickety wooden ladder leads bog-side.

rooms.Name: Meeting Hall
rooms.Description:
The meeting hall is enclosed on all sides by wicker-frame walls 
interwoven with thick glossy green leaves. The roof is some kind of 
coarse fabric made from vines and has a sickly brown-green hue. The
floor is covered with dried marsh-grass, matted together with mud to 
form a slightly crunchy carpet. The only visible exit is west to the
main platform.

Exits.Description: The main platform lies to the west.

rooms.Name: Anchored Walkway
rooms.Description:
The narrow walkway is firmly anchored to the nearby tree - the 
closest any of the visible structures reach this particular oak. The 
bark of the oak is especially pale, almost glowing with a ghostly 
light. The main platform lies to the north, while to the south, the
walkway sways alarmingly as it is no longer anchored to the great tree.

Exits.Description: The main platform lies to the north.
A swaying walkway leads south.

rooms.Name: Swaying Walkway
rooms.Description:
The narrow slatted walkway swings erratically underfoot. Rough rails 
have been built onto either side to stop unwary folk falling off and
down to the bog shrouded in dark mist below. The walkway further to the
north is more firmly anchored, and to the south is a circular platform.

Exits.Description: The walkway to the north is anchored to a pale oak tree.
There is a firm platform to the south.
into the bog below.
into the bog below.
A swaying walkway leads north.
A swaying walkway leads east.

rooms.Name: Swaying Walkway
rooms.Description:
The walkway lurches alarmingly underfoot, suspended from the boughs
of the Ghostly Oak high above. The low rail on either side might stop
a merkin from falling over, but surely nothing larger. The walkway
continues unsteadily to the east, while to the west is the safety of 
a circular platform.

Exits.Description: A swaying walkway leads east.
A firm platform lies to the west.
into the bog below.
into the bog below.

To the
north is a squat round house, with a rough wooden gate across the
entrance. The wooden walkway continues both east and west.
A swaying walkway continues to the east.
A swaying walkway continues to the west.
into the bog below.
into the bog below.

mist and creeping sounds
of insects echo around. The walkway continues unsteadily westwards, 
while to the east the wooden structure seems to be anchored to the
trunk of a large blackened oak tree.
A swaying platform lies to the west.
into the bog below.
into the bog below.

the burned appearance of the tree. To the east is a wide 
platform with reinforced railings. The walkway to the west sways gently
in the breeze.
A swaying walkway leads west.

rooms.Name: A Solid Platform
rooms.Description:
Thick railings surround the edge of the platform, and also a wide
hole in the centre, through which a rough ladder protrudes. A large
square section of wood lies nearby, along with a pair of sharp axes, so
presumably this entrance could be closed off quickly and at short 
notice. Narrow walkways lead north and south around the merkin village.

Exits.Description: The walkway to the north is anchored to a mighty dark oak.
The walkway to the west is anchored to a mighty dark oak.
A rickety wooden ladder leads bog-side.

rooms.Name: Inside a Merkin Hovel
rooms.Description:
A grim stench rises from the grubby blankets strewn over the rough
pallet on the floor. Muddy footprints and a selection of filthy 
loincloths are all over the place, and there is a distinct lack of
fresh air. The only exit is to the north.

Exits.Description: A curtain separates the hovel from the rest of the roundhouse.

rooms.Name: The Merkin Roundhouse
rooms.Description:
The merkin roundhouse sways gently, being suspended from the boughs
of one of the mighty oaks trees hereabouts. A circular slab of cracked
stone in the centre forms a crude fireplace, and smoke drifts idly 
upwards through the hole in the centre of the roof. Worn leather
curtains grant some measure of privacy to the hovels north, east and
south of this communal area.

Exits.Description: The smell of a Merkin hovel comes from behind a curtain to the north.
The smell of a Merkin hovel comes from behind a curtain to the east.
The smell of a Merkin hovel comes from behind a curtain to the south.
A rough gate protects the entrance to the roundhouse from intruders.

rooms.Name: Inside a Merkin Hovel
rooms.Description:
A grim stench rises from the grubby blankets strewn over the rough
pallet on the floor. Muddy footprints and a selection of filthy 
loincloths are all over the place, and there is a distinct lack of
fresh air. The only exit is to the west.

Exits.Description: A curtain separates the hovel from the rest of the roundhouse.

rooms.Name: Inside a Merkin Hovel
rooms.Description:
The odour of old worms and rotting fruit rises from the grubby pile
of worn blankets which serves as a bed for some poor merkin. The walls 
are bare in this little hovel, although the meagre collection of 
loincloths suggests that this tiny room is home to three or four 
merkins.

Exits.Description: A curtain separates the hovel from the rest of the roundhouse.

rooms.Name: Anchored Walkway
rooms.Description:
This section of wooden walkway is anchored firmly to the Blackened
Oak, the trunk of which is just out of reach to the west. Waist high
railings are there to prevent the drunk and the stupid alike from 
falling down to the dark bog far below. To the north, the walkway widens
considerably, while to the south is a fortified platform, complete with
reinforced railings. A rough wooden gate covers the entrance to the
merkin roundhouse just to the east.

Exits.Description: A wide walkway leads north.
A Merkin Roundhouse swings from the trees to the east.
There is a fortified platform to the south.

rooms.Name: Wide Walkway
rooms.Description:
The walkway widens at this point, before a large elaborately 
decorated door just to the west. The railings form a wide arc about the 
door, as if folks often gather around the entrance and the wooden 
floorboards underfoot are worn and patched with additional pieces of 
wood. The walkway continues to the north and south.

Exits.Description: The walkway to the north sways gently in the breeze.
The walkway continues to the south.
There is a door to the west, with some important looking markings on it.

rooms.Name: The Chieftains Hut
rooms.Description:
The chieftains hut is filled with little offerings from his grateful
subjects. On little shelves around the perimeter of the room are a
selection of the shiniest stones and most unusual feathers. On the far
side of the room is a little bed and in the centre of the room a 
rope ladder leads down.

Exits.Description: The main walkway lies to the east.
A sturdy rope-ladder leads down through the fog to bog-side.

rooms.Name: The Chieftains Private Wallow
rooms.Description:
This tiny area of swamp is completely isolated from its surroundings
by an impenetrable wall of rushes and marsh grasses. In the center of 
this little area, is a small merkin-sized mud patch - especially for
the chieftain to wallow in private.

Exits.Description: A sturdy rope ladder leads upwards to the chieftains home.

rooms.Name: Swaying Platform
rooms.Description:
The narrow bamboo handrails on either side of this narrow walkway 
are not really very sturdy, and as if to emphasise this, the wooden
path chooses this moment to lurch alarmingly in the gentle breeze.
The walkway continues to the north and south.

Exits.Description: There is an intersection of several walkways to the north.
The walkway becomes much wider to the south.
into the bog below.
into the bog below.
The walkway to the north is firmly anchored to the tree nearby.
A narrow walkway to the east sways alarmingly in the gentle breeze.
A swaying walkway leads south.

rooms.Name: Narrow Walkway
rooms.Description:
This walkway is narrower and less steady than a lot of the others 
and has a rope handrail which provides no support at all. Even the 
slightest breeze causes the walkway to lurch alarmingly. The walkway
further to the east sways in the breeze, or to the west is the safety
of a more stable intersection.

Exits.Description: The narrow walkway continues east towards a gigantic tree.
The narrow walkway rises to meet an intersecting platform.
into the bog below.
into the bog below.
The narrow walkway opens up to a wider path surrounding an oak tree.
The narrow walkway continues west.
into the bog below.
into the bog below.

A narrow unsteady looking walkway leads west away from the
tree.
The walkway curves south and east around the Great Tree.
A fragile walkway leads west.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The markings are etched into the bark of the tree and written in a spidery
script. The letters are unfamiliar, but they look like a cross between
dwarf runes, and elvish high script - they must be magical in some way.

rooms.Name: Before the Great Tree
rooms.Description:
A sturdy wooden platform is anchored to the massive bole of The Oak.
The wooden rail is sturdy enough to support the weight of even the 
chubbiest merkin, and the walkway continues around the tree to the east
and west. To the north a small hut swings from the branches of the tree.
You can enter the little hut across a narrow and flimsy looking bridge.

Exits.Description: A tiny and very smelly hut lies to the north.
The walkway curves east and south around the Great Tree.
The walkway curves west and south around the Great Tree.

rooms.Name: Inside the Shamans Hut
rooms.Description:
The shamans hut is filthy even by merkin standards. There are not 
even any blankets on the floor - only a nest of muddy oak leaves. A
foul smell lingers in the air, and it is a while before you realise that
the hut is lit by torches made from dung.

Exits.Description: To the south is a wide walkway, anchored to the Great Tree.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: EEEEeeeeewwwww! Its horrible (and probably not very hygienic either!)

rooms.Name: Before the Great Tree
rooms.Description:
Thick wooden planks form a sturdy walkway encircling the Sacred Oak
Tree. A wooden waist-high rail is there for safety purposes. The Oak
towers so high above that its branches disappear into the clouds, and
below, the trunk plummets into thick mist. The bark is pale and almost
glowing, and there are spidery runes scrawled all over it.

Exits.Description: The walkway curves north and west around the Great Tree.
The walkway curves south and west around the Great Tree.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The markings are etched into the bark of the tree and written in a spidery
script. The letters are unfamiliar, but they look like a cross between
dwarf runes, and elvish high script - they must be magical in some way.

rooms.Name: Before the Great Tree
rooms.Description:
The strange pale oak tree almost seems to hum with power. Tiny 
spidery scrawlings cover the bark, possibly some kind of prayers or
magic spells. A wide platform encircles the oak, and continues around
to the east and west.

Exits.Description: The walkway curves east and north around the Great Tree.
The walkway curves wear and north around the Great Tree.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The markings are etched into the bark of the tree and written in a spidery
script. The letters are unfamiliar, but they look like a cross between
dwarf runes, and elvish high script - they must be magical in some way.

rooms.Name: Anchored Platform
rooms.Description:
This little area is lovely and calm. The pathway is firmly connected
to the weeping oak, just over the rail on the west side, and there are
intersections to the north and south. Drooping fronds dangle down from
the branches of the weeping oak, giving a nice bit of shade.

Exits.Description: A sturdy corner platform lies to the north.
There is an intersection of several walkways to the south.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The oak tree is one of the largest in the area. Unlike a regular oak, the
branches of this one seem to droop like a weeping willow, and tiny
streams of sap flow down its bark like tears.

rooms.Name: Corner Platform
rooms.Description:
This corner of the merkin village looks to be one of the busiest 
parts and the boards underfoot are polished smooth by the passing of
many leathery webbed feet. The walkway to the south and west looks to
loop around the whole village, but to the east is a wider pathway 
leading away from the village.

Exits.Description: There is a narrow extension to the platform, leading east.
The walkway to the south is securely anchored to the trees.
A walkway leads west.

rooms.Name: East Extension
rooms.Description:
This wide annex to the merkin village is made from rougher pieces of
timber, although they are worn smooth now by the passing of so many
feet. A number of reed baskets lie to either side of the walkway. The
extension continues to the east, while to the west is the main part of
the village.

Exits.Description: The extension continues further east.
The corner platform lies to the west.

rooms.Name: East Extension
rooms.Description:
Gathering baskets are stacked up against the rough wooden rails on 
either side of the walkway, ready to be collected and used by the
hunter-gatherer merkins. To the north there is a wide platform, with 
more baskets, and a ladder. To the west, is a whole village, suspended 
from the five sacred oaks.

Exits.Description: To the north, there is a descent platform.

The east extension leads west back towards the main part of the 
village.

rooms.Name: Descent Point
rooms.Description:
Empty gathering baskets are strewn around this platform, along with
long lengths of rope, woven from vines. A rough-looking ladder protrudes
through a hole in the centre of the platform, allowing access to the 
prime hunting grounds of the marsh. Aside from the ladder, the only
exit is south.

Exits.Description: The walkway to the south eventually leads to the Merkin village.
A rickety wooden ladder leads bogside.

rooms.Name: Inside a Merkin Hovel
rooms.Description:
A grubby pile of leathery loincloths and torn cloaks covers the 
rough wooden pallet which the owner of this smelly hovel presumably 
calls home. Occupying pride of place in a little alcove on the east
wall is a strangely coloured rock, and a speckled eagles feather.

Exits.Description: A curtain separates the hovel from the rest of the roundhouse.

rooms.Name: The Merkin Roundhouse
rooms.Description:
A small fire burns on the wide stone slab in the centre of the 
roundhouse, the smoke drifting wearily upwards through a small hole in
the centre of the straw roof. Alcoves to the north, west and east are
divided from the main part of the house by worn leather curtains, which
fail to keep by the unpleasant smell. The main walkway lies to the 
south through a rough wooden gate.

Exits.Description: The smell of a Merkin hovel comes from behind a curtain to the north.
The smell of a Merkin hovel comes from behind a curtain to the east.
A rough gate protects the entrance to the roundhouse from intruders.
The smell of a Merkin hovel comes from behind a curtain to the north.

rooms.Name: Inside a Merkin Hovel
rooms.Description:
This cramped single room dwelling could hardly be described as 
a home, but for some primitive merkin, it undoubtedly is. There is 
barely enough room to stand beside the messy bed and the damp air 
makes this more than a little claustrophobic. The communal section 
of the roundhouse lies to the south.

Exits.Description: A curtain separates the hovel from the rest of the roundhouse.

rooms.Name: Inside a Merkin Hovel
rooms.Description:
A grim stench rises from the grubby blankets strewn over the rough
pallet on the floor. Muddy footprints and a selection of filthy 
loincloths are all over the place, and there is a distinct lack of
fresh air. The only exit is to the east.

Exits.Description: A curtain separates the hovel from the rest of the roundhouse.

rooms.Name: Anchored Walkway
rooms.Description:
Attached directly to the weeping oak, this section of the platforms
is relatively stable. To the north, a merkin roundhouse dangles from the
drooping limbs and sways gently in the breeze. There is an intersection
to the east, but the walkway continues for quite some distance to the 
west.

Exits.Description:
A rough wooden gate blocks the way into the Merkin roundhouse to the 
north.
A stable platform lies to the east.
A swaying walkway continues west.

rooms.Name: Swaying Walkway
rooms.Description:
This narrow wooden walkway is roughly half way between the swaying oak
and the weeping oak, whose drooping limbs dangle around you. To the 
south is a large wooden building attached to the weeping oak, which
smells of stagnant water and fresh mud. The walkway continues east and
west.

Exits.Description: A swaying walkway continues east.
A door blocks entrance to a small hut to the south.
A swaying walkway continues west.

rooms.Name: Inside the Merkin Nursery
rooms.Description:
In the merkin nursery are a number of large pens, into which the 
young merkins are divided by age. Until they reach maturity, merkins
require very little apart from fresh mud (the good stuff has a high
slime-content) and fresh worms (for protein). Once the merkins are
large and agile enough to climb out of the pens themselves, they
are considered grown and are expected to begin to provide for the rest
of the village.

Exits.Description: A door leads north to a swaying walkway.

A smell of stagnant water comes from behind a leathery curtain to the 
south.

rooms.Name: Merkin Hatchery
rooms.Description:
The hatchery is where all the freshly hatched spawn are placed, to 
gain some weight and begin the maturation process before becoming 
true merkins. The smell in here is not very pleasant, but a much
worse smell leaks from under the door to the west. A leather curtain 
hangs over the northern exit.

Exits.Description: A leathery curtain hangs across the northern archway.
A sliding door divides this room from the spawning room to the west.

rooms.Name: The Spawning Room
rooms.Description:
This is possibly the most unpleasant aspect of merkin society - the
village spawning room. Despite their notions of romance, merkin
reproduction is like most other amphibians and requires only a pond of
stagnant water, and some privacy. In this room, large vats of marsh
water stand ready for the procreation process. Some contain fresh spawn
and others are still awaiting fertile couples.

Exits.Description: A sliding door divides this room from the hatchery.

rooms.Name: Walkway Junction
rooms.Description:
This intersection high above the marsh is securely anchored to the
large oak tree just to the northwest. Gaps between the boards have been
covered over with lumps of mud fresh from the marsh. The walkway 
continues to the east and west, and to the north the way is barred by
a hanging drape of moss and leaves.

Exits.Description: A leafy hanging drapes across the entrance to a secluded walkway.
A walkway continues east.
A walkway continues west.

rooms.Name: Secluded Walkway
rooms.Description:
Thick moss covers the oak tree on the west of the pathway, while to
the east, dangling vines and descending tree branches form a kind of
tunnel high above the marsh. The walkway continues towards the north, 
while to the south, there is an intersection visible through the
hanging leaves.

Exits.Description: The secluded walkway continues north.
A leafy hanging drapes across the walkway to the south.

rooms.Name: Secluded Walkway
rooms.Description:
Oak boughs heavy with vines, moss and flowers form an archway over 
this secluded walkway, anchored to the huge oak tree. From this corner
platform it is possible to see another two large oak trees poking out
of the mist which clings to the marsh below. The walkway continues to
the south and west.

Exits.Description: The secluded walkway continues south.
The secluded walkway continues west.

rooms.Name: Hanging Garden
rooms.Description:
Sweet perfume wafts from the red and blue flowers scattered over the 
railings and down the bark of the oak on the south side of the walkway.
A pair of rough wooden benches look made for two, and give a great view 
northwards over the misty marsh towards forested mountains in the 
distance.

Exits.Description: A secluded walkway continues to the east.
The hanging garden continues to the west.

rooms.Name: Hanging Garden
rooms.Description:
Clusters of bright yellow and blue flowers grow haphazardly over the
rails and along the edges of the platforms. There is a low bench here, 
about the right size for two people - this can only be some kind of
lovers lane! The flowery secluded walkway continues to the east, while
to the south there are no flowers.

Exits.Description: The hanging garden continues east.
A secluded walkway leads south.

rooms.Name: Secluded Walkway
rooms.Description:
Hanging vines and graceful tree limbs have grown around this section
of the platforms giving it a private feel. Thick moss growing over the
tree-bark on the east side muffles any sound, and the mist which 
drifts up from the marsh has a similar damping effect on noise.

Exits.Description: A hanging garden lies to the north.
A platform lies to the south, beyond a curtain of vines.

rooms.Name: Corner Platform
rooms.Description:
Firmly anchored to the Swaying Oak, this roughly square platform 
creaks slightly as weight is redistributed on top, but otherwise is 
very stable. The hanging boughs of the oak, and a tangle of dangling
vines blocks the way north, but the walkways to the east and south
are unobstructed.

Exits.Description: A secluded walkway lies to the north, beyond a curtain of vines.
A walkway continues east.
A swaying walkway continues south.

rooms.Name: Sturdy Walkway
rooms.Description:
Thick beams support this section of walkway, which rather than being
suspended is anchored firmly to the large oak tree to the north. There
are intersections to the east and west, under the sheltering limbs of 
the smallest of the great trees.

Exits.Description: A walkway continues east.
A platform lies to the west.

rooms.Name: Swaying Platform
rooms.Description:
The narrow slatted walkway sways in the gentle air currents high
above the marsh. Thick ropes made from some kind of twisted vines creak
as the platform moves. To the north is one of the Great Trees, and a
more stable platform anchored to it, while to the south, the walkway
continues.

Exits.Description: A sturdy platform lies to the north.
A swaying platform lies to the south.
into the bog below.
into the bog below.
A swaying Walkway continues north.
The main platform lies to the south.
into the bog below.
into the bog below.

of some hapless impoverished merkin, 
although the three brightly coloured rocks and the eagles feather
displayed proudly above the squalid bed suggests that the inhabitant
is content with his lot in life. To the east the roundhouse opens up
into a more spacious communal area.

rooms.Name: Merkin Roundhouse
rooms.Description:
The merkin roundhouse is a low circular wooden frame hut, with walls
made of overlapping flexible willow twigs. To stop the wind coming 
through and blowing things around, thick globs of swamp mud have been
haphazardly pasted across the cracks. In this central area a small fire 
burns on a circular stone plate. The smoke escapes through a narrow
hole in the roof. To the north, east and west ragged leathery curtains
hide more private alcoves where the merkins sleep.

Exits.Description: The smell of a Merkin hovel comes from behind a curtain to the north.
The smell of a Merkin hovel comes from behind a curtain to the east.
A rough gate protects the entrance to the roundhouse from intruders.
The smell of a Merkin hovel comes from behind a curtain to the west.

rooms.Name: Inside a Merkin Hovel
rooms.Description:
A grim stench rises from the grubby blankets strewn over the rough
pallet on the floor. Muddy footprints and a selection of filthy 
loincloths are all over the place, and there is a distinct lack of
fresh air. The only exit is to the west.

Exits.Description: A curtain separates the hovel from the rest of the roundhouse.

rooms.Name: Inside a Merkin Hovel
rooms.Description:
This cramped single room dwelling could hardly be described as 
a home, but for some primitive merkin, it undoubtedly is. There is 
barely enough room to stand beside the messy bed and the damp air 
makes this more than a little claustrophobic. The communal section 
of the roundhouse lies to the south.

Exits.Description: A curtain separates the hovel from the rest of the roundhouse.

rooms.Name: Floating In The Air
rooms.Description:
You find yourself floating about 50 meters above the ground. You see the
soft ground below you and suddenly wish that you were firmly planted there.

Exits.Description:
Above you can barely make out what seems to be a large structure reaching
towards the heavens.
Below you see the Mountain of the Gods.

rooms.Name: Flying in the Air
rooms.Description:
You are flying quite high above the ground. You think you can see your house
off to the left! Something very big is also directly above and to the south of
you.

Exits.Description: Above you is a large, fluffy cloud.
Below will take you closer to the ground. . . it looks safer.

rooms.Name: A Fluffy Cloud
rooms.Description:
You are standing on a fluffy cloud before a large structure of sorts. You
notice that the structure is covered in gold and some sort of writing covers
the outside of the great doors.

Exits.Description: To the south lies a glowing temple.
Below you is the path back towards land. . . you might better head that way.

rooms.Name: Entrance to Temple
rooms.Description:
You find yourself standing in the entrance to the great Temple of the
Samurai. This temple glows golden and is a tribute to all of the great warriors
of the past. You feel as if you have intruded where mortals were never meant to
tread.

Exits.Description: North of you is the exit to the temple.
South you notice a flower filled room.

rooms.Name: Ceremonial Gardens
rooms.Description:
You find yourself in a brightly lit room. All around you are flowers and
wild herbs. A message scribbled on the wall tells you that this is where the
warriors prepared gifts for their sick companions.

Exits.Description: North of you is the entrance hall of the temple.
East of you is another room in the temple.

rooms.Name: Hospital
rooms.Description:
You are in a room filled with empty cots. Elixirs and herbs line the walls.
Books cover the shelves. The room itself has an antiseptic smell and reminds
you of a hospital.

Exits.Description: North is the abode of the shogun.
You see the gardens back to the west.

rooms.Name: Shogun of Jin
rooms.Description:
You find yourself in a peaceful abode. Before you stands the Shogun of Jin.
Although you don't know exactly what Jin means, you feel that this man can
teach you much about people. Stairs lead upward to the next level.

Exits.Description: To the south lies the hospital.
A golden stairway leads you ever upward.

rooms.Name: Homely Hallway
rooms.Description:
You find yourself standing in a homely looking hallway. This room reminds
you of your youth and brings back images of your parents teaching you right
from wrong.

Exits.Description: South lead to another room.
To the west is another room.
A golden stairway leads you downward.

rooms.Name: Another Room
rooms.Description:
You find yourself in another room similar to that you just came from. You
can't particularly tell any differences in this room at all.

Exits.Description: East leads back where you came from.

rooms.Name: Yet Another Room
rooms.Description:
You find yourself standing in yet another room. Your mind reels as you
discover this room is the same as the one you just came from!

Exits.Description: North is where you came from.
East leads to a room that LOOKS different.

rooms.Name: Shogun of Gi
rooms.Description:
You finally find yourself in a different room! You see the Shogun of Gi
standing before you pointing his finger and lecturing you for killing his
fellow Shogun. Now you gonna get it!

Exits.Description: East is where you came from.
A stairway leads upward.

rooms.Name: Third Floor Landing
rooms.Description:
You find yourself on a landing of the third floor of the temple. Your legs
ache from all the climbing and you wonder to yourself exactly how many floors
this place has.

Exits.Description: To the east you see a slave chamber.

rooms.Name: Slave Chamber
rooms.Description:
You find yourself in a room full of slaves. The slaves, however, have no
chains, shackles, or bondage devices of any kind. These people are voluntary
slaves to their master . . . the Shogun of Chu. They don't feel worthy to be
anything else. Do you?

Exits.Description: To the north you hear sounds of metalworking.
The west is where you were a minute ago!

rooms.Name: Metal Shop
rooms.Description:
You are standing in a metalworking shop. The trainees here are pounding
their swords and other weapons into razor sharp tools of defense. You watch as
they continue to pound away and think to yourself 'Hmm... I wonder if they
would temper my sword?'

Exits.Description: South leads to the slave chamber.
You see another Shogun chamber to your west.

rooms.Name: Shogun of Chu
rooms.Description:
You find yourself standing in the chamber of the Shogun of Chu. All around
him you notice warriors who are completely loyal to their master. You better
not try to mess with this guy . . .

Exits.Description: Sounds of metalworking come from the east.
Stairs lead upward yet again.

rooms.Name: Fourth Floor Landing
rooms.Description:
You are standing on the fourth floor of the temple. You have traveled much
too far already, but feel that going onward is a must. Something about this
floor demands respect.

Exits.Description: You hear water to the south.
Stairs lead down from here.

rooms.Name: The bath
rooms.Description:
You are standing in a public bath. Samurai's walk around in towels and glare
at you for intruding. You have a strange feeling that no one should ever
interrupt a samurai while he's bathing.

Exits.Description: A landing is to your north.
The antechamber is to your east.

rooms.Name: The Antechamber of Ko
rooms.Description:
You stand in the antechamber of the Shogun of Ko. The room is brightly
colored and the walls are filled with inscriptions honoring fathers and mothers
of the samurai who abide here.

Exits.Description: To the north is the chamber of the Shogun.
Water can be heard to the west.

rooms.Name: Shogun of Ko
rooms.Description:
You are standing in the chamber of the Shogun of Ko. This shogun looks
exactly like your father. In fact, he looks exactly like anyone's father. You
expect to see him pull his belt and whip you at any moment... then you notice
his weapon.

Exits.Description: The antechamber lies to the south.
A ladder leads upward.

rooms.Name: Fifth Floor Landing
rooms.Description:
You are on the landing of the fifth floor of this mammoth temple. You have a
feeling that you still have quite a ways to go, however. You notice drawings on
the wall telling of the respectful warriors of long ago.

Exits.Description: Grinding sounds come from the south.
The antechamber lies to the west.

rooms.Name: Weapons Room
rooms.Description:
You have entered the weapons room. You see warriors standing before
primitive, yet very effective, tools for putting a razor's edge on swords. It
looks like they could really put a hurtin' on someone with their weapons.

Exits.Description: A landing is to your north.

rooms.Name: The antechamber
rooms.Description:
You are in the Antechamber of the Shogun. This room is full of paintings of
warriors, written declarations of respect for fellow Samurai, and what seems to
be a grocery list.

Exits.Description: A landing is to your east.
The Shogun's chamber is south of you.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The list reads:
		Eggs
		Flour
		Condoms

rooms.Name: Shogun of Rei
rooms.Description:
You are in the chamber of the Shogun of Rei. The Shogun here knows well of
the value of other people. In fact, he even respects your insignificant
carcass. Hmm . . . how odd, no one else does.

Exits.Description: The antechamber is north of you.
A stairway leads up from here.

rooms.Name: Sixth Floor Landing
rooms.Description:
You are standing on the landing of the sixth floor. The muscles in your body
ache, you're thirsty, you haven't eaten for some time, and now would be a good
time to rest some.

Exits.Description: A strange humming is north of you.
Yet another antechamber is west.
Stairs lead down from here.

rooms.Name: Machine Room
rooms.Description:
You are standing in a large room filled with computers. This room is where
the samurai must learn word processing skills that they are known to have. Kewl
huh?

Exits.Description: A landing is south of you.

rooms.Name: The antechamber
rooms.Description:
You are in the antechamber of yet another Shogun. You faintly remember
hearing somewhere that there are about eight basic principles of the samurai.
Only three more to go . . .

Exits.Description: The Shogun chamber is north.
The landing is to your east.

rooms.Name: Shogun of Chi
rooms.Description:
You stand before the Shogun of Chi. His glowing aura tells you that he is
not only extremely good, but VERY wise. You think that this wise individual
could indeed teach you quite a few things about life.

Exits.Description: The antechamber is to the south.
A ladder leads upward.

rooms.Name: The Seventh Floor Landing
rooms.Description:
You are standing on the landing of the seventh floor of the temple. The
walls are very clean and the writings on the wall tell of crusades for truth.
You wish you truthfully knew how many darn rooms were in this temple.

Exits.Description: South of you comes the sounds of scribes.

rooms.Name: Hall of Truth
rooms.Description:
You stare at the scribes who seem oblivious to your presence. But upon
looking closer, you find that no scribes are in fact even in this room! You
notice that truth is not all within the realm of sight. Nifty idea ain't it??

Exits.Description: A landing is to your north.
To your east you hear cheers.

rooms.Name: Courtyard
