the west you can see people walking along Temple Street to visit the
various merchants.There is a faint portal to the east with an odd
triangle engraved on it.

rooms.Name: Tailor's
rooms.Description:
You have entered a tailor's shop, bright and colorful garments are
here on display. You can probably find clothing here for any
important occasion. Like that wedding you heard about for this
weekend...

rooms.Name: Jeweler's
rooms.Description:
You have entered a Jeweler's Shop, tasteful racks have carefully
arranged jewelry and gems for sale. I am sure you can find that
special gift for that special person in your life here. Remember:
Diamonds are forever!

rooms.Name: Rosy's Flowers
rooms.Description:
This is a florist shop. Beautiful roses adorn the shelves in
tasteful arrangements. You are nearly overwhelmed by the smell of
growing things. Isn't there someone whose day you could brighten with
a thoughtful gift?

rooms.Name: Stationary Shop
rooms.Description:
Fine Stationary is on display here. Writing implements are also
available.  Why don't you pick up a supply and practice your
spelling!

rooms.Name: City Bank
rooms.Description:
This is the city bank. In the interests of security all
transactions are now handled by computer. The clerks got tired of
being attacked by newbies.

rooms.Name: The Casino
rooms.Description:
Gambling of all types is available here. Try some blackjack,
roulette, craps, or if you are a real player, go downstairs for some
poker!

Exits.Description: The poker palace is downstairs, hmm maybe you could double your money.

rooms.Name: City Library
rooms.Description:
This building has a long hallway running north and south.  Each
cubby has a different board of information. On the west side (in
order of closest to farthest) is the Mortal board, Quest board, and
Skills & Spells board.  On the east side (in order of closest to
farthest) is the Social board, remort board, and Area board.  The
entire building is silent and you are expected to be too.  Please no
spamming in here and post only what the room states is acceptable
please.  In general, no hateful postings or vulgar language please,
or the posting will be removed.  Thank you.

rooms.Name: Roulette Room
rooms.Description:
This room only contains a large roulette table. There is a sign on
the wall.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
HOW TO PLAY:
> BET <AMOUNT> <SLOT> - where slot is 0-36, LOW, MID, HIGH, RED or BLUE
> BET LIST - lists all your bets
> LOOK TABLE
Bets must be between 1000-100000

rooms.Name: The Old South Gate
rooms.Description:
The ruins of the old south gate stand here.  This gate has been
unused and unguarded for years now, and has fallen into a state of
disrepair.  Moss grows everywhere, eating into rock, and parts of the
wall have crumbled off.  A small sign points south, with the word
"Dump" written on it.  You hear the bustle of peasants to the north.

Exits.Description: You see the common square.
You see the sewers.

rooms.Name: City Library: East->Social Board/West->Mortal Board
rooms.Description:
This is a long hallway which starts in the south at the entrance
and runs the length of the building.  You see little reading rooms to
the east and west. Each has it's own purpose.

Exits.Description:
You see in the distance, the Social board used for player social
announcements.

You see in the distance, the Mortal board used for discussions with
Elite's gods.

rooms.Name: City Library: East -> Remort Board/West-> Quest Board
rooms.Description:
This is a long hallway which starts in the south at the entrance
and runs the length of the building.  You see little reading rooms to
the east and west.  Each has it's own purpose.

Exits.Description:
You see in the distance, the Remort board used for discussing Remort
policies and information.

You see in the distance, the Quest board used for announcing upcomming
quests and past results.  It is usefull for discussing quests.

rooms.Name: City Library: East->Area board/West->Skills&Spells board
rooms.Description:
This is a long hallway which starts in the south at the entrance
and runs the length of the building.  You see little reading rooms to
the east and west.  Each has it's own purpose.

Exits.Description:
You see in the distance, the Area board used for discussing areas, mob,
equipment, and such with the gods and other players.  Hints, but not
actual directions or solutions can be given here as well.

You see in the distance, the Skills and spells board used for
discussing the character related parts of the game with the other
players and the gods (new ideas, comments, etc).

rooms.Name: City Library: Area Board
rooms.Description:
You are by the Area board which contains information about areas.
Please post only things relating to areas on this board, such as
hints on areas, level information, comments on areas, ideas for new
areas and mob, etc.  Thank you -- Midguaard Librarian --

Exits.Description: You see the main hallway of the Midgaard Library.

rooms.Name: City Library: Skills and Spells Board
rooms.Description:
You are by the spells and skills board which contains information
about character spells and skills. Please post only things relating
to character abilities here, which includes spells and skills
corrections, ideas, comments, and character classes and races.
Thank you -- Midgaard Librarian --

Exits.Description: You see the main hallway of the Midgaard Library.

rooms.Name: City Library: Quest Board
rooms.Description:
You are by the Quest board which contains information about
quests. Please post only things related to quests here on this board.
This includes such information as quest results, comments, ideas,
suggestions, etc.  Thank you -- Midgaard Librarian --

Exits.Description: You see the main hallway of the Midgaard Library.

rooms.Name: City Library: Remort Board
rooms.Description:
You are by the Remort board which contains information about
remorting.  This is mostly an informational board, but comments and
questions about remorting can be posted on this board.  Thank you --
Midgaard Librarian --

Exits.Description: You see the main hallway of the Midgaard Library.

rooms.Name: City Library: Social Board
rooms.Description:
You are by the social board which contains general social
information for this mud.  This includes wedding and divorce
announcement, social announcements, character announcements, clan
information not clan specific, taunts, teases, and other things
related to the general social aspects as you might see in a society
page of your local newspaper.  This can include special events too.
With the exception of clan questions, please do not use this board as
a serious message board as far as asking the Immortals any thing in
general.  That is found on the Mortal board 2 west of here.  Thank
you -- Midgaard Librarian --

Exits.Description: You see the main hallway of Midgaard's library.

rooms.Name: City Library: Mortal Board
rooms.Description:
You are by the Mortal board which is for general information and
posts which is passed between the mortals and Immortals on this mud.
This includes such things as general questions and comments about the
mud, it's operation, or anything specific to it's operation (shy of
code).  This also is for anything not covered in any of the other
boards.  In general, a way of discussing things with the gods of
Elite.  Thank you -- Midgaard Librarian --

Exits.Description: You see the main hallway to the Midgaard Library.

rooms.Name: Midgaard Chat room
rooms.Description:
You are in a slightly noisy room.  The noise is caused from
several conversations going on at once.  This is a no magic room as
the talking is cause for more then enough spam, thank you very much,
and you should bring a supply of food and drink here.  Willful
spamming of this room is cause for removal.  Repeated offenses will
lead to jailing.

Exits.Description:
You see a slight shimmering across the archway holding back the flood of
sound.

rooms.Name: City Library: East->Clan Board
rooms.Description:
This is a long hallway which starts in the south at the entrance
and runs the length of the building.  You see a little reading room
to the east.

rooms.Name: City Library: Clan Board
rooms.Description:
You are by the Clan Board which contains information dealing with
the offical clans and their structure as a whole (Not for a clan to
promote or discuss clan business or to degrade another clan).  If you
have questions, comments, or other official postings dealing with
clans (as a whole), then post them here. (Do not ask about individual
clans here either.)

rooms.Name: Bot Storage Room
rooms.Description:
This is where all the bots go when they are left on unattended.
By going up, you go to the temple.  If a bot is caught automatically
going up and back to a bot room or clan house, they will be put here
and frozen until such a time that the player talks to an Imm capable
of unfreezing the PC.

Exits.Description: This path leads you to the temple.

rooms.Name: Temple stairs
rooms.Description:
This is a magic room that was constructed by the mightiest remorts
of the mud.  After waves of violence struck Midgaard when the avatars
could not enter the guilds, their most powerful wizards constructed
this portal into the guilds.  You see light shining in from above.

Exits.Description: The stair continues down.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
This is the non-clan Bot room.  Please use or have your clan place its
Bots inside of your clan house.

rooms.Name: BOT Room
rooms.Description:
You are in a special room up in the temple which has been set
aside for Bots, those mystical automatons which make life simple.
Please park them here and there is a max of 2.  If you are in a clan,
please go to a clan bot room

Exits.Description: There is a stair here going down.

rooms.Name: The Poker Room
rooms.Description:
You are standing in the Midgaard Poker Room. It is a smelly,
smokefilled room with many tables. There are decks of cards
everywhere. Why don't you settle down with some friends and play
their shirts off? There's a sign here with the title: HOW TO PLAY?

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
*************************************************************************
*
                          GENERIC CARD GAME BY IO

        Appoint one player as dealer.  Everyone else follow him/her.
        The dealer can:
        GET CARDS               - get a new deck of cards. or get all the
                                  cards back from the players.
        DEAL <player> #         - deal # number of cards to player.
        DEAL ALL #              - deal # number of cards to all players.
                                  i.e. dealer and all followers.
        SHUFFLE CARDS           - shuffles the deck.

        All players can:
        LOOK CARDS              - Look at your own hand.
        DISPLAY CARDS           - Show others in room your cards.
        DROP CARDS # # # ...    - Drops cards (Back to dealer's deck)
                                  ex: > drop ca 3 2 5
                                  will drop the second, third and fifth
card.
                                  or: > drop ca all
        SORT CARDS              - Sort the cards in your hand.
        SWITCH CARDS # #        - Will switch two cards in your hand.
                                  i.e. for putting your aces together.

        System newly made and will certainly have bugs.
*************************************************************************
*

rooms.Name: Clifftops
rooms.Description:
The trail comes to an abrupt end at an impressive range of cliffs, 
which look out over a wide ocean.  There was once a city here, according
to rumor, but no longer.  You think it might be possible to make your 
way down to the waters edge.

Exits.Description: You see a trail through the forest.
A narrow pathway leads down the cliff face.

rooms.Name: Crumbling Pathway
rooms.Description:
As you edge carefully along the pathway it begins to crumble, chunks of 
stone dropping into the sea below you.  There doesn't seem to be a way 
back anymore, so the only way is to continue downwards.

Exits.Description: The path has started to crumble behind you, you can't go back this way.

The pathway ahead looks more dangerous than you first thought, but the 
safety of a ledge is not far ahead of you.

rooms.Name: In a whirlpool
rooms.Description:
The ledge falls away beneath your feet and you fall into the water, 
as you try to swim for shore you become caught in a whirlpool which 
pulls at you insistently.  You don't think you can keep your head above 
the water any longer.  You could try diving down to clear the current - 
better take a deep breath.

Exits.Description: You can't see anything, the whirlpool is dragging you underwater.

You can make out the shapes on the sea floor, they don't  look like 
natural formations.

rooms.Name: Entrance to the city of Delray
rooms.Description:
Although you are standing on the bottom of the ocean, you appear not 
to have drowned.  You stand before the grand city of Delray, sunk 
beneath the ocean nearly half a century ago by a powerful magician in 
order to save its inhabitants from invasion.  Although four hundred 
years have passed above, the inhabitants live on beneath the sea, 
oblivious to the passing of time, and the rays and dogfish swimming down 
the streets. The city lies to the north and the palace gate, encrusted 
with coral and colourful seaweeds, stand proudly to the east.

Exits.Description:
Looking north you see a thriving city, its halfling citizens hurrying 
about their business.  Streets and shops, taverns and houses, all look 
familiar to you, but not the fish swimming down the main street, 
seaweeds and corals growing over the buildings.  Without doubt this is 
the strangest sight you have ever seen.  Surprisingly the halflings do 
not even seem to notice the sea creatures with whom they share their 
city.

The palace  gate stand proudly  before you, the  brasswork is tarnished 
and  the shape  disguised by  growths of  coral, but  they look to be in 
working order.

The ocean  surface  glitters  above you and the  whirlpool is off to the 
south. You can now surface clear of the current and swim to shore.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Beneath the brightly coloured coral, and flowing fronds of seaweed you 
can just make out a silver five-pointed star, the symbol of the city of 
Delray.

rooms.Name: Treading water
rooms.Description:
You  float on  the  ocean  surface at the  base of the  cliffs. It 
looks possible to climb back up to the top from here - though it won't be 
easy.  Or you could swim back down to the city and take another look 
around.

Exits.Description: There looks to be a route back up the cliffs.
You see the city of Delray below you.

rooms.Name: Halfway up the cliffs
rooms.Description:
You cling dangerously to the cliff face, high above the rocks. You 
don't think you could survive the fall so don't look down!

Exits.Description: You can see the clifftops above you.
It would be suicide to try and climb back down this way.

rooms.Name: SPLAT!
rooms.Description: You were right...suicidal.

Exits.Description: You are staring at the sky through dead eyes.

rooms.Name: Palace Hallway
rooms.Description:
You stand in the hallway of the grand palace of Delray. The ceiling 
glitters above you in the light from peculiar looking lanterns in niches
in the walls. The floor  is tiled, but there is a layer of sandy-silt 
everywhere which wafts around your feet as you move.

Exits.Description: You see that the hallway opens out to the east.
You see the Palace gate.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: They must be magical - how else could they burn below the ocean..?

rooms.Name: Intersection in the Palace
rooms.Description:
A fantastic high domed ceiling and crystal chandelier catch your eye 
upon entering this room, an intersection of a north-south passage and 
hallways leading east and west.  The chandelier glows with a magical 
fire, and the symbol of the kingdom of Delray is inlaid into the floor, 
a shining silver five-pointed star.  Small brightly patterned fish flit 
about the chandelier making it appear even more outlandishly coloured, 
and a small squadron of tiny crabs scuttle eastwards.

Exits.Description: A dim passage leads north.
A hallway leads east.
A dim passage leads south.
A hallway leads west

rooms.Name: North-South Passage
rooms.Description:
The passage seems dim after the brightness of the intersection, but 
it is lit with the same strange lanterns as the entrance hallway. Some 
of the niches contain small idols and statues which appear to be images 
of the heros of Delray.

Exits.Description: You see an intersection to the north.
You see an intersection to the south.

rooms.Name: West-end of the Great Hall
rooms.Description:
You find yourself at the west end of a spectacular hall. The vaulted 
ceiling is covered by fantastic paintings, which seem to represent the 
gods, smiling benevolently over the city.  The hall is lit as bright as 
daylight, although you can see no lanterns.  To the north there is a set 
of ornate double doors, and opposite these, to the south, you see a 
guard room.  The hall continues to the east, and to the west is a 
hallway leading towards an intersection.

Exits.Description: You see a pair of ornate doors leading to the kings private apartments.
The Great Hall continues to the east.
You see a small guardroom.
A short hallway leads to the intersection.

rooms.Name: Private stairs
rooms.Description:
You stand at the entrance to the kings private apartments. The floor 
is carpeted in a rich red, although a thin layer of sand covers 
everything.  The Great Hall is to the south, while the kings apartments 
are situated on the next floor, atop the magnificent gilded staircase 
ahead of you.

Exits.Description: You see the ornate doors to the south.
The golden staircase winds upwards to the kings private apartments.

rooms.Name: Ornate Landing
rooms.Description:
Although richly decorated, the landing feels very private, you 
imagine that the king does not receive visitors here in his private 
apartments, but elsewhere.  There is a set of doors to the north, or 
you can return to the great hall downstairs and leave the king's family 
in peace.

Exits.Description: A set of double doors lead north, both doors have a small silver star upon them.
You see the staircase leading down.

rooms.Name: Dressing Room
rooms.Description:
This is where the queen prepares herself for her public appearances. 
Wardrobes line the walls, filled with formal gowns, and there are rows 
of drawers filled with jewelry and other accessories.

Exits.Description: An archway leads into the king and queens' bedroom.

rooms.Name: Bedroom
rooms.Description:
This is everything you would expect from the bedroom of a king, and 
more besides.  The room is dominated by a huge four-poster bed made from 
some dark wood and polished to a deep glow.  All the furniture is made 
in the same style decorated with gold and fanciful paintings of strange 
beasts.  Even the most simple and functional item is made to look like a 
work of art.  You feel sure you will never see such luxury again.

Exits.Description: There is a small door leading east.
A pair of double doors lead south.
An archway leads west into the queens dressing room.

rooms.Name: Nursery
rooms.Description:
This room is home to the heirs to the kingdom of Delray.  The King 
and Queen were blessed with twin boys, their tiny cots sit one on either 
side of this room.  Beautifully crafted toys, made of wood and precious 
metals can be found all over the place.  The tragedy of the saving of 
the city is that since the population hasn't aged since, the young 
princes will be babies forever.

Exits.Description: A small door leads west.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
They look like the kind of toys that young boys would like, miniature 
halfling soldiers and orcs, finely crafted and painted.  The orcs look a 
bit chewed, clearly the young princes have mastered the art of war.

rooms.Name: Council Chamber
rooms.Description:
This is where the king consults with his advisors on matters of 
national security.  Since the nation has been secure for four-hundred 
years, this room is not used very often.  A round table in the centre of 
the room is surrounded by five  chairs.  The table is inlaid with the 
symbol of Delray.  On one wall is a large map, which shows the kingdom 
of Delray in its full glory.  You recognise enough to realise that 
Delray was once a very large kingdom.  Small markers on the map seem to 
represent military units - blue ones representing the halfling forces 
surrounded by a sea of red invaders from the Moria mountains.

Exits.Description: A small door leads south.

rooms.Name: East-end of the Great Hall
rooms.Description:
This is the true centre to the lost kingdom of Delray.  A huge golden 
throne stands upon a dais at the east end of the Hall.  The high vaulted 
ceiling shimmers with bright light from an unknown source, the gods 
painted upon it smile approvingly down at the throne.  A smaller throne 
also stands on the dais - clearly meant for the queen - and a third 
ornate chair sits near the bottom of the steps where the kings first 
advisor traditionally sits.

Exits.Description: A small door, inlaid with the national symbol, leads north.
The throne truly is magnificent.
The Great Hall continues west.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The throne is made from wood and covered entirely in gold leaf.  The top 
of the throne is crafted such that a silver five-pointed star set with 
sapphires floats above the head of someone sitting upon it.

rooms.Name: Ruined Hall
rooms.Description:
This rooms appears to be some kind of audience chamber, though not 
used for quite some time.  Silt fills the corners of the room and there 
is lots of rubble from the collapse of the corridor.

Exits.Description:
The southern end of the hall is filled with  rubble from the collapsed 
corridor.

rooms.Name: North-South Passage
rooms.Description:
The passage seems dim after the brightness of the intersection, but 
it is lit with the same strange lanterns as the entrance hallway. Some 
of the niches contain small idols and statues which appear to be images 
of the heros of Delray.

Exits.Description: You see an intersection to the north.
You see an intersection to the south.

rooms.Name: Guard Room
rooms.Description:
This room is where the palace guards rest off duty.  There are racks 
of weapons along  the  wall and several breastplates left on a bench. 
Although the palace guards are generally only for display, rather than 
war, the weapons look razor sharp and the guards look like they know how
to use them.

Exits.Description: The Great Hall lies to the north.

rooms.Name: Deep Cavern
rooms.Description:
You are in a massive underground chamber far below the palace.  This 
chamber must have been broken open when the city was sunk beneath the 
waves.  Seaweed clings to the walls, fish large and small swim in and 
out of the gloom.

Exits.Description: The cavern continues east.
The cavern continues south.
There is an opening behind the seaweed above your head.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: As you brush the seaweed you notice a hole behind it.

rooms.Name: Deep Cavern
rooms.Description:
You are in a massive underground chamber far below the palace.  This 
chamber must have been broken open when the city was sunk beneath the 
waves.  Seaweed clings to the walls, fish large and small swim in and 
out of the gloom.

Exits.Description: The cavern continues to the south.
The cavern continues to the west.
There is an opening behind the seaweed above your head.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: As you brush the seaweed you notice a hole behind it.

rooms.Name: Deep Cavern
rooms.Description:
You are in a massive underground chamber far below the palace.  This 
chamber must have been broken open when the city was sunk beneath the 
waves.  Seaweed clings to the walls, fish large and small swim in and 
out of the gloom.

Exits.Description: The cavern continues to the north.
The cavern continues to the west.
There is a cave below you.

rooms.Name: Deep Cavern
rooms.Description:
You are in a massive underground chamber far below the palace.  This 
chamber must have been broken open when the city was sunk beneath the 
waves.  Seaweed clings to the walls, fish large and small swim in and 
out of the gloom.

Exits.Description: The cavern continues to the north.
The cavern continues to the east.
There appears to be a hole behind the seaweed to the west.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: As you brush the seaweed you notice a hole behind it.

rooms.Name: Twisting Passage
rooms.Description:
The corridor winds downwards and to the south and the water is 
becoming a little cloudy.  Small statuettes rest in niches along the 
passage walls, but they become more sinister in appearance as you 
progress.  The walls are covered with a think layer of weed, and sand 
swirls around your feet as you walk.

Exits.Description: The passage becomes narrower to the south.
You see an intersection to the west.

rooms.Name: Intersection in the Palace
rooms.Description:
You stand at an intersection in the palace.  A passage leads north 
and south and another leads east and west. To the west the passage seems 
very gloomy, while the eastern passages quickly twists out of view.

Exits.Description: A dim passage leads north.
A hallway leads east.
A dim passage leads south.
A hallway leads west.

rooms.Name: Collapsed Corridor
rooms.Description:
The reason for the gloom soon becomes obvious, just after the 
corridor turns to the north it has collapsed, blocking the way 
completely.  This appears to have happened quite some time ago -  
seaweed and coral have grown over the rubble that blocks the way.

Exits.Description: The corridor has collapsed to the north, rubble blocking the way.
You see an intersection to the east.

rooms.Name: Malaig's secret store
rooms.Description:
This is where Malaig keeps his private things, tomes of lore and 
magical objects adorn the room.  The room seems disorganised, but then 
no-one ever enters save Malaig himself.  There are prototypes here also 
for several conjured creatures, fully functional and looking very 
fierce, despite being only a couple of inches high - they jabber and nip 
at your feet, but are unable to hurt you.

Exits.Description: The rear of the fireplace lies to the east.

rooms.Name: Malaig's Chambers
rooms.Description:
This is the room of the Kings first advisor, and saviour of the city, 
the magician Malaig.  When the hobgoblin and kobold hordes overran the 
outlying regions of the kingdom  Malaig coordinated all the magical 
defences, but to no avail. Fierce creatures were created to hunt kobolds 
and hobgoblins, but the sheer numbers drove the halflings back to the 
city gates of Delray.  Malaig's last gamble was to move the entire city 
to where it could not be reached - beneath the ocean.  There is a large 
desk on one side of the room and a rug covered in mystical symbols lies 
on the floor. A fire burns in the fireplace and there is also what 
appears to be a steel locker against the south wall.

Exits.Description: A wooden door leads east.
There appears to be a steel locker against the south wall

A fire burns in the fireplace, despite the fact that you are hundreds of 
feet  below the  ocean.  You can place your hands right into the flames, 
but they give no heat - they must only be an illusion.

This rug must have been  specially made,  Malaig must use it for some of 
his conjurations.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: There is a tiny name tag on it. It says 'D.Jones'.

This rug must have been  specially made,  Malaig must use it for some of 
his conjurations.  There looks to be a trapdoor beneath it.

A fire burns in the fireplace, despite the fact that you are hundreds of 
feet  below the  ocean.  You can place your hands right into the flames, 
but they give no heat - they must only be an illusion.  There is a 
square hole at the back of the fireplace, perhaps it is a keyhole?

rooms.Name: Narrow Hallway
rooms.Description:
The hallway gets darker and narrower the further you go.  It ends 
abruptly at a wooden door that has mystical symbols carved into it.

Exits.Description: A twisting passage lies to the north.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
There is a humanoid face carved in the door, it looks very realistic, 
its eyes almost glow with power.  All kinds of mystical symbols are 
carved around it, their exact meaning is unknown, but you recognise that 
they are used as wards...to keep out demons.

rooms.Name: Lair of the Wyrm
rooms.Description:
This is the home of one of Malaigs creations.  The Kingdoms finest 
magician expended great energy creating monsters to destroy the 
invaders, and only one of these monsters survived the invasion and the 
saving of the city.  Now it lives beneath the palace - keeping the lower 
caverns free from intruders.

Exits.Description: The huge cavern is above you.

rooms.Name: Davey Jones' Locker
rooms.Description:
The door closes behind you and spikes pierce you from all directions. 
You're dead!

rooms.Name: Gaol Entrance
rooms.Description:
This is the entrance to Malaig's private gaol, where prisoners of war 
are held for Malaig to experiment upon them.  The single cell lies to 
the east, and wooden steps lead back up to Malaig's chamber.

Exits.Description:
The cell look quite spacious as you peer through the bars, though hardly 
comfortable,  especially  with the  prospect of  becoming one of Malaig's 
experimental subjects.
Wooden steps lead upward to Malaig's room.

rooms.Name: Western end of cell
rooms.Description:
The cell is almost bare, save a couple of wooden framed beds, and 
some threadbare blankets.

Exits.Description: The cell extends further to the east.
The gaolers room lies to the west.

rooms.Name: Eastern end of cell
rooms.Description:
A couple more beds fill this end of the cell together with a few  
pieces of battered armor.

Exits.Description: The cell extends further to the west.

rooms.Name: Main Street
rooms.Description:
This wide and busy avenue runs north from the Palace of Delray, to 
Jubilee Square. The familiar bustle of everyday city life is all around 
you. People walking up and down, greeting each other in a cheerful 
fashion, and generally going about their business. They do not seem to 
have even noticed that they are underwater, and that the cracks in the 
paving stones are filled with coral, and that limpets and anenomes 
cover the walls of the buildings. You almost stand on a flatfish, which 
skitters out of the sand at your feet, and heads off down an alley. 
How strange!

Exits.Description: Main Street continues north.

You see the front of the Palace of Delray, home of the king and his 
advisor, Malaig.

rooms.Name: The Temple of Hrorn
rooms.Description:
This is the only temple in Delray - its inhabitants are not exactly 
big on religion, however they are all devout believers in Hrorn the 
Trickster. It is said that if anything can go wrong it will, and if 
nothing can go wrong, then Hrorn will make it. In short they see the 
funny side of everything, and then get on with life, probably for this 
reason noone seems to mind that a family of terrapins is living in the 
altar, and that a huge barnacle has attached itself to the statue of 
Hrorn in a rather amusing place.

Exits.Description: Steps lead down to the east and out of the temple.
Steps lead down to the east and out of the temple.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The huge statue of Hrorn towers above you, the expression on its 
divine face can only be described as amused. A massive barnacle has 
attached itself to the face of the statue such that is resembles a large 
wart on the face of a witch. Undoubtedly Hrorn sees the funny side.

A small family of terrapins has hade it their home, and they happily swim 
in and out of the small recess in the back.

rooms.Name: Before the Temple of Hrorn
rooms.Description:
You stand just to the east of a marvelous temple, contructed from 
blue flecked marble and raised up on a small hill where it gazes out 
over the city. You can climb the steps up to the west and enter the 
temple, or you can make your way back to Main Street.

Exits.Description: Main street lies to the east.
You see steps leading up to a magnificent temple.
You see steps leading up to a magnificent temple.

rooms.Name: Main Street
rooms.Description:
You have arrived a junction in Main Street. To the west you can make 
out the shape of a large temple, with shoals of fish idly circling the 
marble columns. Main Street leads south towards an impressive looking 
palace. To the north the street opens out into a large square, while 
to the east is a dark narrow alleyway.

Exits.Description: You can see Jubilee Square to the north.
A dark alley leads east.
Main Street continues south towards the palace.
You see a stylish temple in the distance.

rooms.Name: Dark Alley
rooms.Description:
You pick your way carefully down a narrow alleyway, cluttered with 
junk and debris. Crates and boxes have been stacked haphazardly, and 
been subsequently covered with a layer of sediment. A quick search 
reveals that the boxes contain building materials, and tools, and a 
whole family of seahorses who are less than impressed by your intrusion.

Exits.Description: The alley continues east.
You see Main Street to the west.

rooms.Name: Dark Alley
rooms.Description:
There are more abandoned crates here, although someone has made
an attempt to clear a way through to the building to the south. From 
the sounds you can hear, you assume that it is an Inn. The alley 
continues east, but you can see that it does not continue very far.
To the west you can make out the bustle of Main Street.

Exits.Description: Looks like it might be a dead end.
You hear sounds of merriment.
A dark alley leads west.

rooms.Name: Scruffy Inn
rooms.Description:
Your not quite sure if this Inn is for real, or perhaps a parody of 
dockside Inns you have known. The wooden floor is covered with a layer 
of sandy silt, and the bar is decorated with all kinds of seafarers 
memorabilia - bits of rope, various anchors and several lobster pots.

Exits.Description: You see a dark alley.

rooms.Name: The End of the Alley
rooms.Description:
The alley comes to an abrupt end at a high stone wall. There is more 
junk piled up against the wall, which you assume encloses the city, but 
it is not piled high enough for you to climb over the wall. The ground 
under your feet is covered with a layer of sandy silt, though you 
notice a grate outlined by the sand.

Exits.Description: A narrow alley leads west.
It looks like the entrance to a sewer.

rooms.Name: Entrance to the Sewer
rooms.Description:
You've crawled through lots of sewers on your adventures, and this 
must be one of the cleanest you've ever seen. No bad smells, no 
festering rubbish, in fact it seems to be a haven to many shy creatures 
who have made it their home. The sewer continues east, or you can climb 
out of the grate above you to street level.

Exits.Description: You can see that the sewer leads east.
You can see the end of an alley.

rooms.Name: End of the Sewer
rooms.Description:
The sewer ends here, presumably you are just beyond the walls of the 
city. From here the sewer drains down a narrow grating into what appears 
to be a system of narrow caves. The grate sparkles with magic, and as 
you get closer a face appears above it, and stares right at you.

Exits.Description: The sewer continues east.
A narrow grate leads down into the darkness.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The face that appears above the grate is that of a halfling. He looks 
incredibly wise and powerful. He turns towards you and begins to speak.

#yThe Magical Warning Beacon says, 'Danger! Do not proceed! This point#N
#ymarks the boundary of effect of Malaig's barrier around the city.#N
#yOnce past this point you will need to protect yourself from the sea#N
#yby your own means.'#N

rooms.Name: Cramped Tunnel
rooms.Description:
There is barely enough room to turn around in this narrow tunnel, 
clearly noone ever comes down here to clean it out. Thick dark weeds 
grow around the inside of the tunnel, long fronds reaching out to 
entangle your weapons and limbs. You could climb up to the safety of 
the old sewer, or with a little effort you can continue along the 
tunnel, which leads east.

Exits.Description: The cramped tunnel continues east.
The safety of the sewer is above you.

rooms.Name: Cramped Tunnel
rooms.Description:
You are forced to continue on your hands and knees, pressing onwards 
through the thick seaweed that grows here in profusion. You can't see 
very far ahead, but by the feel of the currents swirling around you, 
you conclude that the tunnel heads downwards from here or to the west.

Exits.Description: The cramped tunnel continues west.
You sense from the currents here that you can continue downwards.

rooms.Name: Murky Tunnel
rooms.Description:
You fight your way through the seaweed, which claws at your limbs and 
possessions. The water here is murky, and coupled with the dense seaweed 
this makes it impossible to see what lies ahead. You can just make 
out that the tunnel continues west, although the flow of water in this 
area is upwards.

Exits.Description: You can't see a thing through the dense seaweed.
You can't see a thing through the dense seaweed.

rooms.Name: Twisting Tunnel
rooms.Description:
Feeling your way through the thick, clinging seaweed, you manage to 
figure out that the tunnel leads south from here, and also east. The 
fronds and tendrils twist themselves around your hands and feet, you'll 
have to disentangle them before you can continue.

Exits.Description: You can't see a thing through the dense seaweed.
You can't see a thing through the dense seaweed.

rooms.Name: Twisting Tunnel
rooms.Description:
You continue along the narrow twisting tunnel on your hands and 
knees. Surely it must get wider soon? The seaweed lashes at you 
furiously and the water is clouded by some inky black substance, 
making it difficult to see further ahead. You eventually decide that 
the tunnel heads east and north from here.

Exits.Description: You can't make anything out through the flailing seaweed.
You can't make anything out through the flailing seaweed.

rooms.Name: Twisting Tunnel
rooms.Description:
The inky blackness grows darker here, and to the east. Strong 
currents swirl around you, making it difficult to continue. The 
twisting and turning tunnel leads east and west from here.

Exits.Description: You can't make anything out through the murky water.
You can't make anything out through the murky water.

There appears to be some kind of secret entrance concealed 
behind the seaweed.

rooms.Name: Underwater Cave
rooms.Description:
The tunnel suddenly widens out into a large cave, lined with 
colourful seaweeds and corals, and crowded with thousands of tiny 
fish. The brightly patterned fish seems to flash as your light 
touches them through the gloom. At the far end of the cave is a 
recess from which the inky blackness emanates. There is only one
exit - back the way you came.

Exits.Description: A narrow twisting tunnel leads west.

rooms.Name: Basement
rooms.Description:
You find yourself in what appears to be a large cellar. Boxes and 
crates were once carefully stacked around the walls, although they have 
become rotten, and many have broken open, damaged by the salty seawater. 
The floor also looks very unsafe here, but the cellar extends further 
to the east and looks a little safer there. A trapdoor lined with 
seaweed lies in the centre of the cellar.

Exits.Description: The cellar extends further to the east.

A trapdoor covered in a thick layer of seaweed leads downwards into 
the darkness.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Looks like this place was used for storage. There are casks of lamp oil 
and boxes of building materials, and stoneworking tools. Nothing useful 
though unfortunately.

rooms.Name: East End of the Basement
rooms.Description:
The eddy currents caused by your movement swirl the silt all around 
you, making it difficult to see very far. There are more broken crates 
at this end of the cellar, but again they don't hold anything usable. 
You can make out some stairs leading upwards and a door to the north.

Exits.Description: A small wooden door bars the way north.
The cellar extends further to the west.
A set of rickety wooden steps lead upwards.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Its a strange little door, with a wide slot at the bottom. A sliding 
section indicates that the bottom section of the door once slid open, 
but it appears now to be sealed.

rooms.Name: A Small Room
rooms.Description:
There is barely room to stand in this tiny room, which was clearly 
used at some time to store coal. Your movement stirs up a thick cloud of 
coal dust, making it impossible to see around the room. By feeling your 
way you discover a trapdoor in the ceiling, where the coal was once 
loaded, but it is impossible to open it.

Exits.Description: A narrow dorrway lies to the south.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Its firmly wedged shut from the outside.

rooms.Name: Outside
rooms.Description:
You stand on the seabed, next to a stone structure, which stretches 
upwards and out of sight in the murky water. Broken wooden supports 
slick out of the seabed all around you, as if this area were once 
enclosed by wooden walls. Swirling clouds of sandy silt obscure your 
view, but feeling around you discover that you are surrounded on all 
sides by coral-encrusted rocky outcrops. Some steps lead downwards into 
a gloomy looking cellar, and the tower to the west looks interesting.

Exits.Description:
You see a tower stretching upwards beyond your sight, there is a door 
in the base of the tower.
Steps lead down into the darkness.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It seems to be in very good condition, although thousands of small 
sea creatures, and wildly coloured varieties of plant life have made 
the coarse dark stone their home. From what you can see, the tower 
is round, and very tall. There is a door in the base inlaid with 
writing.

An inscription on a bronze plaque on the door tells you that this is 
the last great work of the halfling architect Tepan. Unfortunately the 
cost of making the signal tower escalated enormously during 
construction and Tepan was bankrupt long before its completion. It 
therefore became known as Tepan's Folly.

rooms.Name: Inside Tepan's Folly
rooms.Description:
The inside of the tower is smaller that you might have thought from 
the outside, clearly the walls are very thick. A rotten wooden door lies 
to the north, and a thin iron spiral staircase winds around the wall and 
up to the next level. There is a ventilation grating about halfway up 
the wall, but it appears dark.

Exits.Description: There is a door to the north, on the door is written 'Wardroom'.
You can just make out a set of stairs outside the Folly.
A thin iron staircase spirals upwards.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The grating is blocked by silt and sand and you are unable to see 
anything through it. Perhaps you are still below the level of the sea 
floor?

rooms.Name: Ward Room
rooms.Description:
This is where the keepers of Tepan's Folly rested while off duty. The 
Folly was manned constantly during the war with the kobolds and orcs, 
in order to give advance warning of any attacks. You see a few scattered 
pieces of broken armour on the floor, but nothing useful. There is a 
large chest on the far side of the room.

Exits.Description: You can see the ground floor of Tepan's Folly.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It looks like it was used for storing signalling torches, but it is 
empty now.

rooms.Name: Climbing the Stairway
rooms.Description:
Flakes of rust fall from the iron stairway as you climb, giving the 
water around your feet an orange hue. Narrow windows give a view to the 
outside, but theres not much to see - the water is still too murky for 
you to see very far.

Exits.Description: The stairs continue upwards.
The stairs continue downwards.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The water outside is still very cloudy, you think that you are not very 
much higher than the level of the natural sea floor.

rooms.Name: Climbing the Stairway
rooms.Description:
The water is clearer here, giving you a great view out of the narrow 
window slits of The Folly. Looking down you can see the water becomes 
clouded with sandy silt, above you the water becomes ever clearer, and 
you can make out a brief flash of sunlight.

Exits.Description: The iron stairway continues upwards.
The iron stairway leads downwards.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The water is clear enough for you to see as far as the city walls, 
which are just below the level of the window slit. Over the walls you 
can just make out a large temple in the distance, and a large open 
square full of hurrying people.

rooms.Name: Climbing the Stairway
rooms.Description:
You are now quite a distance up the Folly, and the narrow iron
staircase stretches a long way down, and much further up too. The 
water here is a lovely clear blue and you can see for miles through 
the narrow windows. Hundreds of tiny fish flit excitedly around you 
and the walls are covered with beautiful multicoloured corals.

Exits.Description: The iron stairway continues upwards.
The iron stairway continues downwards.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
You can see the whole City of Delray stretched out before you 
like a relief map. The people hurrying through the streets and 
squares are as small as ants, and even the palace looks like a 
carefully crafted model.

rooms.Name: Top of The Folly
rooms.Description:
The top of Tepan's Folly is actually above sea level! Waves crash 
against the windows, but they are well constructed, and have survived 
the centuries intact.The centre of the room is dominated by a large 
altar, once used for lighting signal fires during the war. A narrow 
ladder leads up to a small trapdoor in the ceiling.

Exits.Description: A narrow ladder leads upwards.
The iron stairway leads downwards.

rooms.Name: The Roof of The Folly
rooms.Description:
You are instantly stung by spray from the ocean, but stout railings 
make it easy to keep your footing. Your first instinct is to climb down 
the ladder and back inside, but it might be possible to swim back to 
the mainland from here.

Exits.Description: A narrow ladder leads down.

rooms.Name: South-West Corner of Jubilee Square
rooms.Description:
You stand at the southwest corner of a large bustling square. All 
around you the citizens of Delray go about their daily business, 
apparently unaware of the fact that the city is several hundred feet 
below the ocean. Coral grows haphazardly over the buildings and long 
fronds of seaweed grow from between the paving slabs on the ground.

Exits.Description: Jubilee square extends further to the north.
Jubilee square extends further to the east.
A wide street leads south towards the palace.

rooms.Name: South-East Corner of Jubilee Square
rooms.Description:
Sand swirls around your feet as you walk around the square. Just to 
the east you can see a tiny shop, although it appears to be selling 
mainly junk. The square extends further to the north, and in the 
distance you think you can make you some kind of monument.

Exits.Description: Jubilee square extends further to the north.
You see a little junk shop to the east.
Jubilee square extends further to the west.

rooms.Name: Jakat's Junk Shop
rooms.Description:
You stop short upon entering the Jakat's Junk Shop. There is no room 
for you to move at all, the piles of collected bric-a-brac slope 
outwards from all four corners, threatening to bury you. Glancing around 
you notice a halfling, apparently trapped in the heap of assorted junk. 
On closer inspection however you realise that this is the proprietor, 
wonder if he has anything worth buying?

Exits.Description: You can go outside to Jubilee Square.

rooms.Name: End of Kingdom Road
rooms.Description:
Kingdom Road ends rather surprisingly at a vertical cliff. You 
imagine that before the sinking it was a busy highway, encouraging trade 
with distant Stanneg in the mountains. Strong currents swirl around 
you, making it difficult to keep your footing. You have no option but 
to return along Kingdom Road to the centre of Delray.

Exits.Description: A wide paved road heads east.

rooms.Name: Kingdom Road
rooms.Description:
The Kingdom Road leads west from Jubilee Square towards Draconia and
the mining town of Stanneg in the Mountains. Of course its not been used
since Delray was sunk beneath the ocean, but it might be worth 
investigating where it leads. You are not along on the Kingdom Road - a 
swirl of colorful fish dance around your head, and silky seaweeds 
entangle themselves about your legs.

Exits.Description: You see a large open square to the east.
Kingdom Road continues west.

rooms.Name: North-West Corner of Jubilee Square
rooms.Description:
Two wide paved roads leave the square from the northwest corner, one 
leading north and the other making its way west. In the heyday of the 
Kingdom of Delray, these roads lead to other great trading nations, the 
mining town of Stanneg in the mountains, and Rome and Tynstri in the 
north. Noone appears to walk these roads now, seaweeds have grown up 
between the huge paving slabs and hundreds of tiny fish flit about.

Exits.Description: The North Road leads, well, north.
Jubilee Square extends further to the east.
Jubilee Square extends further to the south.
The Kingdom Road leads west.

rooms.Name: North-East Corner of Jubilee Square
rooms.Description:
The north side of Jubilee square is slightly less busy than the 
south. A few citizens wander around with barely a glance at the strange 
sights that make you stare in amazement. Your attention is immediately 
drawn to a large monument just to the north, although the gates just 
visible to the east might also be worth investigating.

Exits.Description: You can see a large statue just to the north.
A wide street heads east.
Jubilee Square extends further to the south.
Jubilee Square extends further to the west.

rooms.Name: Jubilee Street
rooms.Description:
Large sprawling single storey hobbit homes lie both to the north and 
south. The little doorways look very secure - it seems likely that 
waking up with a family of crabs in your bed, or a shark in your privvy 
is not even slightly amusing. It seems unlikely that any of the 
inhabitants will allow you into their homes, hobbits are very private 
folk. A strip of sandy earth down the centre of the street is filled 
with growing fronds of seaweed and decorative outcrops of coral. Jubilee 
Street opens onto a large square to the west, and continues east.

Exits.Description: You can see a hobbit home sprawling out to the north.
Jubilee Street continues east.
You can see a hobbit home sprawling out to the south.
Jubilee Square lies to the west.

rooms.Name: Jubilee Street
rooms.Description:
Jubilee Street passes between large sprawling single storey hobbit 
habitations to the north and south. Hobbits are notoriously private 
creatures, so it seems unlikely you will find any of these homes 
unlocked. A wide strip of earth down the centre of the street contains 
tall seaweed and narrow fluted spires of pink and red coral. Thousands 
of tiny fish flit about the seaweed, making the whole centre of the 
street seem alive.

Exits.Description: You can see a hobbit home sprawling out to the north.
Jubilee Street continues east.
Jubilee Street continues west.
You can see a hobbit home sprawling out to the south.

rooms.Name: Jubilee Gates
rooms.Description:
Jubilee Street ends before a pair of tall silvery gates. Someone has
attached a large sign to the gates, which might be worth reading. 
Peering through the narrow bars of the gate you see that the water 
shimmers strangely as if the ocean currents cannot pass beyond the gate.

Exits.Description: A tall pair of silvery gates stand to the east.
Jubilee Street leads west.

rooms.Name: Coral Trail
rooms.Description:
Pillars and outcrops of delicate coral stand all around you forming 
an impassable barrier to the south and east. The walls and gates of 
Delray just to the west are covered by the fine pinkish corals, 
although there seems to be a route through to the north.

Exits.Description: A narrow trail leads through the delicate coral.
A tall pair of silvery gates stand to the west.

rooms.Name: Coral Trail
rooms.Description:
Pillars and outcrops of delicate coral stand all around you forming 
an impassable barrier to the south and east. The walls and gates of 
Delray just to the west are covered by the fine pinkish corals, 
although there seems to be a route through to the east and south.

Exits.Description: A narrow trail leads through the delicate coral.
A narrow trail leads through the delicate coral.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The coral really is quite beautiful, shimmering in a thousand colours, 
and teeming with life. Little polyps feed if the drifting plankton, 
and fish of all sizes feed off the crustaceans and each other!

rooms.Name: Coral Trail
rooms.Description:
Tall delicate spirals, and broad outcrops of pink and white coral 
glitter all around you. The swirling sand, and the bright fish 
flitting this way and that obscure your view, although you can see 
a trail through the coral spires to the east and west.

Exits.Description: A narrow trail winds through the coral.
A narrow trail winds through the coral.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The coral really is quite beautiful, shimmering in a thousand colours, 
and teeming with life. Little polyps feed if the drifting plankton, 
and fish of all sizes feed off the crustaceans and each other!

rooms.Name: Before The Folly
rooms.Description:
The pathway through the coral comes to a dead end. The living 
barriers to the north and south butt up against a huge tower, which 
stretches up towards the ocean surface. You wouldn't want to damage 
the coral by clambering all over it, so there is no way you can 
continue. There appears to be a tiny window in the tower, just 
above the level of the sandy sea bottom.

Exits.Description: There is a clear pathway through the coral leading west.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
You swish the sand away from the tiny window with one hand, nearly 
choking as it swirls up about your face. When it finally clears you 
peer through the window and into the tower. It appears to be mostly 
empty, with a few items of damaged armour left strewn about. A rusted 
iron stairway winds it's way up the centre of the tower until it 
disappears from sight. Staring down the tower you think you can make 
out a tiny wooden door far below.

Despite searching all around, you are unable to find any sign of a way 
in. You can't seem to figure out where the entrance could be.

rooms.Name: North Road
rooms.Description:
A wide paved road leads north out of the city of Delray. Also called 
the Marching Road, this was the main route by which Delray's legions 
went to war against the Morian hordes. You think you can make out a tall 
gate to the north, while to the south the road opens into a wide square.
Fronds of seaweed try and wrap themselves around your legs.

Exits.Description: The Marching Road leads north.
The road opens into a wide square.

rooms.Name: Victory Monument
rooms.Description:
This towering statue commemorates a great victory for the Kingdom 
forces, over the evil hoardes of orcs and kobolds from the Moria 
mountains. It consists of a proud halfling soldier, wounded and in 
battered armour, standing over the corpses of several mean looking 
orcs. The base of the statue is decorated with hundreds of silvery
symbols of the city of Delray.

Exits.Description: Jubilee Square lies just to the south.

Carefully examining the base of the statue, you notice a tiny release 
lever concealed near the corner.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The base bears many six-pointed stars of silver - the symbol of the
City and Kingdom of Delray. A tiny trapdoor set in the base leads 
into a crawlspace beneath the monument.

rooms.Name: Crawlspace
rooms.Description:
This tiny recess beneath the statue is a hiding place for local 
priests in the event that Delray is invaded. It is no surprise to you 
that if a halfling has to crawl in here, you are forced to wriggle on 
your belly like a snake. You hope that you can turn around though, 
otherwise you might become stuck in here forever.

Exits.Description: You can crawl upwards out of this tiny hole.

rooms.Name: North Arch
rooms.Description:
The North Road passes beneath a huge arch, blocked by a pair of tall 
bronze studded gates. Looking above the arch the water shimmers 
strangely, as if the ocean currents cannot pass over the barrier. 
Hoards of tiny fiddler crabs scuttle in and out of small holes in the 
city wall where they have made their homes. If you can't get past the 
gate, then the only way to go is south.

Exits.Description: The gates just won't budge!
The wide North Road leads south.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
No matter how hard you push, there is no way to shift the massive gates. 
Their centuries under the sea have not weakened them in the slightest - 
they must be magically sealed.

rooms.Name: Slag tunnel
rooms.Description:
It is dark. Warm slag from the purging station comes continuously in
from the south. A little hole in the bottom of the tunnel leads down to
something, further down. Maybe it is worth a following... maybe not.

Exits.Description: The purging station.
Darkness.

rooms.Description: takes ...

rooms.Name: A little grassy clearing
rooms.Description:
The path comes in from the west and ends rather abruptly at a huge
and presumably very very deep hole in the ground. The edge of the hole
has been reinforced on one side so that you can approach without risking
a fall into it, at least not due to bad construction.

Exits.Description: A small path leads off.

Down a deep, deep hole.
- Going there is possible but just do not expect to get back up.
   At least, not this way.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The hole is 10 yards in diameter and quite smooth, at least as far
down as you can see. The sheer presence is a question in itself, and what
is it used for? There definitely is some kind of use for it as there
is a path up here. A small ladder goes down opposite the reinforced
edge.

The ladder is broken about a yard down. That means that there is or
was something down there. If you wait for it to be fixed you could find
a whole new world for you to explore. Or, you can try to use your well-
trained body and try to climb down the rather rugged surface of the hole.
Should not be too big of a problem for you.

rooms.Name: Lesser used path of giants
rooms.Description:
The caravan way of giants leads in a south-east direction even if its
travellers are somewhat less frequent than on the way in between the
high storages.

Exits.Description: The path ends in a small grassy field.
The small path continues.

rooms.Name: Lesser used path of giants
rooms.Description:
The caravan way of giants leads in a south-north direction even if
its travellers are somewhat less frequent than on the way in between the
high storages. A smaller trail leads off the path north towards
something else.

Exits.Description: The small path continues.
The path continues.

rooms.Name: Chute V
rooms.Description: DO not let any guard WALK out...

rooms.Name: Rest and Dressing room
rooms.Description:
Warm and friendly air seems to emanate both from north and south.
Right here, wooden panels cover the walls and warm marble covers the
floor. How they manage to keep the marble warm is a mystery to you, but
why complain and to whom? Some well-polished wooden benches stretch out
along the wall and there even are some hooks here for you to hang your
clothes. Behind the northern wooden door you hear laughter and random
splashes while from the south, soft dance music pours out and fills your
ears. There is a small sign hanging next to the stairway entrance to
this room.

Exits.Description: Steam slips out from under the door to the Sauna and Jacuzzis.
A constant flickering of light comes out from the lowered dance floor.
The stairs lead up to the VIP Lounge.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Your hostess Gretchen, invites YOU all to the Mill VIP club.
   Here there are no restrictions in age, gender or preferences.

                        WELCOME  and  ENJOY !!!

If you place your ear to the floor you can hear a weak sound
resembling flowing water. The heat must originate from some hot
springs or maybe someone has taken the effort to lead warm water through
the floor just to heat it up. Anything to make you feel good.

rooms.Name: Sauna and Jacuzzi
rooms.Description:
The heat and humidity is enormously high and the difference from the
Rest and Dressing room is extreme. This is where the VIPs of the mill
get started for their big parties. The evenings amusement take on new and
intriguing forms every time. Sometimes local employees and specially
invited guests join the event. This might become a new experience for
some, ancient history for others, but everyone seems to be happy.

Exits.Description: You can see the dressing room through the mist.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
You read #<OE>LYT on a sign, which could be the brand name. Beware! It
is very hot and would surely burn a crude tattoo into your skin if you
happened to sit down on it.

rooms.Name: Dance floor
rooms.Description:
The dance floor is one of the smallest ones you have ever seen. It is
even smaller than the one at Granite Head's Bakery and he does not even
admit to having one. A crystal sphere rotates on its hanger in the
ceiling and some coloured lanterns have their flow of light directed
directly towards it, giving multicoloured reflections all over the room.
The few people here look up at you as the newbie you are, but they smile
invitingly towards you and bid you out on the small dancefloor. It
is always nice with a new face.

Exits.Description: The dressing room reveals itself through the dim lighting.

rooms.Name: Hotter than Hot!!!
rooms.Description:
One really should stop to think before one dives into a pool of smelt.
This time you only DIED!
It could have been worse.
You could have ended up eternally imprisoned in a metal block.
Or perhaps as a lethal part in a slaying weapon.
Not a nice future.
Consider yourself LUCKY!

Exits.Description: Someone put the plug in. You can not get out. What a pity.
To Late!

rooms.Name: Road heading towards the Iron Mill
rooms.Description:
The road surrounded by bushes turns west-north here allowing you to
either reach some large greyish buildings to the north or some more road
to the west. The buildings seem to let go of some smoke, smoke of the
same colour as the landscape around you.

Exits.Description:
You see a large sign in the distance. It has to be large, as you would
not see it this far away otherwise.
A bushed road leads away.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Dirty does not really bear good comparison with the real situation
here.
Just by barely touching a leaf or almost anything you get dirty and this
include trying to brush it away, as it only spreads it out more.

Dust and Dirt. The environmental issue does not seem to exist.
Perhaps that is the price for progress, perhaps not.

rooms.Name: At a large Sign
rooms.Description:
The road continues south toward the southern outskirts of the mill and
splits up west and east, heading for the large complex of very dirty
buildings in your view to the north. A large sign next to the road shows
that if you go in that direction you will end up being treated rather
hostile by the owners. They do not like trespassers. So you would better
stroll some other way or be prepared to encounter trouble.

Exits.Description: Further in between the mill buildings
The road goes on towards somewhere else.
Some big building towers up towards the dirty sky.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Dwarven Kingdom Iron Mill  a joint venture with
              Glob Inc. Development Group.


    Trespassers will be punished in the most severe manner.
            Minimum Removal Distance - Two Yards.

rooms.Name: In between buildings
rooms.Description:
One large grey building ends and another one begins. This has to be
the height of dwarven architecture. Add a little fog (smog) and your
sense of direction would go haywire. A little sign next to the western
door is still visible. Nothing seems to have stopped you so far so why
wait.

Exits.Description: In front of yet another large grey building.
Inside yet another large grey building.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The very dirty sign reads:

                    Prep Facility
           Preparation room and Mixing station


                 Do not feed the giants.
              (Unless you are supposed to)
There seems to be a shortage of that.   Hehe.    Sorry.

rooms.Name: In front of a large grey building
rooms.Description:
A little east-west path goes next to the wall of a huge grey
building. From its enormous chimney a thin chain comes down. Wonder what
they mean by 'For emergency use only - Unauthorized use will be punished
by DEATH!' as the sign next to it reads. These people really mean
business. The chain is climbable, at least upwards, but it looks a bit
unstable. And what was that thing about unauthorized use?

Exits.Description: A front a very huge door.
More grey buildings.
You can climb but it will not be popular.

rooms.Name: At a HUGE gate
rooms.Description:
You stand at the huge gate in an even larger building. The gate is so
large they had to split it up into two parts. A stream of air penetrates
the gate from the inside. It is warm and a bit dirty. A small sign with
a lot of writing on it is placed on the gate. You had better read it. If
you decide to not to enter the gate the yard stretches out in just about
any direction.

Exits.Description: It is warmer inside the building.
The huge gate continues.
You see the back side of a large sign along the path from the mill.
A grey building...

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
'GO AWAY!'
   'RAUS!'
   'STICK DIN FULA KOSSA!'
   'SKRID!'
   'VAI passear camelo'
... and a lot other more or less rude 'go away expressions'.

rooms.Name: At a HUGE gate
rooms.Description:
You stand at the huge gate in an even larger building. The gate is so
large they had to split it up into two parts. A stream of air penetrates
the gate from the inside. It is warm and a bit dirty. A small sign with
a lot of writing on is placed on the gate. You had better read it. If
you decide to not to enter the gate the yard stretches out in just
about every direction.

Exits.Description: It is warmer inside the building.
The large grey building ends.
You see the backside of a large sign along the path from the mill.
The huge gate continues.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
'GO AWAY!'
   'RAUS!'
   'STICK DIN FULA KOSSA!'
   'SKRID!'
   'VAI passear camelo'
... and a lot other more or less rude 'go away expressions'.

rooms.Name: End of a huge building
rooms.Description:
Heaps of ashes and stone can be seen in abundance. The drawbacks of
development can be duly noted in the large amounts of trash and waste
that have been dumped here without any discrimination or regard for the
mountainside vegetation. A good suggestion would be to head west.

Exits.Description: A huge gate.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Stone that had its ore extracted is just waste. Apparently this is the
place where the dwarfs dump it, awaiting something better to do with it.

rooms.Name: South wall inside the extraction house
rooms.Description:
A variety of craftsman tools hangs on the walls as well as lie in
well-organised piles neatly stuffed away in the correct small toolboxes.
The temperature seems to increase in the northwards direction.

Exits.Description: A schlurping sound can be heard, but you can not see anything special.
A less organised corner.
The draft from the outside can be clearly noted in the aerosol flow.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Tools, tools, everywhere tools. Everything you, or anyone else would
ever need in order to run an iron mill staffed mainly by dwarfs is here
or out in the mill somewhere, but has its box here. Needless to say,
quite a lot of ladders have their places here.

rooms.Name: Inside the Main Extraction building
rooms.Description:
A huge hall stretches out in all directions but south, where the
large gate leads out into the fresher air. In the northern part of the
building a yellow-reddish glow can be seen at floor-level. The glow
appears to originate from the large chimney that goes from floor to roof
in the western part of the building and it ends abruptly in the
north-eastern corner of the building.

Exits.Description: A glow warms your face.
Outside, it is a bit colder but just as dirty.
Also inside the huge gate.

rooms.Name: Inside the Main Extraction building
rooms.Description:
A huge hall stretches out in all directions but south, where the large
gate leads out into the fresher air. In the northern part of the
building a yellow-reddish glow can be seen at floor-level. It appears to
originate from the large chimney that goes from floor to roof in the
western part of the building and ends abruptly in the north-eastern
corner.

Exits.Description: A glow warms your face.
Inside the huge gate.
Outside, it is a bit colder but just as dirty.

rooms.Name: Inside the Main Extraction building
rooms.Description:
West, you see a large platform above head-level from where you can
detect a faint swooshing sound. At ground level you can also walk
around the cigar-shaped chimney. The chimney seems to be very hot and
you hesitate to move in any closer, even though it should not be
dangerous. But you can always wimp out back east toward the gate.

Exits.Description: A faint glow warms your bared skin.
Next to a huge gate.
Next to the furnace.

rooms.Name: Next to the blast furnace
rooms.Description:
You stand under a small platform next to the blast furnace. A small
ladder lets you climb up to the platform. It is rather hot and
you wonder what makes the worker endure this environment. If it wasn't
for the high noise level and all the dirt the climate would be really
nice (if it wasn't for the dwarfs who keep on complaining about you
getting in the way all the time - Perhaps a large heap of sand and a few
big umbrella drinks would do the trick).

Exits.Description: The smelt outlet.
The draft from the outside can be clearly noted in the aerosol flow.
The southwest corner.
The platform.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
FIRE!!!
You see nothing but the scorching white heat of molten metal. Wonder how
they muster up that kind of temperature.

A metal grid allows you to walk around on a higher level of the
building.

Made up of bricks, its cigar shape surely has some process importance,
but you are not an extractive metallurgist. Then you would know. There
are some small windows one could look through to see the inside of the
furnace.

The ladder is very narrow - or maybe standard size for a midg..
                                                                dwarf.

rooms.Name: Southwest corner of the main extraction building
rooms.Description:
You stand under a small platform next to the blast furnace. It is
rather hot here and as everywhere else, a bit dirty too. A swooshing
sound can be heard intermittently from above the metal grid platform
above your head. There seems to something going on there.

Exits.Description: A corner.
A little ladder leads up to the platform.

rooms.Name: Northwest corner of the main extraction building
rooms.Description:
You stand under a small platform next to the blast furnace. It is
rather hot here but you ignore that as you see a very odd construct
placed on a rail here. The thing is apparently not in use right now but
the rail goes eastward if you want to activate it.

Exits.Description: The smelt outlet.
The south-western corner of the extraction building.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The complexity of the thingies indicates gnome workmanship, but
surprisingly it DOES seem to be working. The dwarfs would not have it
any other way so some bright dwarf must have had her hand into this
before it was taken on-line in the mill.

rooms.Name: Smelt outlet
rooms.Description:
Here the furnace is 'bled' of the molten metal. It plunges out of a
small hole in the furnace and splashes into a stream going eastward. A
small rail starting right under the hole goes out in an arch towards the
west.

Exits.Description: The smelt flows away.
A little ladder goes up the furnace.
Follow the rail to the solution.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The plug fits perfectly in the furnace hole. The mill staff uses it to
halt the flow of metal once in a while or as there is a need for it.
It leads west of here. Wonder what the use of it is.

Ooohh, so very hot. Melting metal in that inferno must be child's
play. But you DO wonder how they do it.  The flowing smelt is sooo sexy -
You stay and admire it for a while.  Why did you not learn about this in
school?
 Sigh.

rooms.Name: Next to the smelt flow
rooms.Description:
A small channel in the floor conducts the smelt in an eastward
direction. The smelt seems to be covered with some slag that surely
would ruin the fine iron if left on and in the metal. You can
follow the flow east-west or you can head towards the south and the exit
out of the building.

Exits.Description: There is some kind of blocker in the smelt flow.
You can see the dirt in the air whirl at the huge gate.
The smelt outlet!

rooms.Name: Slag Scraper
rooms.Description:
Here the slag is scraped off from the smelt coming from the west. All
of the slag it seems, by some large doctors blade. Some small amount of
pure metal is scraped of too, but that is just to be on the safe side.
The off-scraped is turned into a small channel leading primarily north.
The rest of the now clean smelt continues east.

Exits.Description: The slag channel leads away the slag.
The metal flows on.
The metal comes flowing.

rooms.Name: Slag Channel
rooms.Description:
The slag comes in from the scrapes in the south and slowly follows
the channel here to where it plunges down into some black hole in the
floor.

Exits.Description: More slag comes from the scraper.
The slag tank accepts all kind of trash and will keep it safe.

rooms.Name: Slag Tank
rooms.Description:
Its warm, DARK, without exit and there is absolutely no magic in this
place. What did you think of when you jumped into this place. You had
better stay and contemplate your situation for a while before you start
whining about rescue. Perhaps some study of the slag heaps down here
is something to do while being stuck.

Exits.Description:
It is far away and more hot slag keeps on coming, effectively
hindering you from going up again. Your only chance is to pray to the
gods that be to take you home again.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Slag is no good. Well perhaps maybe as roadfill. Well maybe it is
good. Slagbuilders are added to the furnace setup to create a slag with
wanted, specific properties. But what is slag then, you ask yourself as
you sit there having a real dull time? Slag is a complex gathering of
mostly oxides that bond the real unwanted stuff in the smelt to itself in
a way that makes it, at least somewhat, easily removable before the smelt
reaches the foundry. Neat, is it not?

rooms.Name: Next to the smelt flow
rooms.Description:
A small channel in the floor conducts the smelt in an eastward
direction. The smelt is free from any kind of impurities and is now
ready to continue to alloying and final treatment. The big building you
are in also stretches out southwards.

Exits.Description: The lighting change at the huge gate.

rooms.Name: Scrap corner
rooms.Description:
Broken tools, empty barrels and a lot more are scattered around in
this place. It seems that the things have been here for years but the
dirt in the mill easily covers up any proof of that. As the building
expands to the north and west the scrap density clearly decreases.

Exits.Description: The world seems more organised.
The world seems more organised.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Tools, tools, everywhere tools. All and everything you, or someone
else, would ever need in order to run a iron mill populated mainly of
dwarves is here or is out in the mill somewhere but have their boxes
here. Needless to say quite a lot of ladders have their place here.
Unfortunately these items and boxes no longer seem to be used. They
almost look abandoned.

rooms.Name: The smeltpath plunges down
rooms.Description:
The smelt falls down through a hole on the channel to some sublevel
part of the plant. The sound of it splashing into the collector below is
fascinating. The intriguing sound fights the urge to explore further but
you loosen yourself from its grip and start to search for some stairs to
descend, which is not easy as the building expands into all directions.

Exits.Description: The smelt comes running.

Schluurrrrp!!!
The darkness gleams, but there is no way down for you here.

rooms.Name: East of the plunging path
rooms.Description:
The temperature is a bit lower here compared with next to the westly
smelt but the dirt is still here. A small spiral staircase is north of
you.

Exits.Description: A small flight of stairs comes up from below.
A lot of junk is piled up here for you to sort out.
The smelt flow ends and a schlurping sound can be heard.

rooms.Name: North of the plunging path
rooms.Description:
The temperature is a bit lower here compared with next to the southern
smelt but the dirt is still here. A small spiral staircase is east of
you.

Exits.Description: A small windle of stairs comes up from below.
The smelt flow ends and a schlurping sound can be heard.

rooms.Name: Windle of stairs
rooms.Description:
Stairs go down to the foundry on the floor below this level of the
iron mill. Steam and smoke come blowing up through the metal grid steps.
The humidity down there must be enormous. Perhaps you should stay up
here and troop off south or west into the big building.

Exits.Description:
The air coming from below is warm and humid. Perhaps they have a sauna
down there.

rooms.Name: Up on a shelf - SouthEast corner.
rooms.Description:
You can see through the metal grid making up the floor you stand on.
The view over the mill inside is rather disappointing. The place has
not been cleaned for ages it seems, but on the other hand you should not
be in here in the first place, so who should you complain to? Some kind
of air pumping device is here awaiting to be served.

Exits.Description: More grid.
More grid.
A tiny winy ladder leads down.

rooms.Name: Up on a shelf - SouthWest corner.
rooms.Description:
You can see through the metal grid, making up the floor you stand on.
The view over the mill inside is rather disappointing. The place has
not been cleaned for ages it seems, but on the other hand you should not
be in here in the first place, so who should you complain to? Some kind
of air pumping device is here awaiting to be served.

Exits.Description: More grid.
More grid.

rooms.Name: Up on a shelf - NorthWest corner.
rooms.Description:
You can see through the metal grid, making up the floor you stand on.
The view over the mill inside is rather disappointing. The place has
not been cleaned for ages it seems, but on the other hand you should not
be in here in the first place, so who should you complain to? Some kind
of air pumping device is here awaiting to be served.

Exits.Description: More grid.
More grid.

rooms.Name: Up on a shelf - NorthEast corner.
rooms.Description:
