evidence of the family's wealth.  The banquet rooms are just east of
here.  The children are to the west, and the entrance room with the
family's shrine is south.

Exits.Description: A large elegant room may be seen through a partially open door.
A large open room lies south of here.
Sounds of children playing come from the room just west of here.

rooms.Name: Banquets
rooms.Description:
This is the northern section of a huge area used for entertaining
important guests.  Large platters of food are kept here and circulated
by slaves among the guests.  The room is beautifully furnished with
expensive tables and chairs.  It continues to the south, and there is a
door to the west.

Exits.Description:
The southern half of the room holds three large dining couches and some
low tables.
A small arch-shaped door leads west.

rooms.Name: Banquet Couches
rooms.Description:
Three lovely aqua couches sit at right angles to each other, forming
a U shape around a low square table.  Each couch holds 3 diners, and
slaves circulate to serve such delicacies as flamingo tongues and sow's
udders.  You will frequently see a bard or jugglers here, providing
entertainment for the guests.

Exits.Description: The large banquet room extends northward.

A wide archway shows you the apartment's entrance area and family
shrine.

rooms.Name: Atrium
rooms.Description:
Murals of country life and bountiful harvests adorn the walls of
this atrium.  Hanging brass oil lamps provide soft lighting during the
evening and at night.  One corner holds the family shrine, dedicated to
the household gods that guard the family's prosperity.

Exits.Description: Through a wide archway you can see living quarters for the family.
Looks (and smells) like a banquet.  The family must be entertaining.

Stairs provide access to the ground floor and the upper level
apartments.

rooms.Name: Small Apartment
rooms.Description:
The entrance room of this tiny apartment is predictably small, but
predictably has a small shrine in one corner devoted to the household's
gods.  The bare wood walls of the apartment provide little protection
against the heat of summer or the cold of winter.  The flat's little
bedroom is east of here.

Exits.Description: The small bedroom is just through a louvered door.
A small wooden door leads to the outside world.

rooms.Name: Small Apartment
rooms.Description:
The entire family sleeps in this tiny room on straw pallets on the
floor.  There is a small wooden cabinet in one corner used to hold
their few belongings.  There is a small balcony out the door to the
east, and the atrium lies west.

Exits.Description: A large wooden shutter closes off the balcony.
A louvered door separates the atrium from the sleeping quarters.

rooms.Name: Balcony of a Small Apartment
rooms.Description:
From here you have an excellent view of via Vestia and the huge
basilica just to the west.  The husband in this small family works in
the courts as a bailiff, keeping the courtrooms peaceful despite some
heated battles.

rooms.Name: Balcony of a Small Apartment
rooms.Description:
Tunics, loincloths and other, less identifiable pieces of clothing
have been set out to dry in the sun on this balcony.  You may wish to
stop to admire the view.  From here you can spot the east gate of Rome
and the clay road stretching east.
   #GA stack of laundry sits waiting to be hung out to dry.#N

Exits.Description: The main room (the only room) of this small poor apartment lies west.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Sitting in a large straw basket, you can make out a large jumble of
loincloths, tunics and other, less-identifiable pieces of cloth.  They
are all damp, and waiting to be hung out on the balcony to dry in the
hot sunshine.

rooms.Name: Small Apartment
rooms.Description:
The successful tutor who lives here recently bought his freedom.  A
Greek who teaches diction to the sons of the mighty, he now lives in
this tiny one room apartment over some shops in eastern Rome.  His
balcony lies to the east, the apartment entrance is west.

Exits.Description: A small balcony is just to the east.

The apartment door is usually kept locked against thieves, of whom
there are many.

rooms.Name: Apartment Stairs
rooms.Description:
The stone staircase ends here at two plain wooden doors, each with
doorknob and keyhole.  There are two large potted palms here, and a
small pot with a fern struggling to survive in the hot climate.  The
doors are framed with thick wood, and there is a feeling of poverty
about the landing.  One of the doors has a rather thick lintel over it.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Over the top of the doorway, where you can barely see, there seems to be
something hidden, something that glitters.

rooms.Name: via Phobia
rooms.Description:
via Phobia continues here in its straight path from Forum to Gate,
past some lovely public gardens.  They look green and cool in the
summer heat, and a bright sunny spot in the winter cold.  The entrance
to the gardens is north.  Just to the south is a small dirty shop
selling captives from foreign lands.

Exits.Description: Green plants and tall palms beckon to you.
A dusty archway leads into a small shop.

rooms.Name: via Phobia
rooms.Description:
A well-paved well-swept and well-trodden east-west street intersects
here with a quieter, shadier one that leads north past the public
gardens.  Off to the east you can see the forum, to the west lies the
impressive west gate of Rome, and to the north at some distance lies an
enormous building that you recognize as the racetrack.

rooms.Name: via Phobia
rooms.Description:
Strange sounds and smells emanate from the little store north of
here.  The store is unmarked, and fairly dark.  From the lovely mosaics
decorating the door, however, you can tell that the owner is quite
wealthy.  What manner of business could lead to such wealth?  via Phobia
continues in its straight course east and west.

Exits.Description: It's too dark to see anything, really.
A busy intersection near a park ...

You can see the western gate of the city to the west, down this very
straight street.

rooms.Name: Augurer
rooms.Description:
You have entered a small office lined with scrolls, many in strange
languages, many quite ancient.  Some you see locked away in a cabinet,
marked "Sibyl".  Others you may examine.  This is the home of one of
the 16 prophets of Rome, a very powerful group of men and not ones to
offend!  They are the augurs.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The augurs examined the sky for flocks of birds, cloud shapes,
lightning and other natural events, omens to tell them the future.

Sibyl was a prophetess who lived in caves in Cumae in early republican
times.

rooms.Name: Gladiator Training
rooms.Description:
A very wealthy, very successful gladiator, Mattias has retired from
the arena and opened a school to train men to follow in his footsteps.
His large oak desk sits in a corner.  From the thick dust on it you can
tell he is not often there.  The eastern wall displays a wild assortment
of weapons and various trophies, including his wooden sword and crown
won at great cost in the arena.  Training grounds lie north of here, and
the busy street is back south.

Exits.Description:
The training area begins through the doorway to the north.  You are
welcome to observe, but if you want lessons you will have to pay!
via Phobia is right outside the door.

rooms.Name: Healer
rooms.Description:
Although his apprentices assure you he has had much training and
experience as a physician in Rome's glorious battles, nevertheless you
eye the many instruments laid out on the table with fear.  A corner
cabinet is filled with scrolls, and the sweet scent of herbs floats in
through the window.

Exits.Description:
If you decide to remain ill rather than trust your luck with the
physician, the exit to the street is just south of here.

rooms.Name: Gladiator Training
rooms.Description:
An assortment of weapons lines one wall of this huge area devoted to
training new gladiators.  You are in a large walled yard, not unlike
the gladiators' arena.  Looking at the weapons and tiny shields, you
wonder if you would survive even the training.

Exits.Description: The training yard stretches off to the west.

rooms.Name: Gladiator Training
rooms.Description:
The sand shifts softly beneath your feet, and you avert your eyes
from the darker, slightly sticky patches where trainees have learned a
valuable lesson.  You hope your lesson will be less bloody.  The huge
training arena continues east and west, and the entrance to Mattias'
office is south.

rooms.Name: Gladiator Training
rooms.Description:
The training arena is surrounded by a high white wall.  With the
wall to your back, the arena seems to stretch endlessly westward,
filled with desperate men with nothing to lose except their lives.
Great riches and glory may be found in the Colosseum, although the cost
may be quite high.

Exits.Description: The arena continues west.

rooms.Name: via Phobia
rooms.Description:
Just north of here lies a famous school for training gladiators.
Becoming a gladiator is a great opportunity for some, and for some
there is no choice.  via Phobia continues both east and west from here.

Exits.Description: Loud clangs and grunts are heard from the open doorway north of here.
Far off in the distance you can spot the Forum.
The west gate of Rome is quite close.

rooms.Name: West Gate of Rome
rooms.Description:
The west gate of Rome has been securely locked.  Through the widely
spaced iron bars of the gate you can see the river Tiber flowing
freely.

Exits.Description:
The corner shop of this apartment / shop building looks busy, with 
gladiators and others coming and going in large numbers.
via Phobia runs east and west throughout the heart of the city.

The gate is kept securely locked to prevent undesirables from entering
the city.

rooms.Name: via Ravena
rooms.Description:
via Ravena runs north and south, intersecting with via Phobia by the
gardens and via Aggripina to the north.  Just east are some public
gardens which are lovely and soothing to walk through.

Exits.Description: The public gardens offer a peaceful place to rest and relax.
via Ravena intersects with busy via Phobia just south of here.

rooms.Name: via Ravena
rooms.Description:
Just east of here you may walk through lovely green gardens, planted
by some benevolent (and ambitious) Roman to show his wealth and his
devotion to the welfare of Rome.  To the north, you will walk by the
west end of a very large building which, from the smell, is probably a
racetrack.

rooms.Name: via Agrippina
rooms.Description:
This short street lies between the high northern wall of the city
and the even higher northern wall of Circus Maximus, the city's
racetrack.  Both walls are covered with graffiti, most of which is
devoted to the two racing teams, the Leeks and the Venetians.

Exits.Description:
Horses and chariots are entering a large archway in the wall just east
of here.

rooms.Name: Outside the West Gate
rooms.Description:
The river Tiber flows swiftly just west of you, and to the east you
can look through the gates of the western entrance of Rome at the many
splendors of this large city.  A large tunnel is fairly dry at the
moment, but from the odor emanating from it, you know its usual burden
is sewage.

Exits.Description:
Through the iron bars of the gate, the entrancing city of Rome beckons
to you.  Hope you found the key.

rooms.Name: Public Bathrooms
rooms.Description:
Public toilets smell much the same all over the world.  You eye
the sponge-on-a-stick with distaste, and think about the clean sweet
smell of the countryside outside of Rome.  The loud clatter of the
street is north of here.

Exits.Description: Through the open door you can see the street.

A large grate covers the service entrance to the sewers.  Only slaves
need go down there.  The smell is enough to kill.

rooms.Name: Public Gardens
rooms.Description:
You wander through lush green bushes, under tall palm trees that
thrive in this warm climate.  The gardens are a wonderful place to
rest, relax and think.

Exits.Description: Shaded pathways lead to other parts of the gardens.

When you have finished your lunch (or your rest), you may wish to
wander Rome's busy streets.

When you have finished your lunch (or your rest), you may wish to
wander Rome's busy streets.

rooms.Name: Public Gardens
rooms.Description:
Beautiful gardens thrive in the warm climate of Rome.  They are
carefully tended by slaves of the citizen who had gave them to the
city.  Plants are brought in from far distant provinces to add their
beauty and scent to please the Romans.  The gardens continue south of
here, and the quiet street via Ravena is just to the west.

rooms.Name: Praetor Petyus Enormous Gilded Box at the Racetrack
rooms.Description:
The Praetor, with some generous "donations" from the Maximus family,
oversaw the building of the enormously popular Circus Maximus racetrack.
There is always a party in his box, although many of the guests are
citizens eager to curry favor, laughing at his jokes.

Exits.Description: Some of the Praetor's best friends are sitting in the seats east.
The Praetor's area continues south.

rooms.Name: Mob Chute #1
rooms.Description:
This is mob chute #1 and will only be seen by mobs and imms ... flagged
for no_teleport.  This is also the holding pen for slaves sold by
Maximus Maximus.  The slave shop MUST be numbered 1 LESS than this room.
The slaves MUST be marked SENTINEL.

Exits.Description: via Vestia
via phobia by Jupiter
Baths
Clay road east
Circus
Colosseum

rooms.Name: Slave Shop
rooms.Description:
This dusty little room off the via Phobia is where captives from
Rome's glorious wars are sold.  If you need someone to comb your hair
for you, teach your children, build your home or simply be your
companion and give his life for you, Maximus Maximus will be happy to
fill your requirements from his frequently replenished stock.  If you
have wandered in here by mistake, the street is straight out the door to
the north.
#GA large sign has been hung on the wall in front of your eyes.#N

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The sign reads:

  Use 'List' to see the available slaves.
  To buy yourself a slave, use:
      'Buy <slave>'  or 'Buy <slave> <name>'

  Instructions for having slaves:

   You can order your slave with 
                  'order <slave> <instructions>' 
   If you have several slaves you may use 
                  'order followers <instructions>'
   If you abuse your slave, it will no longer regard you as its master.
 
  
 Regards,

 Maximus Maximus

rooms.Name: Cold Storage for Slaves
rooms.Description:
This is the holding pen for slaves sold by Maximus Maximus.  The
slave shop MUST be numbered 1 LESS than this room.  The slaves MUST be
marked SENTINEL.

rooms.Name: Priest Chute #2 (Temples)

Exits.Description: Mars
Venus
Jupiter
Mercury
Vulcan
Bacchus

rooms.Name: Mob Chute #3
rooms.Description:
This is mob chute #3 and will only be seen by mobs and imms ... flagged
for no_teleport.

Exits.Description: Baths - Entrance
Theater - good seats
Circus
Colosseum
Streets West
Streets East

rooms.Name: Start of the sandy track
rooms.Description:
You find yourself on a sandy track that leads east to what seems to be a 
small town. You hear little noise except for some soft melodic music and you
feel quite at peace in this tranquil place.  A large temple lies just
south of here.

Exits.Description: The trail continues in that direction.

rooms.Name: The sandy track
rooms.Description:
The track becomes harder here and the sand thins out. The walking is
easier on this harder ground and you start to look forward to what may
be ahead. The sound of wildlife and the song of the birds adds to your
mood.

Exits.Description: The trail continues.
You see the start of the sandy track.

rooms.Name: The stone path
rooms.Description:
Now the track is paved and is shaded by large ornamental hedges on
either side. The hedges are beautifully trimmed and it is evident that a
lot of care and attention has gone into the landscaping. You realize that
the people inhabiting the town must be very meticulous and proud.

Exits.Description: The entrance to the town.
The sandy track.

rooms.Name: Entrance to Old Japan
rooms.Description:
You find yourself in a large open area. All around you there are neatly
manicured plants and flowers. The smell is enchanting and your spirits
are lifted. You decide that it was a good idea that you decided to venture
so far from home after all. As you take in the astounding beauty a large
banner that seems to be made from paper rustles in the wind and raises your
interest.

Exits.Description: The stone path.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The banner reads:

         Welcome to the palace of the Emperor Nazaki.
         All are welcome to explore the grounds and
         to pay homage to the great Emperor himself,
         who extends his hospitality to you. Please
         visit the monks in the shrine and they will
         help you find enlightenment and peace within
         yourself.

rooms.Name: South-west corner of the square
rooms.Description:
You are standing along the border of the square. The exquisitely tended
hedges reach up far above your head and you wonder how they are kept in
such a good condition, surely they are too high to be reached. The square
continues to the east and to the north you can see the entrance to the town.

Exits.Description: The entrance to the town.
Southern side of the square.

rooms.Name: Southern side of the square
rooms.Description:
You are at the southern-most side of the town square. From here you can
see the whole square and the view is magnificent. To the west and east are
the corners of the square and in the distance to the north you spy a small
trail leading away from the square. One thing strikes you as a little odd,
the hedge here seems slightly discolored and a little more tatty than the
other parts are. Also to the north it looks as though something has been
demolished.

Exits.Description: Center of the square.
South-east corner of the square.
You can just see through the discolored hedge.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: You try to push the hedge and you find that it gives a little.

rooms.Name: The small, dusty trail
rooms.Description:
You find yourself on a small trail leading southwards. The air is cooler
here and the light seems fainter as if dusk were setting in. You put this
down to the fact that the large hedges are blocking most of the light but
you can't help but feel a little disconcerted. All around you insects are
buzzing and humming and this eerie melody only darkens your mood. To the
south the trail continues, but for some reason you can't really see where
it is going.

Exits.Description: The discolored hedge is to the north
The trail darkens

rooms.Name: South-east corner of the square
rooms.Description:
The whole of the square looks beautiful. All the flowers are in full
bloom and bees hum quietly around looking for pollen. To the north you can
see the bordering hedges and to the west you can nearly make out the trail
which you followed here.

rooms.Name: Eastern side of the square
rooms.Description:
You are standing at the side of the square directly opposite from where
you entered. You can see the center of the square to the west and to the
east there is a wide bordered path which leads up to a large building. The
building appears to be a kind of temple, most probably the residence of the
Emperor, you think to yourself.

Exits.Description: The north-eastern corner.
A white path
The south-eastern corner.
The center of the square.

rooms.Name: North-east corner of the square
rooms.Description:
You are standing at the corner of the great square still finding it hard
to believe that such a work of beauty could be accomplished. You ponder over
who actually looks after the garden, and decide that whoever it is must be
endowed with strange and wonderful talents.

rooms.Name: Northern Side of the square
rooms.Description:
You can see the whole square from here and it looks quite beautiful. To
the south you notice that the hedge directly opposite is slightly different
in color to the rest of that side, but you decide it must just be the way
the light reflects off it. To the north there is a gap in the hedge but it
has been filled by a large pile of rubble, which presumably was at one time
an arch of some description. Anyway, it does not look as though you will be
able to climb it.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The rubble looks quite fresh, as though whatever it was has only been 
   destroyed quite recently.

rooms.Name: North-west corner of the square
rooms.Description:
You are in the top corner of the square. It seems to be a little higher
here than at other places and you are able to just peek over the southern
hedge. What you see is quite an awesome sight, a volcanic mountain shrouded
in mist climbs up into the heavens. You are not able to make out much detail
due to the thick mountain mists, but it quite a wondrous sight. From here
the square extends to the east and south.

Exits.Description: You see the square

rooms.Name: The center of the square
rooms.Description:
Here at the center of the square you can take in all the beauty of your
surroundings. The mystical music you heard earlier can be heard more strongly
now, but its source is indiscernible. From here you can see the white path
leading east from the square and the temple behind that. To the west you
recognize the path you entered on, and to the south you notice that the hedge
is a slightly different color to the rest of the border.

rooms.Name: The rice path
rooms.Description:
You are standing on a white path that seems to be made from rice. It makes
a strange crunching noise as you walk on it and you wonder what the purpose
of it is. To the east you see that the path continues on to a large temple.

rooms.Name: On the rice path
rooms.Description:
You follow the white path quite enjoying the funny sound you are making.
To the north you see there is a small enclave and also an identical looking
one to the south. It appears that they house flowers and some ornamental
statues.

rooms.Name: A small enclave
rooms.Description:
You are stood in a small enclave that appears to be a flower garden of
some kind. The flowers are beautifully arranged and the smell is intoxicating.
To the south, past the path, you see a similar enclave.

rooms.Name: A small enclave
rooms.Description:
You are standing in a small enclave that appears to be a flower garden of
some kind. The flowers are beautifully arranged and the smell is intoxicating.
To the north you see a similar enclave past the white path.

rooms.Name: In front of the temple
rooms.Description:
You are stood in front of a grand temple. The architecture is stunning
and you are truly awed by the sight. It is quite intimidating. The steep 
roof reaches down to nearly touch the floor and the light reflects off the 
tiles hurting your eyes. To the east there are some large engraved doors.

rooms.Name: The Emperor's temple
rooms.Description:
You are at the end of the paper screen. You can now see to the east where
a small passage leads to the great long hall of the Emperor. A smell of fine
foods is wafting from the east.

rooms.Name: The temple foyer
rooms.Description:
You find yourself in a large open space. The temple appears to be just
one large room that is separated by paper-like screens. You can see through
the screens slightly as they are quite translucent in the light, but you
can only make out faint outlines. Along the walls hang great tapestries which
depict wars and horrible monsters. The screen prevents your way eastwards
but you can move north or south.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The tapestries depict scenes of battle, mainly between samurai and ninja.
However these are not the only parties involved, spectral images haunt
the backgrounds of the pictures.

rooms.Name: The Emperor's temple
rooms.Description:
To the east you see a small passage. It leads along the outer wall of the
temple and is quite plain. This room is tidy and clean but there is little to
see.

rooms.Name: The dusty trail
rooms.Description:
You are following a dusty trail which is getting steeper as you go. You
hear the sound of people and animals to the south and smoke is rising in a
steady pattern. It appears there may be some sort of settlement ahead. The
trail continues south for a short while and then turns. You can go back to
the square by traveling north.

rooms.Name: On the dusty trail
rooms.Description:
The trail is quite firm and the going easy. The path turns here and now
leads to the east. The sounds of people are getting closer and you hope that
the inhabitants will be friendly. However, the mist that surrounds this place
is less than inviting.

rooms.Name: The path steepens
rooms.Description:
The path you are on begins to rise a little and you can now see a little
way into the distance. The thick mist prevents you from seeing too far but
you are approaching some foothills by the look of things. Further away to
the south you can see the rocky peaks of a small mountain range. The path
continues to the east for a short way, but you can always change your mind
and return to the west.

rooms.Name: A turning in the path
rooms.Description:
You are at a turn in the path. The trail continues to the south where it
rises up into some foothills. The mist seems thicker now and a chill begins
to set in. You are beginning to feel slightly uncomfortable and rub your hands
together to keep warm. The trail is quite steep now, and you can just make out
a few wooden shacks to the south. Back to the west you can make your way to the
square.

rooms.Name: The path to the shacks
rooms.Description:
You are on a path that leads into a small gathering of huts. They appear
quite run down, but inhabited nonetheless as you can see smoke rising from
the small chimneys. All seems quite except for a chattering sound, like a
child's rattle. The path leads south between the shacks.

rooms.Name: Path between the shacks
rooms.Description:
You are on a small dirt path. To the east and west there are small, wooden
shacks. There is little noise from inside and you wonder whether whoever owns
them is hospitable or not. Smoke rises from the small chimneys and you wonder
whether you should take a look inside.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: You see two small wooden shacks standing opposite one another.

rooms.Name: Inside the small shack
rooms.Description:
You are stood inside a small shack. The smell is terrible in here, like food
that has rotted away. There is a small table and a couple of chairs scattered
around the room. The northern wall houses a fireplace and glowing coals try
to add a little warmth to this cold abode. You look around for exits but it
appears that this is the only room. The small futon lying on the floor seems
to confirm this.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
You see a small wooden table. On it lie a few scraps of food which are rotten
and do not look in the slightest bit edible.

The small chairs are in drastic need of repair and it seems they would collapse
if you were to sit on them.

The glowing coals in the fireplace try in vain to give the room a little
warmth.

rooms.Name: A small shack
rooms.Description:
You are standing inside a small shack, which it would appear, houses at
the maximum, only two people. It is tiny and squalid. There is a small table
and a futon lying on the floor, which the owner must use as a bed. You decide
that there is nothing much to see here as the hut is just a single room. The
door you entered by leads back to the path outside.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: The futon appears to be a small bed where the owner(s) of this place sleep.

rooms.Name: Between the shacks
rooms.Description:
To the east and west you see two more shacks. They look very much the same
as the two to the north. They are just as decrepit and smelly. The path leads
north and south or you can hold your nose and enter one of the huts.

rooms.Name: The smelly shack
rooms.Description:
The smell in here is disgusting. You don't know what caused it and you
don't think you really want to. There is no furniture at all in here. All
there is that prevents this hut just being a wooden box is a small fireplace
in the western wall. The door leads back out to the east.

rooms.Name: Another wooden shack
rooms.Description:
This shack is a little larger than the others but it smells just as badly.
The fire has gone out in the fireplace and is very chilly. It makes you
feel like you should have stayed away from this place. The door leads back
out to the path to the west.

rooms.Name: The mountain trail
rooms.Description:
You are on a trail leading up towards a small mountain range. The small
gathering of shacks is to the north, and fortunately the wind has picked up
enough to take the smell of them away. The path turns quite sharply here and
you may continue along it to the west.

rooms.Name: The mountain trail
rooms.Description:
The trail is made from a hard substance that seems quite porous. It is
light-gray in color and crunches a little as you tread on it. Around you
through the mist you once again hear the sound of animals, but they sound
larger than before. You trail gains height and leads to the south once again
but the way back is to the east.

rooms.Name: The fireplace
rooms.Description:
AGGGGGGGGGGGHHHHHHHHHHHH, it's a tight squeeze but you just manage to
crawl into the fireplace. The coals are glowing hot and you have burnt
yourself quite badly. You attempt to pull yourself out and back into the 
room but find yourself completely stuck. The wind starts to get up outside
and suddenly a gust comes down the chimney. The flames start to rise and 
soon catch on to your clothing. You pull harder but just cannot budge yourself
from this mess. Eventually your hair starts to burn and you smell your own
flesh cooking. You die an agonizing and slow death here in a smelly hut!
What a fitting end for a hero such as yourself!

rooms.Name: The steep path
rooms.Description:
This part of the path rises sharply up to what looks like a small plateau.
It looks as though there is some greenery up there but it is difficult to say.
You can hear the sound of running water from far over to the west but there is
no way you can see that far in this fog. If you like you can return towards the
shacks on the path to the north, or if you feel like braving what lies ahead
south is the direction in which to travel.

rooms.Name: The marshy path
rooms.Description:
The path has become quite wet here. You feel yourself sliding in the
mud. It seems there must be water somewhere close by. To the east it seems
that the path rises slightly and hardens up some. To the west it looks
decidedly boggy. The road into the small village leads back to the north.

rooms.Name: A mountain trail
rooms.Description:
The trail is harder again here and it appears to be made of the same
gray rock as you saw earlier. The trail rises slightly and leads to the
east.

rooms.Name: The mountain trail
rooms.Description:
You are on a small track that appears to have been made by animals
although there are larger footprints here. The path is narrow and there
is a relatively large drop to the north of you. The path continues on to
the east.

rooms.Name: A turn in the mountain path
rooms.Description:
You are at the edge of a small precipice. To the north and east there
are sheer cliff faces. A thin crumbling path leads to the south and appears
to end at a rock face.

rooms.Name: A narrow path on the mountain
rooms.Description:
You are on a path approaching a cliff face. It is narrow and you have to
be careful not to fall down the cliff. The view from here is astounding
and you can see for miles even through the mist. The cliff face is along
to the south.

rooms.Name: Outside a small opening
rooms.Description:
You are right up against the cliff face now. It stretches high up
into the sky and you wonder whether there could be a path leading up
there somewhere. To the east you see a narrow gap that you may just be
able to squeeze in to it if you dare. The trail also leads back to the
north.

rooms.Name: The small, dark cave
rooms.Description:
You are stood in a small cave that stinks of putrefaction and death.
All around you are bones and limbs amongst other things. Creatures have
made nests in the remains here and maggots run freely over the floor.
To the south there seems to be a thin crack in the wall and west will
take you back outside.

rooms.Name: The secret store
rooms.Description:
You find yourself in a small alcove that has been hollowed out of the
rear or the cave. There is not much to see as it's a pretty small room.

rooms.Name: The marshy path
rooms.Description:
The path has become decidedly more marshy and less path-like now and
you hope that you will not sink altogether. You can hear the sound of 
running water quite clearly now from the north-west. Exits lead east
and west.

rooms.Name: The sinking path
rooms.Description:
The path has become more of a mire now and to the south you can see
a small expanse of water to the south which seems quite still. It may
be the source of the river you can hear.

rooms.Name: The source
rooms.Description:
You are swimming in ice cold water. There is not much vegetation around
due to the biting coldness, but small reeds and rushes extend from the
surface in places. There is more water to the south and west.

rooms.Name: The source
rooms.Description:
You are swimming in a pool of water that meets the cliff face to the
south, it may be possible to climb out there if you can find any hand-holds.
To the north and west is more water but it seems to be running a little
faster to the west.

rooms.Name: The foot of the mountain
rooms.Description:
There is a steady stream of water running down the mountain here which
gathers in a pool to the north of you. To the south the cliff face stretches
high into the sky and there is no way to climb straight up. You will have to
follow the small path, which appears to have been made by goats, eastwards
if you want to try to climb up.

rooms.Name: A trail up the volcano
rooms.Description:
As you walk along the path you can see through the mist slightly. This is
actually a volcano, not just a mountain after all. The gray rocks you have
seen must be pumice stone. Smoke rises in thin wisps from the peak and you
hope that this particular volcano isn't active. The trail continues on east
from here which appears to be the only way up the mountain from here.

rooms.Name: The source
rooms.Description:
The water here is running much faster and in a northerly direction.
To the south there is a rocky slope leading into the pool. To the north
you see that the pool becomes a small river and flows away down the cliff.

rooms.Name: The source
rooms.Description:
You feel as though you are being pulled along by the flow of the water
and have to swim against it. There are strange noises coming from the
south but you aren't sure if they are caused by the flow of water or not.
There is more water east and south of you and the pool becomes a small
river to the north.

rooms.Name: The small river
rooms.Description:
You are on a small but fast flowing river which is proceeding at a
steady pace down the mountain-side. The current is strong but you are
able to swim against it. It flows northwards into the thick mist and 
you cannot easily tell where it leads to. You can always fight the current
and return southwards if you wish though.

rooms.Name: On the small river
rooms.Description:
The river is much faster here and you can hear a loud crashing sound to
the north. Rocks jut out of the river at curious angles and the sides of
the river are smooth stone, from where the water has grooved it's path. You
can continue north further down the river or you may wish to try to swim
back upstream to the south.

rooms.Name: The small river rapids
rooms.Description:
You are at the terminus of the river. The flow is extremely fast here and
it is difficult to stay afloat. All around you the waves crash and the noise
is deafening. If front of you to the north the river crashes over the edge of
the cliff in an astoundingly beautiful waterfall, the spray from which causes
a rainbow to appear in the haze. You may swim back up the river southwards or
you may dare to risk the hazards of the waterfall.

rooms.Name: The waterfall
rooms.Description:
WHHHHHHHHHHHHOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAAA, what a thrill. You are traveling down
the mountainside at a ridiculous speed and the excitement is immense! However,
there are also HUGE rocks at the bottom of the fall! As you plunge down you
notice them and then they flash by, you missed them! Unfortunately the under-
current is so strong here at the bottom that there is no way you can break
the surface once you have been pulled under. You manage to hold your breath
for a while but then the strain becomes too much and you inhale a lung-full
of water. What they say about drowning isn't right and your death is agonizing!

rooms.Name: The volcanic trail
rooms.Description:
You are following a small gray trail along the mountainside. The trail
is thin and the gusty wind makes this trek quite treacherous. The view is
superb, even through the mist. You can see the Emperor's temple in all its
magnificence and the small shacks you passes over to the north-west. From
here the trail leads southwards into what looks like a lava gully.

rooms.Name: The volcanic trail
rooms.Description:
You are in a small gully carved from the rock by previous flows of lava.
It looks like the going may get tough here as the trail appears to end. You
will have to try to make your way up the mountain without the aid of a path
now. You may wish to turn back and head northwards or risk the climb upward.

rooms.Name: Climbing the volcano
rooms.Description:
You are hanging dangerously on the mountainside. It is difficult going
but you are managing to slowly edge yourself upwards. Eastwards there seems
to be a thin ledge that you may be able to stand on.

rooms.Name: A ledge on the volcano
rooms.Description:
You are teetering precariously on a small ledge hundreds of feet up the
volcano. It leads in a southerly direction towards a large opening in the
rock face. The ledge is very steep and it appears you will have to climb at
least some of the way.

rooms.Name: A ledge on the volcano
rooms.Description:
The ledge is slightly wider now and your footing more secure. Above you
and to the south there seems to be a cave of some sort and the trail leads
you in that direction apparently.

rooms.Name: A ledge on the volcano
rooms.Description:
You are standing on a small ledge far up the mountainside. To the south
you see a large, dark cave while the ledge seems to go east where it meets
a more stable and wider path.

rooms.Name: A cave in the volcano
rooms.Description:
The cave is huge and dark. Shadows flicker and scatter unnervingly from
your light source and you feel ill at ease. It is difficult to tell how
this cave was created as the walls are jagged rather than smooth and there
appears to be no other openings around.

rooms.Name: The ledge widens
rooms.Description:
You are on what seems to be a small platform. The ledge is much wider
here but is seems some subsidence has caused this part to slip and you
will have to climb up to continue your ascent.

rooms.Name: The volcanic trail
rooms.Description:
The ledge now becomes a trail once again. It winds around a jagged
outcrop of rock and it is difficult to tell where it is leading to.

rooms.Name: The winding path on the volcano
rooms.Description:
The path curves around quite sharply and you have to be careful not to
fall off the edge. The path extends a little to the east but does not look
particularly safe there. It may be safer to follow it to the south or even
to return west.

rooms.Name: The path crumbles
rooms.Description:
OOOOOOOOOHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHH NNNNNNNNNNOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO
The path crumbles beneath your feet. You slip and slide down the mountain
side, but are able to eventually grab hold of a tree. But, as luck would
have it, and in the spirit of irony the tree breaks sending you plummeting
to your death hundreds of feet below.

rooms.Name: Outside a cave on the volcano
rooms.Description:
You are on a small path that winds around the volcano. The going is tricky
but you think you are progressing well. To the south is a wide opening that
seems to be a cave, whereas the path continues to the west. North leads back
down the mountain.

rooms.Name: A cave in the volcano
rooms.Description:
You are in a small cave hewn out of the rock by some unexplainable force.
There is very little of interest here and the wind moans across the entrance
making you feel uneasy. You may exit the cave to the north.

rooms.Name: A trail on the volcano
rooms.Description:
The trail is beginning to thin out again and before you know it you are
up against a vertical climb. There is no way around it so you will be forced
to climb up. The way back leads to the east.

rooms.Name: Near the summit of the volcano
rooms.Description:
You are on a small plateau. Looking around you can see for miles. The island
is larger than it appears at first and you can see strange lands far away. The
sea looks rough, but from this height you can get no real impression of the
size of the waves. A few scattered vessels can be seen being tossed around by
the elements and you feel glad to be on land. As you are on a much flatter area
the mist does not obscure your view so badly now and you can see a well used
path winding along to the south.

rooms.Name: On the volcanic plateau
rooms.Description:
Large rocks jut out of the ground all over the place and you have to
follow the trail around these. The going is much easier as you do not have
to fight a slope now and you can see the smoke pouring from the opening at
the top of the volcano. Although it makes you quite uneasy it is a stunning
sight. The trail leads south still where it appears to curve around another
crag.

rooms.Name: The volcanic plateau
rooms.Description:
The trail you are following comes to a sharp turn to the east here. From
there it looks as though it will lead southwards but the outcrops make it
difficult to tell.

rooms.Name: The wide volcanic pathway
rooms.Description:
The trail become much wider here and it looks as if a conscious effort
has been made here to lay a path. It looks as though this part of the mount
is inhabited by someone, or something. This particular path leads south to
a very large opening in the rock face.

rooms.Name: Outside the large cave
rooms.Description:
You are stood in front of an extremely large cave entrance. Above the
cave there appears to be a ledge which you should be able to climb up to.
The entrance to the cave is south or if you wish to explore the ledge you
can climb up to it.

rooms.Name: The great cave in the volcano
rooms.Description:
You are stood inside a huge cave which seems to be a natural crevice in
the mountainside. The walls are covered in arcane signs which have been
painted in blood. Small evil-looking creatures scurry about in the shadows
and a sticky-looking goo drips from the ceiling in places creating a horrible
atmosphere.

rooms.Name: The Lair
rooms.Description:
You are on top of a small outcrop of rock which is covered in grasses
and moss. All around bones and scraps of meat litter the floor. It seems
the be the lair of a group of creatures, but what would be living up here?
You may climb back down to the path if you wish as you can see no other
exits.

rooms.Name: A tunnel inside the volcano
rooms.Description:
You are standing in a tunnel which leads into the actual volcano. The
walls are jagged and coarse and the floor is uneven. You can actually
feel the heat emanating from the walls of the tunnel and you hope that
it won't get much worse as you go onwards. The tunnel continues to the
south but you can reenter the cave to the north.

rooms.Name: The tunnel inside the volcano
rooms.Description:
The tunnel you are in now turns to the east. The heat is getting much
worse the further you go into the volcano and you are beginning to sweat.
Strange noises can be heard from the east but you put this down to the
lava gurgling inside the volcano.

rooms.Name: The tunnel inside the volcano
rooms.Description:
The tunnel now opens out into a large cavern to the south. Back to the
west you can follow the tunnel out of the volcano if you wish.

rooms.Name: The lair of the Dai-Oni
rooms.Description:
This huge cave is decorated with human corpses. They hang from the roof,
the walls and even decorate the floor in places. An enormous throne stands
against the southern wall. It is made from bones and the head-rest from large
skulls. It is covered in human skin, which is beginning to rot creating a
disgusting smell. The tunnel is to the north but that appears to be the only
exit from this vile place.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The throne is huge and made of human bones. The sight of it makes you want
to vomit.

rooms.Name: A passage in the temple
rooms.Description:
You are stood in a small passage. It leads east to what seems like a long
hall. There are some nice smells coming from the eastern direction.

rooms.Name: The long hall
rooms.Description:
You are standing in a long hall that leads northwards. A short way to the
north there is a grand looking throne. The eastern wall is decorated with a 
large assortment of weapons and armor and is quite a stunning sight.

rooms.Name: Before the Emperor's throne
rooms.Description:
In front of you is a beautiful throne made from bamboo and the finest cloth.
It is the throne of the Emperor and is beautiful in design. To the north and
south you can follow the hall and from the west comes the smell of fine food.

rooms.Name: The long hall
rooms.Description:
You are at the northern end of the long hall. To the south you see the 
great throne of the Emperor. The wall to the east is decorated with the
finest weapons and armor. Westwards will take you away from the hall.

rooms.Name: The passage in the temple
rooms.Description:
You are stood in a small passage that leads to the grand hall of the
Emperor Nazaki. From somewhere the smell of fine food assails your nostrils
and you begin to feel a little hungry. East will take you to the grand hall
whilst going west should eventually take you out of the temple.

rooms.Name: The Sushi Bar
rooms.Description:
You are stood inside a small room that appears to be where the Emperor
and his men eat. There is a small serving hatch behind which you can see
a small man scurrying about trying to prepare his food faster. The smell is
incredible and you want to eat right away. When you are finished you can
enter the hall by going east.

rooms.Name: The island coast
rooms.Description:
You are following the coastline of what appears to be a small island.
All around you waves crash into the rocks and the sea breeze whips your
hair about. The you can follow the coastline to the north or south.

rooms.Name: The island coast
rooms.Description:
You are walking along a thin stretch of beach which is shadowed by
large cliffs to the east. There is no way you would be able to climb 
them so it would be best to look for a way through.

rooms.Name: The small cove
rooms.Description:
You find yourself in a small, natural cove. The water laps up the
sandy bank to a small beach which runs along the length of the coastline.
In the distance a huge mountain peak reaches up into the clouds. An 
impressive range of cliffs block your view east, although you can make 
out a small cave at the base of the cliff.

rooms.Name: Smugglers Cave
rooms.Description:
After a short while you become accustomed to the darkness in the 
cave, and take a proper look around. Broken boxes and casks, along with 
various items for the repair of boats are scattered all around this 
area. Judging from the contents of the boxes, you assume that this is 
either the result of smuggling, or of a large scale exploration. Peering
into the darkness at the back of the cave, you notice a narrow tunnel 
heading upwards.

rooms.Name: Winding Tunnel
rooms.Description:
You struggle to clamber over and around the rocks that fill this 
narrow tunnel. The sound of the sea roars in your ears, and the smell 
of salt stings your nostrils, carried by a strong breeze from the cave 
below. The cave disappears in darkness to the east. A deep rumbling 
almost shakes you from your feet, and fragments of igneous rock rain 
down on your head.

rooms.Name: Rocky Shaft
rooms.Description:
The heat and smell of sulphur are very strong at this end of the 
tunnel, which at first sight appears to be a dead end. You soon notice 
however that it is lighter here than elsewhere in the caves, a rocky 
shaft leads straight up from here, and you can see the sky. It's a 
difficult climb, but not for a hardy adventurer like you.

rooms.Name: Chute I
rooms.Description: takes Ma and some janitors to different subareas of the zone.

Exits.Description: games
Entrance
Kitchen
DanceHall
Restaurant

rooms.Name: Chute II
rooms.Description: takes the crows in from above the chimney.

rooms.Name: Chute III
rooms.Description: takes the extra guards into Ma's Office

rooms.Name: Chute IV
rooms.Description: takes in some more querers.

rooms.Name: In Line
rooms.Description:
This is Wrong place to be. Because if you are here then you are not
inside and that's the Right place to be at. It is a bit cold here, could
be, it is much warmer inside. The preferred direction from here is south
towards the entrance but of course you can always wimp out and go north
towards home too.

Exits.Description:
The safety boredom of Stanneg. The Stanneg Inn is visible north of the
main road.
The queue continue south.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
You peek in through a window. You really want to be further ahead in the
line because it looks very comfy in there.

rooms.Name: Outside the Entrance
rooms.Description:
You are standing outside a large but friendly door. You can feel
warmth welcoming you in. So, open the door, go in and shake some. you
will enjoy it. Above your head is a large sign reading 'Ma Glob's
Dancing Parlor'. North of here there usually is a line trying to get in.
West is the door.

Exits.Description:
The door is heavy oaken on very rigid, but it seems its hinges are well
greased because there isn't a sound slipping away as the guards open it.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It has large letters, built up by pulsating colors. Strange magic must
have been used to create that sign. Maybe that tells you something about
the owner.

rooms.Name: Entrance
rooms.Description:
Inside! East is outside. The warmth of the establishment is really
surrounding you. You really do not want to leave again. Let's head west
through the hallway by the bar and seek pleasure at the dance floor. If
you want to you can leave your clothes at the wardrobe north of here. Or
you can just stand here and soak in the atmosphere. South, there is a
ticket office, but you don't really need a ticket.

Exits.Description: A sip of fresh air slips in through the oaken door.

The ticket office does not look very used. But its not empty because the
lights are on in there.
The hallway continues.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: You cant see through the curtain but the light in there is definitely on.

rooms.Name: Wardrobe
rooms.Description:
As any other classy establishment Ma Glob's Dancing Parlor offers you
a safe place for your clothing. A small sign hangs from the roof and
there ought to be some guards here. If there are not they will probably
be here very soon. Robes and furs hang on hooks in abundance, but if you
do not have a ticket, you will not get any of it. There is a guard
quarters west of here and the entrance is southbound.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Please, leave your winter clothing here. It will be guarded. Glob Inc.

rooms.Name: Guard Headquarters
rooms.Description:
This is the room for the local guard force. So you'd better get out
of here before they get angry. The walls are covered with wanted posters
and awards for the outstanding heroism by some of the guards. In the
center stands the Chief of Guards desk covered with papers and forms.
Organization takes its tribute. Only way out (and you'd better take it)
is east into the wardrobe.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The face of a big gruff man looks at you. Hmm, isn't that a member of
your clan. You are absolutely sure you have seen it somewhere else.
There is another notice here too.

Ah. this one you recognize. It is Duwick. The well known criminal and
leader of a gang of bandits living in the Haon-Dor forest.

'For astonishing bravery in the line of duty.'
'Champion of free form wrestling'
'District fencing master'
Looks like Ma Glob has hired competent people for her security.

rooms.Name: Ticket Office
rooms.Description:
The ticket service is long gone. Nowadays people dance with whoever
they like too, whenever they feel like it. The woman in charge of the
ticket sales has almost been bored to death, which is obvious looking
at the pedantically cleaned and organized room. Everything is order,
even the tablecloth fibres.

rooms.Name: Hallway
rooms.Description:
A hallway leads deeper into Ma Glob's Dancing Parlor, or does it? It
sure looks like those you-must-make-a-quick-stop-at-the-bar paths.
Alternatives are few. Either push on towards the west to see if you can
reach the continuing hallway, go east to see if you come back to the
entrance or accept your fate and head south to the bar. It is a nice
looking bar.

Exits.Description: The Bar looks very inviting.
The Hallway goes on and on and on and on and on and....

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Just a little beer wouldn't hurt, would it ?

rooms.Name: East Side of the Bar
rooms.Description:
This sure is a nice bar to hang around in. You feel instinctively
that this is a place you surely could recommend. You can press yourself
west along the bar, head north to the hallway or sneak east to come out
behind the disk south of you. South of you there is a large disk of
black marble covered with filled or partially filled glasses with our
without tiny umbrellas and beyond that a huge mirror and shelves with
any liquor or beverage imaginable.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: It's pink and green and really gets into your eyes. Ouch !

Single slab of marble. It must weigh several tons. But it sure looks
nice in this place. And it's perfectly clean, too.
You see someone really mean in it.

Think of one. Its there !!!
Don't forget to order it too.
[The last message was sponsored by the Dancing Parlor itself]

rooms.Name: Behind the Bar
rooms.Description:
Here you get a nice view of the bar north of you. South you see a
large bar and another nice locale where you could hang around for a
long time. In the center of the view south there is a very dangerous
looking person staring directly at you. Around you on shelves there is
most anything in fluid form you have heard of and most probably a lot
more. Only visible way out of here is east or west into the bar area.

Exits.Description: It sure is an ugly mirror.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The person in the mirror glares back at you, just as hard as you do.
Someone really need to teach that one some manners. Perhaps you should
offer some deconstructive field surgery with your BIG club.

Think of one. Its there !!!
Don't forget to order it too. It is very price worthy.
[This message was sponsored by the Dancing Parlor]

rooms.Name: Center part of the Bar
rooms.Description:
This sure is a nice bar to hang around in. You feel instinctively
that this is a place you surely could recommend. You can press yourself
west or east along the disk. South of you there is a large disk of black
marble covered with filled or partially filled glasses with or without
tiny umbrellas and beyond that a huge mirror and shelves with any liquor
or beverage imaginable. There should be some snacks around here too.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: It's pink and green and really gets into your eyes. Ouch !

Think of one. Its there !!!
Don't forget to order it too. Today, a special offer for YOU !
[This message was sponsored by the Dancing Parlor]
Bartenders only distribute refreshments from behind the bar.

rooms.Name: West Side of the Bar
rooms.Description:
This sure is a nice bar to hang around in. You feel instinctively
that this is a place you surely could recommend. You can press yourself
east along the disk, head north to the hallway or sneak west to come out
behind the disk south of you. South of you there is a large disk of
black marble covered with filled or partially filled glasses with our
without tiny umbrellas and beyond that a huge mirror and shelves with
any liquor or beverage imaginable.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Think of one. Its there !!!
Don't forget to order it too.
Yummie! Yummie! Yummie!
 - Abstainers are no gainers !!!
[This message was sponsored by the Dancing Parlor]
It's pink and green and really gets into your eyes. Ouch !

rooms.Name: Hallway
rooms.Description:
A hallway lead deeper into Ma Glob's Dancing Parlor, or does it? It
sure looks like those you-must-make-a-quick-stop-at-the-bar paths.
Alternatives are few. Either push on towards the west to see if you can
reach the continuing hallway, go east to see if you come back to the
entrance or accept your fate and head south to the bar. It is a nice
looking bar.

Exits.Description: The Hallway goes on and on and on and on and on and....
The Bar looks very inviting.
The Hallway goes on and on and on and on and on and....

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Just a little beer wouldn't hurt, would it ?

rooms.Name: Hallway
rooms.Description:
A hallway lead deeper into Ma Glob's Dancing Parlor, or does it? It
sure looks like those you-must-make-a-quick-stop-at-the-bar paths.
Alternatives are few. Either push on towards the west to see if you can
reach the continuing hallway, go east to see if you come back to the
entrance or accept your fate and head south to the bar. It is a nice
looking bar.

Exits.Description: The Hallway goes on and on and on and on and on and....
The Bar looks very inviting.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Just a little beer wouldn't hurt, would it ?

rooms.Name: Head Waiters Pulpit
rooms.Description:
A large shiny mahogany pulpit dominates the crossing in between the
entrance with its pub, the gaming area up north, the large inviting
dance floor to the west and the most famous part of the Dancing Parlor
(oddly enough) south of here, the not too big restaurant with its
exclusive cuisine.

Exits.Description: A little sign above the north exit reads 'Casino'.
You see a long Hallway.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
A small booklet lays on top of the shiny black mahogany pulpit showing
off who has and who has not got a table reservation this evening. It
looks like you are not on the list. Guess you must be here solely for
the dance.

Table reservations and awaited guests :
King Welmar with escort
Queen Galadriel with guests
Prince Aglandiir
The Gnomish Chieftain with company
Midori and secret guest (private box)
The world team (courtesy of the establishment)

Auntie Tabitha as always

rooms.Name: Restaurant
rooms.Description:
Two small tables stand here with a small white tablecloth covering
them and a silver candelabra in the center of each one. On one of the
tables well folded serviettes lie used on the plates. Apparently the
rude customers have left without dessert or the nice people just took a
turn on the dance floor to make room for more. The restaurant continues
in all directions.

Exits.Description: The Head Waiters pulpit it there and the rest of the establishment.
One larger table fills out the eastern part of the restaurant.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: The little napkins have the initials MGDP on them.
Ma Glob's Dancing Parlor.

rooms.Name: Restaurant
rooms.Description:
Two small tables stand here with a small white tablecloth covering
them and a silver candelabra in the center of each one. Both tables have
just been presented with a very nice 'prelude'. One table got a few
slices of raw spiced salmon and four kinds of salad while the other
received large crushed crabs in their own shells. You drool at the sight
of it. Even though it looks really delicious, it's not for you. The
restaurant continues in all directions, but north where a "fence"
protects the dance floor.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Don't want stuffed dinner guests tumbling out in the middle of the dance
floor, do we ?

Now this is a very very compliicated recipe.
Take raw salmon (or greaved) place it on fresh, newly rinced and cleansed
leaves of salad.
Thats it.
One could of course add some newly crushed black pepper and a drop of
limejuice on top as well just for the taste of it.

Making crab ready for eating is really rather simple.
Clean it. Clean it again and then clean it.
Boil it in very salted water (1 litre and 1/2 dl salt each)
Let it be in the boiling water under the lid for aprox 20 mins.
When done cool it down quickly, preferably in its own juices.
this could be ashieved by puting the whole pan in a larger one filled
with cold water.
Open it along the natural line on the crab underside.
Take up the meat and spice it or mix it with whatever yuo feel like.
I like to chop it fine and then fry it up with a little oil and finely
grained bread. After which I put it all back into its shell and serve
still a little warm. It brings out more of their delicious tastes.

rooms.Name: A small fountain
rooms.Description:
A huge single crystal fountain stands firmly on the black marble
floor, here in between the northern dance floor and the rest of the
restaurant to the east. Wine glasses and illuminating candles stand
alternatively on small protrusions, inviting you to grab a glass and
drink yourself unthirsty. Auntie Tabitha has her own small table
standing here too, with a great view over the stage, but it's unused at
the moment.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Considering the size of the fountain, you understand why the floor is
stone here and not wooden as in the rest of the restaurant.

As a regular (and with some heavy bribes) Auntie Tabitha has managed
to get her personal table in the exclusive restaurant overlooking the
dance floor, where she can see the youngsters amuse themselves and maybe
even get a glimpse of her favourite, Hulio. She hopes that one day
Stanneg will once again revive and be full of people.
Now, where is that Hulio everybody is talking about ?

rooms.Name: Dimly lit part of the Restaurant
rooms.Description:
One small two-person table stands here, a bit out of the way of
the sometimes disturbing activities in the rest of the restaurant, east
of here. This is the perfect place for a little tete-a-tete. The usual
candelabra is replaced with 3 small candles to give a more calm,
smoothing light. The walls also have a better sound suppressing cloth
cover.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The flame shivers by the small gust of wind you create as you come
close. Perhaps you should be a bit more careful playing with fire.

rooms.Name: Restaurant
rooms.Description:
Two small tables stand here with a small white tablecloth covering
them and a silver candelabra in the center of each one. The main course
seems to have been recently provided. At one table they seem to have
ordered filled grilled wild boar, fresh from the Haon-Dor forest with
vegetables and a nice bottle of red, while the others got some kind of
arroz-de-marisco, a soup with all the delights from the sea together
with a marvelous green wine.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Roast of wild boar. (courtesy of the ancient master Hagdahl)
One large piece of meat.
Fat
Juniper berries
Onions
Pepper
Carnations
Laurel leaves
Salt
Vinegar
Butter
Cream

The best meat for a roast you will get from a one year old. Clean the
meat and put it together with a little water in a pot over the fire.
Remove any foam or slags that appear on the surface, after a while you
can add the spices and the vinegar, but be sparesome with the salt as the
off boiling of water might cause to salty water.
When the meat is tender bring the meat up and start to fry the meat
softly in butter and cream. Do not forget to pour the sauce over it
frequently. The frying time is for a 'standard' leg around 4-5 hours.
So be prepared to stand in the good smell of the roast for several
hours..... The meat can also be marinated a few days before to get that
extra taste experience.

The Arroz-de-marisco is just what it sounds like.
Rice and seafood, preferably in a tomato tasting environment.
Choose your favourite seafood. I prefer a mix of shrimp, crab, lobster
(lot of lobster), some small pieces of squid and maybe even some plain
fish meat (be careful not to get small bones in the soup as they have a
tendency to find that wrong spot in yuor mouth). Take a large pot. Put
all the seafood in it. The ones with longest boiling time goes in first.
It is ok to boil with the shell on as it gives to the taste, just make
sure to clean properly. Boil the rice separately until its almost done
then pour everything over into the fish bowl. Let the rice soak in the
tastes and add the spices you want and the tomato paste. Perhaps some
pepper and a laurel leave. I like to spice little as I prefer the taste
of the components as they were. Perhaps add a little sugar to increase
the experienced taste (but not to much).
Serve hot together with newly baked bread and a lot of serviettes.
Delicious !

The red wine seems to be a rather heavy one. The grapes are grown on the
slopes of some Japanese mountain/volcano which add an extra touch to it.

A perfect choice. This light semi-sparkling wine goes very well together
with the chosen seafood.

Connoisseur, my well trained butt ! There happens to be a lot of
different kinds available... Try a red or a green one.

rooms.Name: Restaurant
rooms.Description:
Two small tables stand here with a small white tablecloth covering
them and a silver candelabra in the center of each one. Mmmmmm, you
smell dessert. It is impossible to tell what it is, but just by the
aroma you feel that this is really really good. The head chef, Miss
Bean, seems to have done it again! The restaurant continues in all
directions but south.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Oh, you will have to ask Miss Bean about her creations.

rooms.Name: Restaurant
rooms.Description:
One large oak table fills this part of the restaurant. A perfect spot
for that big family dinner. And that seems to be in progress right now.
A multitude of small plates cover the table, all with a different
content. It is good that there is a large chandelier hanging from the
roof, because there is no room for any light source on the table. Ma
Glob provides a plenitude of food as always. The restaurant extends only
to the west.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It seems they have almost ordered everything of the menu. Of course in
very small amounts because its a very extensive menu.

rooms.Name: Swinging doors
rooms.Description:
In the wooden wall south of here are two doors leading to the
kitchen. No locks seem to be present but you have to take the right one
to ensure that you won't collide with any of the staff that most
frequently pass through - if you want to pass safely. North of here is
the nice little well-renowned restaurant of Ma Glob's Dancing Parlor.

rooms.Name: Boule-o-Drome Display
rooms.Description:
Posted here are the plans for a full scale 147 lane Boule-o-Drome !!!
Gigantic in size, almost as big as the famous New Spartan football
field. It is Ma itself that has put up these drawings here. Why?, you
ask. Nobody knows and Ma Glob is not the kind of entity you can force
to open up on something Ma won't talk about. The only visible exit is
west towards the blackjack table.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
After some time you figure out that the drawings show a never built
sporting (if you call Boule sport) facility. It was to be placed next to
the Japanese stone gardens to amuse the people living close to it.
   Unfortunately some committee in charge of the land decided to build
some other arena on the spot, uncaring of the local inhabitants hopes
and decisions. Nowadays many people travel to use the already built
facility and the people living in the Japanese Stone Gardens only
managed to create a Chinese Stone Garden outside the sporting centre.

The dream goes on. Some day IT WILL BE BUILT !!!
It will be glorious and the now risen sport facility will wither in
comparison to the marvelous creation of the Stone garden people.
The Japanese Stone Garden is the home of the Mountainmen and Women.
The Chinese Stone Garden is now being viewed from the Japanese.
The mountain people are not here. They have gone back to their stones.

rooms.Name: Black Jack Table
rooms.Description:
A high half circular black jack table stands here, apparently the
center of the card games here. There are no chairs here but the table
seems to be used anyway. Ask around. They might set up a game just for
you. The gaming area continues both east and west and the to the south
you see the Grand Master Waiter's Pulpit.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: There are 6 positions for players on the green cloth covering the table.

rooms.Name: Chemin-de-Fer Table
rooms.Description:
This seems to be a more sophisticated part of the gaming area. A
small table covered in green cloth stands surrounded by 5 chairs. On the
table a small box of cards is placed, obviously the center of attention
during the game. The gaming area continues both east and west.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
One dealer and four players. The games do not get full. The rules are
pretty much the same as dice but for cards and a bit more sophisticated.

rooms.Name: Roulette Table
rooms.Description:
The roulette department in not surprisingly dominated by a large
sized roulette table. It looks like any other table of its kind. Most
likely it looks that way inside too. The gaming area continues both east
and west and south you can head towards the dance floor for a little
swing-about.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
All the segments supposed to be there are there. Black-Red. Odd-Even.
0 up to, well a lot and if you are lucky your number will be present on
the wheel when the ball is tossed.

rooms.Name: Darts
rooms.Description:
Here at the end of the gaming part of the Parlor the establishment
has put up 3 dartboards on the wall for their local throwing addicts
and other customers. The dartboards are the ordinary 83 sector and you
easily notice the absence of marking in the wall. Everyone using these
are real good throwers. Only way out is the way you came in, back east.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
First one down from 301 to exactly 0 wins. Maximum score is received
from that little little zone where the 20 point field triples.

No marks what so ever. Either these players are really good or the wall
is regenerative. Perhaps it's both.

rooms.Name: Next to the Stage
rooms.Description:
There are stairs here leading up to the stage. A big yellow sign with
black letters reads 'Restricted Area' and 'Stage Personnel only'. There
should be a guard here, but sometimes he has more important things to
do. East of here are some panels and benches, from where you can reach
the dance floor.

rooms.Name: Panels
rooms.Description:
The panels are classic, every establishment has one. Here people,
not dancing, gather to do what people who do not dance do. Its not a
very uplifting place as so many hearts have unknowingly been broken
here. A small bench is placed next to the panel so that the girls can
sit and chat with each other while they wait for Mr Right. The dance
floor of dreams is so close to the south, but still so far away.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: The bench is unfortunately very well used.

rooms.Name: Panels
rooms.Description:
The panels are classic, every establishment has one. Here people,
not dancing, gather to do what people that do not dance do. This is the
boys' corner. The smell of old beer is a bit dominant and over the years
it has become impossible to remove it. A small bench, perfect for those
lies about your latest conquest, stands next to the panel. Left the girls
hang out.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The bench is unfortunately very well used and a bit dirty too. It looks
like someone carved in a crude message in the wood.
Raff was here.

rooms.Name: Dance floor
rooms.Description:
This generic type of dance floor is perfect for tango, waltz, any odd
youngster shake or that wonderful pair dance where you embrace each
other and just stand there, slightly swaying back and forth, totally
ignorant of any music. West and south of here you can peek over the edge
of the stage, but you can only swirl eastwardly.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
You see a well polished scene, a perfect place for musicians.
Perhaps you should sneak up for a look if you find a place to climb.

rooms.Name: Dance floor
rooms.Description:
This generic type of dance floor is perfect for tango, waltz, any
odd youngster shake or that wonderful pair dance where you embrace each
other and just stand there, slightly swaying back and forth, totally
ignorant of any music. The dance floor continues in all directions
except north where the games are.

rooms.Name: Dance floor
rooms.Description:
This generic type of dance floor is perfect for tango, waltz, any odd
youngster shake or that wonderful pair dance where you embrace each other
and just stand there, slightly swaying back and forth, totally ignorant
of any music. The dance floor continues in all directions.

rooms.Name: Dance floor
rooms.Description:
This generic type of dance floor is perfect for tango, waltz, any odd
youngster shake or that wonderful pair dance where you embrace each other
and just stand there, slightly swaying back and forth, totally ignorant
of any music. The dance floor continues in all directions but
east where you can see the Pulpit of the Grand Master Waiter.

rooms.Name: Dance floor
rooms.Description:
This generic type of dance floor is perfect for tango, waltz, any odd
youngster shake or that wonderful pair dance where you embrace each other
and just stand there, slightly swaying back and forth, totally ignorant
of any music. The dance floor continues in all directions.

This generic type of dance floor is perfect for tango, waltz, any odd
youngster shake or that wonderful pair dance where you embrace each other
and just stand there, slightly swaying back and forth, totally ignorant
of any music. The dance floor continues in all directions

rooms.Name: Dance floor
rooms.Description:
This generic type of dance floor is perfect for tango, waltz, any odd
youngster shake or that wonderful pair dance where you embrace each other
and just stand there, slightly swaying back and forth, totally ignorant
of any music. West and north of here you can peek over the edge of the
stage, but you can only swirl eastward while the restaurant offers
refreshment to the south.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
You see a well polished scene, a perfect place for musicians.
Perhaps you should sneak up for a look if you find a place to climb.

rooms.Name: Dance floor
rooms.Description:
This generic type of dance floor is perfect for tango, waltz, any odd
youngster shake or that wonderful pair dance where you embrace each other
and just stand there, slightly swaying back and forth, totally ignorant
of any music. Here in the midst of the dance floor young girls often
gather in trance to worship the marvelous mushy singer extreme, Hulio.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Where is he ?  He usually is out there on the catwalk of the stage.

rooms.Name: Hulio's part of the Stage
rooms.Description:
Standing on the polished wooden floor you have a great view over the
dance floor and the restaurant and you can guess that they can see you,
too. No wonder this is Hulio's favourite part of the stage. A place
where he can be adored and where he can get eye contact with whomever he
wants to.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Oh it sure looks inviting.
You feel thirsty.
You feel hungry.

There are loads of people in the Dancing Parlor and restaurant and they
are all looking at YOU !!!
Make your and their day - Sing a song for everyone.

rooms.Name: On the Catwalk
rooms.Description:
The catwalk is an extension of the stage, so that some performers can
be even more the center of attention. Stretching east-west, the polished
wooden floor gleams in the lighting of the place.

rooms.Name: Center of the Stage
rooms.Description:
Slightly highlighted by the stage lighting, the center of the stage
is for musicians to take a step up to, to make solos. It has been used a
lot but is still in a very good condition. East of here the catwalk
protrudes and in all other directions the wooden floor of the stage
continues. There is a tiny prompt box here too, next to the stage edge.

Exits.Description:
The prompt box has not been used in a very long time, but did you not
hear a sound from down there ?

rooms.Name: South-East Corner of the Stage
rooms.Description:
Standing on the wooden stage you have a good view over the dance
floor and the slightly elevated part of the dancing parlor where the
wonderful cuisine created by Miss Bean and her staff is being served
to her guests. From here you can reach the center of the stage to the
north and the rear part to the west.

rooms.Name: North-East Corner of the Stage
rooms.Description:
Standing on the wooden stage you have a good view over the dance
floor and the usually so crowded gambling part of the dancing parlor.
The floor squeaks a bit as you move over it. A good guess is that the
stairs going up from the gaming area to where you are standing are
causing this. The stage continues west and south from here.

rooms.Name: Mad Drummer Corner
rooms.Description:
This corner usually is abandoned by the other musicians. This is a
well made stage so it is not shabby or badly lit. The problem is the
drummer that hangs around here. Well, he usually runs around banging
anything he can find extracting the finest drumming ever heard, but
others just fear for their lives in his vicinity. The stage continues
east and south as well as north behind the curtain.

rooms.Name: Center part of the back Stage
rooms.Description:
The center part of the stage closest to the back wall is not really
that exhilarating. The back wall is covered in a fine cloth of good
quality. The floor is as the rest of the stage, polished hardwood. You
imagine that it would be perfect for a brass section of a big band to be
placed here. The stage continues in all directions except westwards.

rooms.Name: South-West part of the Stage
rooms.Description:
This part of the stage is a bit in the background of the rest. The
surroundings are still in the same excellent shape as the rest of the
stage but here you can more or less do your own thing. And you notice
that the sound conditions here are very good. The stage continues north
and east as well as south behind the curtains.

rooms.Name: Behind the Curtain
rooms.Description:
Standing on the stage but out of view, you are almost surrounded by
ropes that go up and down here. They must be here to allow the curtain to
open and close before and after the shows. The only exit seems to be
north out on the stage, but if you really try you just might be able to
climb the ropes.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It looks climbable but for your own sake you had better fly to make it
up there safely.

rooms.Name: Above the Stage
rooms.Description:
From here you have a nice view of the stage, but only that. The
lighting does not spread well up here. It could be the dust or just that
it is very narrow. You dare not go down again so the only thing is to
