You are standing below a great staircase, that leads up to the second
floor of the Castle. The stairs are made of marble, and there are
pillars carved in the likenesses of trees with little animals running up
and down the trunks.

Exits.Description: You see the passage.
The stairs lead up to the second floor.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Made out of marble, and as all the rest of the Castle made primarily
for beauty and with great skill.
Very nice. Squirrels and little birds all over.

rooms.Name: The servants' quarters
rooms.Description:
You are standing in a large room, that seems to house many of the
servants.  The room is full of comfortable-looking beds. There is also a
large chest, probably containing some of the servants' belongings.

Exits.Description: The door is made out of wood.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The beds all look comfortable, despite the fact that this is just
the servants' place.

rooms.Name: The butler's quarters
rooms.Description:
You see at once that this must be the butler's room, for it lies in
the servants' wing, and still it is large and comfortable; almost
luxurious, in fact. There is a large bed and a drawer in the room. The
only exit is via the door to the south.

Exits.Description: You see the corridor.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Looks very comfortable indeed.

rooms.Name: The Guards' Barracks
rooms.Description:
You are standing in a very large room with bunks all over. It is
obvious, that this is where the guards off duty spend most of their
time, drinking and gambling or, probably, mostly sleeping.

Exits.Description: The door is large and heavy.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: They look a bit hard, but you could sleep in them.

rooms.Name: The stairs
rooms.Description:
You are standing by a staircase leading down. As you look down, you
notice that for the first time since you entered the castle, things are
not aesthetically made. Instead it looks more functional and
prison-like.

Exits.Description: You see the small passage.
The stairs go down to a well lit room.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
They seem to be made of granite, and stretch down into a more dimly
lit area than where you come from.

rooms.Name: At a bend in the corridor
rooms.Description: You are standing where the corridor bends from east to north.

Exits.Description: You see the corridor continue.
You see the corridor continue.

rooms.Name: The corridor
rooms.Description:
You are standing in a long corridor, decorated with tapestries
depicting old times and old heroes. It leads east and west.

Exits.Description: You see the corridor continue.
You see the corridor continue.

rooms.Name: The corridor
rooms.Description:
You are standing in a long corridor, decorated with tapestries
depicting old times and old heroes. It leads east and west.

Exits.Description: You see the corridor continue.
You see the corridor continue.

rooms.Name: The corridor
rooms.Description:
You are standing in a long corridor, decorated with tapestries
depicting old times and old heroes. The corridor continues west, and to
the north you see the luxurious guest wing.

Exits.Description: You see the guest wing.
You see the corridor continue.

rooms.Name: In the south-east tower
rooms.Description:
This part of the tower is fairly uninteresting, but it leads further
upwards...

Exits.Description: The room at the top of the tower seems darkish for some reason.
You see the stairs at the bottom of the tower.

rooms.Name: The corridor
rooms.Description:
You are standing in a long corridor, decorated with tapestries
depicting old times and old heroes. It leads north and south. There is
also an exit to the east here.

Exits.Description: You see the corridor continue.
You see a small room.
You see the corridor continue.

rooms.Name: By the treasure room
rooms.Description:
You are standing by a great iron door. The door is very large, and
seems very solid indeed. There is a sign posted by it.

Exits.Description: You see a large steel door.
You see the corridor.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
TREASURE ROOM

   Authorized personnel only - all others keep out.
   ANY trespassing will be SEVERELY punished!!

rooms.Name: The Great Treasury
rooms.Description:
As you enter this room, you are astonished by the riches that are
stowed away here; not so much in gold, but paintings, tapestries,
skillful carvings and sculptures all over the vast room. You realize,
however, that most of these things are too well known to be sold
anywhere, without branding yourself as a thief, and condemning yourself
to instant death at the hands of the Royal Guard.

Exits.Description: You see a large steel door.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It seems they are stored here temporarily to enable changing of the
decoration in the Castle on a regular basis.

rooms.Name: The Guest Wing
rooms.Description:
You have arrived at the part of the Castle where prominent guests are
housed. To the east there is a large, ornamented door, and a somewhat
smaller one leads north.

Exits.Description: The door seems to lead to a guest room.
You see the guest suite behind the door.
You see the corridor.

rooms.Name: The Guest Suite
rooms.Description:
This must be where only the most highly regarded guests stay, since
it is luxurious beyond your wildest imagination. This is only the living
room  of the suite, but it is huge and tastefully decorated. All the
furniture is not only beautiful, but also made for comfort. To the
north, there is an exit to the bedroom, and there is a door to the west.

Exits.Description: You see the bedroom.
Behind the door you see the entrance to the Guest Wing.

rooms.Name: The corridor
rooms.Description:
You are standing in a long corridor, decorated with tapestries
depicting old times and old heroes. It leads north and south.

Exits.Description: You see the corridor continue.
You see the corridor continue.

rooms.Name: The Ball Room
rooms.Description:
You are standing in the great Ball Room. It is a truly large room,
with a stage for an orchestra in the south-east end.

Exits.Description: You see the Ball Room.
To the east you see the stage.

rooms.Name: By the stage
rooms.Description:
Before you, you see the stage. It is large enough for some 40
musicians to play on at the same time. The Ball Room continues to the
west and north.

Exits.Description: You see the Ball Room.
You see the Ball Room.

rooms.Name: A Guest Room
rooms.Description:
You are standing in a large room. Although it is comfortable enough,
you can tell it is not meant for any of the most illustrious guests,
since it lacks that extreme luxury found elsewhere in the Castle.

Exits.Description: Behind the door, you see the entrance to the Guest Wing.

rooms.Name: The Bedroom
rooms.Description:
This room is dominated by the huge four-poster bed, that stands
against the northern wall. The room is large and cozy, and the bed
virtually begs you to lie down in it and sleep.

Exits.Description: You see the living room of the suite.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Large, comfortable, bolstered... Invites you to sleep in it.

rooms.Name: The corridor
rooms.Description:
You are standing in a long corridor, decorated with tapestries
depicting old times and old heroes. It leads north and south. There is
an exit to the east, that leads to a large room.

Exits.Description: You see the corridor continue.
You see the Ball Room.
You see the corridor continue.

rooms.Name: The Ball Room
rooms.Description:
You are standing in the great Ball Room. It is a truly large room,
with a stage for an orchestra in the south-east end.

Exits.Description: You see the Ball Room.
You see the Ball Room.
You see the corridor.

rooms.Name: The Ball Room
rooms.Description:
You are standing in the great Ball Room. It is a truly large room,
with a stage for an orchestra in the south-east end.

Exits.Description: To the east, you can enter a tower.
To the south you see the stage.
You see the Ball Room.

rooms.Name: In the Tower
rooms.Description:
You are standing in the north-eastern of the three great watch-
towers of the Castle. To the west, you can enter the Ball Room and there
are stairs leading up into the Tower.

Exits.Description: You see the Ball Room.
The stairs lead a long way up to the top of the Tower.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: The stairs are made out of granite, and seem solid enough.

rooms.Name: The Grand Staircase
rooms.Description:
You are standing on a great staircase, that leads up and down. To the
east, there is a large oak door, and a corridor leads south.

Exits.Description: The door is large and made out of oak.
You see the corridor.
The stairs continue up to the top of the tower.
The stairs lead down to the first floor of the Castle.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The stairs are made of marble, and there are pillars carved in the
likenesses of trees with little animals running up and down the trunks.

rooms.Name: The Cozy Room
rooms.Description:
You have entered a large, cozy living room. There is a fireplace with
a fire burning, and a few comfortable chairs around a little table.
There is a door to the west, and also an exit to the east.

Exits.Description: You see a large bedroom.
The door is large, and made out of oak.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The fire is built out of logs, and seems to be able to burn for 
quite a while longer.
The table is made of mahogany, and elegant in a cozy way(!)
The chairs are arranged around the fireplace.

rooms.Name: The King's Bedroom
rooms.Description:
This is a large room, with a wonderful view. To one side of the room,
stands a large four-poster bed. All around the room there are massive
bookshelves, filled with all kinds of books. The titles include works
such as: 'A Treatise on the History of Midgaard and surrounding areas',
'Magic - A Beginner's Introduction' and many others. There is an exit to
the west.

Exits.Description: There is a large and cozy room to the west.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Most of the books seem worn, as if thoroughly studied. The King
evidently is interested in keeping himself educated.

Seems nice enough to sleep in, though you would never dare to, since
it is a Royal Bed!
A dry tome, filled with boring knowledge.

Beginner? This book goes beyond most of what YOU know about magic
anyway. But then, there are levels of magical knowledge, it seems.

rooms.Name: Up in the Tower
rooms.Description:
After a long climb, you finally reach the top of the tower. This room
is small, and the only light source is a flickering candle, on a
cluttered table, in the middle of the room. The only obvious exit is
back down the stairs.

Exits.Description: The stairs go down the tower.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: On the table are various objects, all very strange-looking.
Small, uninteresting... A candle that is as normal as can be.

rooms.Name: The Top of the Tower
rooms.Description:
You have arrived at the top of the tower. This tower is pretty
uninteresting, and seems made purely for reasons of defense and
guarding. The windows are slits for bowmen, very narrow on the outward
side and broad inwards to allow a wide shooting angle. The only evident
exit is down the stairs again.

Exits.Description: The stairs go down to the second floor.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: As you look out the windows, you are granted a view of the country..

rooms.Name: The Top of the Tower
rooms.Description:
This is the highest of all the towers, and is obviously used for
lookout purposes. The view is splendid in all four directions. All
around you, the rich countryside spreads out to the horizon. To the
north and east you see a vast mountain range, and far to the west a
beautiful lake. A bit closer, the town of Midgaard lies at the end of
the King's Road. The only exit you can see is down again.

Exits.Description:
To the north, the tall White Mountains have their highest peaks. The
mountain tops disappear in the white clouds, far above the plains. The
sight of those high, far mountains fills you with a desire to scale
them, to see the world from that vantage.

In the east you see an arm of the dominating mountain range on this
continent, the White Mountains. Though not as high as those in the
north, the sight of those mountains fills you with awe.
To the south, rolling hills stretch away, as far as you can see.

As you look west, you see a river flowing through all of Midgaard and
continuing beyond it towards a great lake. Still further away, you can
glimpse something silvery that has to be the Sea.
You see the stairs going back down to the second floor.

rooms.Name: Bottom of the Stairs
rooms.Description:
At the bottom of a steep stone flight of stairs, you look around at the
well lit, but bare area.  There are two large hard chairs and a small
table.  On a small shelf built into the wall, you can see something
metallic, but the shelf is deep and shadowed.  There is a very heavy
door leading north.  It has a large sturdy knob and a keyhole the size
of a large walnut.

#GA few words have been carved on the lintel of the door north.#N

Exits.Description: A massive, heavy iron-bound door leads northward.
You see the stairs heading up to the main floor.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: #wAbandon Hope, All Ye Who Enter Here#N

rooms.Name: Abandon Hope, All Ye Who Enter Here
rooms.Description:
A small corridor leads to many cells, including one that appears to
hold many prisoners.  There is a distinctly evil feel to this room.  You
can feel the hair rising on the back of your neck.  The room is dimly
lit by two flickering torches resting in wall fixtures at about shoulder
height for a giant.  The stone floor is uneven beneath your feet, and
quite dirty.  You sense that the castles Cleaning Women do not make it
down this far.  There are doors leading in all directions, including a
heavy iron grate beneath your feet.  Each cell door has been labeled.

Exits.Description: Cell #1.  Heavy iron bars form the door to this cell.
Cell #2. A door of steel bars leads to another cell area.
A massive, heavy iron-bound door leads to a well-lit area.
Cell #3. A door of mithril and steel leads west.
A gagging smell rises from the oubliette.

rooms.Name: A Large Cell
rooms.Description:
This cell stretches as far as you can see, which actually isn't very
far considering the lighting.  A dim shroud of hopelessness envelops the
cell, a general cell for all of King Welmar's male prisoners.  Food is
delivered to the cell via the space beneath the door, and the water is a
simple trough, foul with dirt.  You fear venturing forward into this
nightmarish place, and should probably go south to the dismal entrance
room south.

Exits.Description: The gloom thickens north, east and west of where you quiver.
The gloom thickens north, east and west of where you shiver and shake.
Flickering torchlight beckons you away from the gloom.
The gloom thickens north, east and west of where you stand quivering.

rooms.Name: Behind the Steel Bars
rooms.Description:
As the cell is just barely lit by light reflected from the torches in
the room west of here, it is hard to make out any features of the room
itself or its inhabitants.  The floor feels hard beneath your feet,
undoubtedly the same stone as in the access room.  The walls are rough,
dirty, and slightly damp.  The stench is overwhelming.

Exits.Description: Steel bars form the door which leads out of the cell.

rooms.Name: Cell Block #3
rooms.Description:
The torch light from the entryway filters through the mithril and
steel bars forming part of the eastern wall of this cell.  Although by
no means well-lit, the openness of that wall allows you to see the straw
sleeping pallet in one corner, and the few hard crumbs remaining from a
recent meal.  The floor is bare, hard, and dirty as are the walls.
Being locked in here for a day would drive the sanest person mad.

Exits.Description: The small entry area lies east of here.

rooms.Name: The Oubliette
rooms.Description:
A heavy steel grate drops automatically into place overhead, blocking
even sound from above. This pit is one of several oubliettes in this
dungeon.  It is well-named.  Prisoners are placed (dropped?) in here and
then forgotten.  It is a slow death, as there is no escape possible.  As
you look around, you see the source of the horrifying odor rising from
this hole in the prison floor.
 
#GThe putrid remains of a prisoner lie here, rotting.#N

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Small bits of decaying flesh still hang on the bones, but not enough
to tell you who this once was.  The stench is overpowering.

rooms.Name: Thickening gloom
rooms.Description:
All around you you hear soft rustling noises of vermin, nesting in
the straw.  Occasionally a quiet moan reminds you that, incredibly,
there are prisoners still alive here.  The light is so dim that all
directions look the same to you.

Exits.Description: The gloom of endless suffering amidst endless evil beckons to you.
The gloom of endless suffering amidst endless evil beckons to you.
A large door connects you to a torchlit room.
The gloom of endless suffering amidst endless evil beckons to you.

rooms.Name: Thickening gloom
rooms.Description:
All around you you hear soft rustling noises of vermin, nesting in
the straw.  Occasionally a quiet moan reminds you that, incredibly,
there are prisoners still alive here.  The light is so dim that all
directions look the same to you.

Exits.Description: The gloom of endless suffering amidst endless evil beckons to you.
The gloom of endless suffering amidst endless evil beckons to you.
The gloom of endless suffering amidst endless evil beckons to you.
The gloom of endless suffering amidst endless evil beckons to you.

rooms.Name: On the Outskirts of Midgaard
rooms.Description:
The capital city of Midgaard generates a lot of traffic, and the
mayor and his councillors have chosen to encourage growth by improving
the many roads and waterways leading into the city.  The road is broad
and well-paved here.  It is rumored that Roman engineers were brought in
to design and supervise the building of this road.

Exits.Description:
The broad paved road leads east over hill and stream as far as you can
see.
To the west, the sounds and movement of city life increase dramatically.

rooms.Name: Road Through Heavy Forest
rooms.Description:
Trees thickly line the road to both north and south.  The forest
seems impenetrable here, and you wonder at the marvels of the Roman
engineers.  The well paved, Roman laid road continues east and west.

Exits.Description: The wide road continues east towards the kingdom of Welmar.
Midgaard, with all the delights of a capital city, lies to the west.

rooms.Name: Road through Heavy Forest
rooms.Description:
The well-paved road runs east and west, often thick with traffic.
Oxcarts bearing precious metals from the mountain mines, finely-made
dwarven armor, magic and herbs of elven origin - all travel this road at
some time, headed for the city of Midgaard.  With the many tradesmen
come artists and farmers and many who would train in the big city to
become master warriors and mages, clerics and healers and, yes, thieves
as well.

Exits.Description: The road appears to fork at some distance in the east.
A broad, well-paved, well-kept road makes its way towards Midgaard.

rooms.Name: A Fork in the Road
rooms.Description:
The Roman roadwork comes to an end at what is, nevertheless, a
magnificent intersection.  The southern fork follows the river for a
distance, heading for the magnificence of the kingdom of the good king
Welmar.  The other, more sinister fork, heads north into the great
purple mountains where, it is rumored, trolls lie in wait to munch
foolhardy adventurers.

Exits.Description: The road continues, rocky and rough, headed towards the foothills.

The road continues, wide and smooth, clearly well kept even though it is
no longer paved.

The beautifully paved, Roman-made road heads towards the splendors
of Midgaard.

rooms.Name: A Well-Travelled Road
rooms.Description:
The fine courtiers and nobles of the court of King Welmar travel this
road when they have business in the capital city of Midgaard.  The road
has been maintained at great cost to the wealthy king.  The forest on
both sides of the road is heavy.

Exits.Description: The road forks ahead, where Roman paving begins.
The forest begins to thin out ahead.

rooms.Name: Thick Forest
rooms.Description:
The thick forest continues to line both sides of the road, and to the
south you can hear the steady WHACK! Whack! of the lumberjack's axe.
The frenzied rate of building in this kingdom has increased the demand
for lumber.  There have been rumors that the trees scream in protest,
and darker rumors of hideous deaths of those found in the forest at
night.

Exits.Description:
The broad, hard packed road stretches very straightly north through
thick forest.
The thick forest crowds the road south.

rooms.Name: Thick Forest
rooms.Description:
Thick forest, old growth trees, crowd the wide road.  The road itself
winds slowly from north to east here, rolling around a gentle hill in
the deep forest.  An occasional WHACK! WHACK! of an axe is followed by
an eerie inhuman scream. There seems to be something strange about the
bushes to the west.

Exits.Description: The broad, well-packed dirt road heads north through thick forest.

The broad road winds east through gently rolling hills and thickly
encroaching forest.
You notice a narrow trail concealed in the undergrowth.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: There seems to be an opening of some sort behind the underbrush.

rooms.Name: Thick Forest
rooms.Description:
Closely spaced trees thin slightly to the east, creating a small
clearing.  The trees are tall and ancient, with branches which canopy
the roadway far over your head.  The result is a chill even in strong
sunlight, and an odd dappling pattern on the packed earthen road.

Exits.Description: It looks like there may be a small clearing just east of here.
The broad, tree-covered road continues westward.

rooms.Name: A Clearing
rooms.Description:
The trees have been thinned out here, clearly by man rather than fire
or disease.  There is a grassy area with many low stumps where you may
sit and rest, and a little trickle of a path runs north from the
clearing into the trees.

Exits.Description:
A thin, faint path leads into the trees.  It could simply be an animal
trail, or a path made by one of the elves native to this area.
The broad road continues east towards the great Kingdom of Welmar.
The broad road continues west towards the great city of Midgaard.

rooms.Name: Through Thick Forest
rooms.Description:
Pushing your way through lush green foliage, turning sideways to
slide through narrow gaps in trees, the reality of a path becomes
questionable.  Perhaps it is your imagine that sees a pattern in the
slight spacings between plants that leads you north from here.

Exits.Description:
Thick foliage (leaves of three, let it be ... better count them) must be
pushed aside if you wish to continue north.

If you are very careful and very skinny you can move through gaps in
trees and bushes and head south.

rooms.Name: Brigands!
rooms.Description:
A small camp here close to the castle shows the shabby flag of the
anti-monarchists, the revolutionaries of Welmar's kingdom.  In truth,
these revolutionaries support themselves by preying on hapless
travellers along the Welmar-Midgard highway.  A small tent sits at the
west end of the clearing.

Exits.Description:
The bushes and trees surrounding this camp seem slightly less thick to
the south.

A small tent made of elk and other animal hides sits at the west end of
this clearing.

rooms.Name: Inside the Tent
rooms.Description:
Strategy and planning sessions are held here in the tent of the
revolutionary leader Neb N'var.  Fiery speeches and sly plots are both
conceived in this tent, as is the next generation of revolutionaries.
The revolution has been a long time coming.

Exits.Description: The tent flap opens east.

rooms.Name: The Well-Trod Road
rooms.Description:
To the west lies a small clearing, perhaps a rest stop of sorts where
the weary traveller might regain his strength.  Or perhaps it is a trap
laid by one of the many groups of thieves you have heard roam this
forest despite King Welmar's best efforts.  This road continues both
east and west.

Exits.Description: The road east leads smoothly through thick forest.
The road west leads to a small clearing.  Picnic spot or trap?

rooms.Name: Near a Bridge
rooms.Description:
The sound of moving water drifts at you from the east, and in the
daytime you might be able to spot a castle from this spot.  You are
standing on a very wide, hardened dirt road leading west into deepest
forest and east to some body of water.

Exits.Description:
In the distance, for as far as you can see, lies thick forest, forest
which is apparently in a very bad mood.

rooms.Name: Paving Stones
rooms.Description:
The road at this point becomes paved with large flat white river
stones.  In the near distance to the east stands a magnificent old stone
bridge.  To the west, the thick forest continues.

rooms.Name: Past the Fork
rooms.Description:
The road deteriorates rapidly here deteriorating into a heavily
rutted cart track, much in used by both farmers and miners bringing
their wares to the city.  To the north, a new stronghold is being
built in a forest clearing.  South, the road becomes beautifully
paved.  This is the farmland of Welmar's mighty kingdom, perhaps.

Exits.Description: A stronghold is being constructed to the north.

rooms.Name: The Glorious Bridge
rooms.Description:
A very elaborate bridge stretches across the Midgaard River, which is
quite broad at this point.  At this end, the Midgaardian end, the bridge
is guarded by two enormous cast iron knights astride two even more
enormous cast iron horses.  The horses' teeth are bared and the knights
fists' are raised high in the air, clenching their swords.

Exits.Description:
An apparently strong bridge supported by stone arches spans the broad
expanse of the Midgaard River.

You can spot the western gates out of the City of Midgaard from this
point.
You can climb down to the Midgaard River.

rooms.Name: Like a Bridge over Midgaard Waters
rooms.Description:
A wide concrete bridge spans the troubled waters of the Midgaard
River.  Of Roman design and construction, you can tell that this is a
bridge which will be still standing here long after your many lives are
but a myth told over midnight glasses of ale at the local pub.

Exits.Description:
The wide and very sturdy bridge finishes its very long trip over the
River Midgaard just east of here.

Two huge knights mounted on fearsome horses challenge your right to
enter Midgaard.

rooms.Name: Like a Bridge over Midgaard Waters
rooms.Description:
Cast iron animals and odd misshapen figures appear to flee the brave
knights adorning the western (Midgaardian) end of this bridge.
Fantastical figures of fierce gryphons, drooling trolls, goblins and
orcs appear driven out of the city.  Perhaps this is meant as a warning.

Exits.Description:
A well made road clearly of Roman design proceeds in a grand manner
towards the rising sun.
A broad stone bridge spans the turbulent Midgaard River.

rooms.Name: A Narrow Trail
rooms.Description:
A narrow trail leads east and west from here, although some effort 
has been made to disguise the trail. The heavy paving slabs have been 
carefully concealed beneath a thick layer of earth and grass, with the 
stones only showing through in a few places.

Exits.Description: You see a wide road leading east.
The trail opens into a grassy meadow.

rooms.Name: City Entrance
rooms.Description:
You are at the entrance to a small underground city. A great adamantite gate
lies open to the west allowing entrance into the city.

Exits.Description: A huge gate opens to the west allowing entrance into the city.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: A large adamantite gate with giant spider shaped emblems stands here.

rooms.Name: City street
rooms.Description:
You walk along a highly ornate street going north-south. A large gate lies
to the east while a building lies to the west.

rooms.Name: City street
rooms.Description: You walk along a highly ornate city street going north and west.

rooms.Name: City street
rooms.Description:
You walk along a highly ornate city street going east-west. A large house
stands to the south.

rooms.Name: 3rd House
rooms.Description:
You stand inside the 3rd house of the city; it is fairly well decorated by
drow standards having a few statues, murals and such. A door leads to the
south.

rooms.Name: Throne Room
rooms.Description:
The throne room of the 3rd house is about as decorated as the inner
courtyard except with a blood covered altar in the center of the room.

rooms.Name: City street
rooms.Description:
You walk along a highly ornate city street going east-west. To the north is
a large building.

rooms.Name: City street
rooms.Description:
You walk along a highly ornate city street leading north and east. To the
south is an extremely large house.

rooms.Name: 2nd House
rooms.Description:
You stand inside the 2nd house of the city. The room is highly decorated
with statues of spiders and murals everywhere.

rooms.Name: Throne Room
rooms.Description:
The throne room of the 2nd house is just a little more decorative than the
inner courtyard having an altar in the center of the room.

rooms.Name: Main Gate
rooms.Description:
You are at the entrance to the 1st house of the city. A large gate, almost
as big and elegant as the one at the entrance to the city, stands here.

Exits.Description: A large gate lies to the west.

rooms.Name: 1st House
rooms.Description:
You stand in the inner courtyard of the 1st and largest house in the city.
The room is extremely large and decorative. Mural and paintings hang on the
walls depicting some battles and a spider queen.

rooms.Name: Throne Room
rooms.Description:
The throne room of the 1st house is in one word... awesome. It is so
horrifying it is almost beautiful.

rooms.Name: Main Chamber
rooms.Description:
This is the council chamber for the Matron Mother herself. A huge table and
chairs surrounding it sits in the center of the room.

rooms.Name: City street
rooms.Description: You walk along a highly ornate city street leading north-south and east.

rooms.Name: City street
rooms.Description:
You walk along a highly ornate city street leading south. A building is to
the west.

rooms.Name: Cleric Academy
rooms.Description: This is the most lavish of the academies being that it is for the clerics.

rooms.Name: City street
rooms.Description:
You walk along a highly ornate city street going east-west. To the north is
a giant temple.

Exits.Description: The entrance to the temple of Lloth.

rooms.Name: Warrior's Academy
rooms.Description: This looks more like a barracks than a school.

rooms.Name: Entrance to the Temple of Lloth
rooms.Description:
The temple is the largest building in the city. Even it's doors are beyond
imagination. Inside of the temple entrance, the walls are made of gold and
adamantite.

rooms.Name: Mage's Academy
rooms.Description:
The Mage's Academy is fairly well decorated see that the drow prefer magic
over physical power greatly.

rooms.Name: City street
rooms.Description:
You walk along a highly ornate city street going eastward. To the north is a
building.

rooms.Name: Slave Chamber
rooms.Description:
The room is in shambles. Straw is strewn all about the room as beds for the
unfortunate creatures who have fallen prey to drow imperialism.

rooms.Name: City street
rooms.Description:
You walk along a highly ornate city street leading west and south. To the
north is a relatively small house.

rooms.Name: 4th house
rooms.Description:
You stand inside the 4th house of the city. Its inner courtyard is rather
dull by drow standards and rather small as well.

rooms.Name: Throne Room
rooms.Description:
The throne room is basically similar to the inner courtyard in regards to
decor. there is a small throne behind the altar but that is about it.

rooms.Name: Entrance Way
rooms.Description:
You stand in the entrance way to the temple which opens up to the north into
a large hallway going east and west. Small statues of spiders line the entrance
way's walls.

rooms.Name: Hallway
rooms.Description:
You are in a long hallway lined with adamantite. The walls are engraved with
pictures of elves and spiders. The hallway continues east and west. As you look
down the hallway you can make out one or two figures moving away from you. To
the north is a obsidian stairway.

rooms.Name: Long Hallway
rooms.Description:
You are in a long hallway lined with adamantite. The walls are engraved with
pictures of elves and spiders. The hallway continues east and west. As you look
down the hallway you can make out one or two figures moving away from you.

rooms.Name: Long Hallway
rooms.Description:
You are in a long hallway lined with adamantite. The walls are engraved with
pictures of elves and spiders. The hallway continues east and west. As you look
down the hallway you can make out one or two figures moving away from you. To
the north is a door.

rooms.Name: Long Hallway
rooms.Description:
You are in a long hallway lined with adamantite. The walls are engraved with
pictures of elves and spiders. The hallway continues east and west. As you look
down the hallway you can make out one or two figures moving away from you.

rooms.Name: Long Hallway
rooms.Description:
You are in a long hallway lined with adamantite. The walls are engraved with
pictures of elves and spiders. The hallway continues east and west. As you look
down the hallway you can make out one or two figures moving away from you.

rooms.Name: Long Hallway
rooms.Description:
You are in a long hallway lined with adamantite. The walls are engraved with
pictures of elves and spiders. The hallway continues east and west. As you look
down the hallway you can make out one or two figures moving away from you. To
the south is a door.

rooms.Name: Warrior's Barracks
rooms.Description:
The room is a complete mess. None of the beds are made, clothes and other
items have been left all about the room. Well drow warriors never were known
for neatness.

rooms.Name: Long Hallway
rooms.Description:
You are in a long hallway lined with adamantite. The walls are engraved with
pictures of elves and spiders. The hallway continues east and west. As you look
down the hallway you can make out one or two figures moving away from you.

rooms.Name: Grand Stairway
rooms.Description:
You are standing at the bottom of a giant obsidian and adamantite stairway.
The edges are trimmed with gold.

rooms.Name: Grand Hallway
rooms.Description:
You are standing in the middle of a grand hallway. The walls are of the
purest adamantite with gold trim. Mosaics line the walls.

rooms.Name: Mage's Barracks
rooms.Description:
The mage's living quarters is rather clean with the exception of a few used
component containers. It is rather well decorated as well. Cots line the floor
for the mages to sleep on. the only door is to the west.

rooms.Name: Grand Hallway
rooms.Description:
You are walking down a grand hallway, heavily decorated with adamantite and
gold. To the north the hall goes down a flight of stairs while a door is too
the west.

rooms.Name: Cleric's Barracks
rooms.Description:
The bed chamber is brightly decorated with spider shaped statues, murals and
the like. Large beds line the floor making this a comfortable room to live in.

rooms.Name: Grand Stairway
rooms.Description:
You are climbing a set of obsidian stairs surrounded by adamantite walls. To
the north are a set of large golden doors.

rooms.Name: Main Chamber
rooms.Description:
This is the south side of a large auditorium used for services by the drow
priestesses. In the center is a large sacrificial pit and beyond that is an
altar.

rooms.Name: Eastern Side of Chamber
rooms.Description:
You are on the eastern side of the chamber overlooking the pit. To the east
is a door while to the north is an altar.

rooms.Name: Sacrificial Pit
rooms.Description:
A you climb down into the pit, thousands of spiders cover you, tearing your
fragile body to shreds. Lloth thanks you for your sacrifice.

rooms.Name: Western Side of Chamber
rooms.Description:
You are on the western side of the main chamber overlooking a sacrificial
pit. To the north is an altar.

rooms.Name: The Altar
rooms.Description:
You are standing in front of a highly and freshly bloodstained altar.
Engraved on the top of the altar is a giant spider with a human head. Looking
down from the altar you see a large sacrificial pit with thousands of swarming
spiders looking for their next meal!

rooms.Name: Slave Cells
rooms.Description:
This is the main room to the cell chambers for the slaves to be sacrificed.
You notice there are no guards around.

rooms.Name: Slave Pen
rooms.Description:
Rotten meat and breads lie about the floor while shackles hang from the
walls. The room reeks of death. You almost become nauseous and decide to leave
the room since you were obviously too late to save the slave.

rooms.Name: Dias
rooms.Description:
You stand upon a dias behind the altar. Above you is a enormous illusion of
a female drow turning into a giant spider and back again. There is a door to
the west.

rooms.Name: The Treasury
rooms.Description:
This is obviously only a temporary storage place for the collected treasure
being rather bare.

rooms.Name: Weaponsmaster's Chamber
rooms.Description:
This one person bedchamber is very elegant. The owner must be held in
high regard to get this kind of treatment. 
§N

rooms.Name: Outside Redferne's residence
rooms.Description:
A huge cloud forms the plateau on which you are now standing. The wind here
is absolutely quiet and the sun is shining warmly upon you. From under the
cloud you can hear the faint sounds of Midgaard. Right before you to the north
lies the grand Mansion of Naris, the residence of the Greater God Redferne.

Exits.Description: You see a HUGE arched gate leading into this magnificent building.
You see a Huge Chain that anchors the Mansion of Naris to the ground.

rooms.Name: The Southern end of the hall
rooms.Description:
You are standing in a vast hall that is dimly lit, but from where the light
comes, is a mystery. The walls seem to radiate warmth and give the pleasant
feeling of being welcome here. A large portrait is hanging on one of the walls.
A large wooden staircase leads up into the tower. To the east there is a high
passage away from the hall. This ends shortly after by a tall oak door. The
enormous hall extends further north from here. To the south you can see a huge,
and VERY heavy- looking iron-wrought door. It looks like this is the only exit
from this magnificent old house. To the west you can see a large ashen door.

Exits.Description:
The hallway continues that way. You can see more doorways under the wooden
staircase in that direction.

You see there a tall oak door. It looks quite tightly closed to you. On it
little runes are chiseled into the wood.

Here you see a REAL door. It would be more proper to call this a "GATE", rather
than a "door". It's really HUGE! On it hangs a large sign with very large
letters spelling : "EMERGENCY EXIT".

This looks like a "door" in the meaning of the word. The ashen wood is painted
in a peculiar yellow color. Small letters are written with black on it.

You see the staircase extending upwards into the very high tower. It ends in
what seems like a large bedroom up there.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
These runes are utterly strange to you, but you are in luck today: Under
the runes you can just make out a sentence in Common.  It goes : " Stay out,
if you treasure your life.  That is if you are mortal.".
They read "LIBRARY".

rooms.Name: Redferne's Library
rooms.Description:
This is truly a magnificent place! Books and scrolls lie together on every
shelf. A large globe, with the map of the Mud-world upon it, stands in the
dimly lit north-western corner of the room. Two large and comfortable- looking
leather arm-chairs adorn the center of the library together with a huge oak
desk. Dim light radiates from an enormous crystal chandelier hanging down from
the ceiling approximately 10 feet off the floor. To the east there is a great
old ashen door. A large glass window is set in the west wall.

Exits.Description: You can see an old ashen door, painted in a peculiar yellow color.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
You see a large world map stretch out on the enormous globe.  It has towns
drawn in every spot available for such.  In the middle of the map you can
spot a large town with the name 'MIDGAARD' written over it.  The rest is
mountains, woods, plains and water.

You see a small speck with woods on the west from it, plains to the east
from it and mountains to the north from it.  To the south from it you can
see a thin trail lead to a large castle.  Finally you notice a rather large
river pour in from the east and go through Midgaard in the middle.

These two chair are exactly alike one another.  They look incredibly
comfortable.  They're both made from old leather, and yet they seem so worn
that they can be nothing but a perfect place for a long needed rest.

These windows are really BIG!  They reach from about 20 inches above the
floor to approximately 10 inches under the ceiling.  If you try and
"look out", you might see what might lie beyond these windows.

The clouds muster and form the ground on which this entire building is set.
Through the thinnest of the clouds you can just make out MIDGAARD with all
it's magnificent activity.

You see a large and winding river cut through the landscape, starting at an
enormous inland lake, it seeps through Midgaard and finally ends up in the
Grand Sea on the West-coast of the land.

rooms.Name: The Artifact room of Naris
rooms.Description:
This is gloomy and dark room with only a faint light radiating from the
walls. A bunch of funny-looking items fill the center of the room. There are no
furniture here what-so-ever. The only way out seems to be west, through the low
steel door.

Exits.Description: You see only the back of a safe's steel door.

rooms.Name: The Northern end of the hall
rooms.Description:
You are standing in the northern end of the huge hall. This part is under
the grand wooden staircase so the light seems a little less bright here, but
this doesn't bother your sight at all. To the north lies the kitchen. To the
south lies the Southern end of the hall. To the east there is a huge metal
door. To the west there is a large aspenwood door.

Exits.Description:
You see a huge metal door. From it a foul stench emanates. The smell is the
most awful experience in your entire life. A thought seeps through this
terrible stench and into your mind : "Monsters", you feel BAD about opening
that door.
The rest of the hall lies in that direction, and so does the exit.

The door has "SITTING ROOM" written on it. It is made from Aspenwood and is
beautifully carved with small elves as main issue of sculpture.

rooms.Name: The Sitting room of Naris
rooms.Description:
You are standing in the middle of a really comfortable place. The walls are
decorated with paintings of smiling Kings and Queens. The most attractive
picture is one of a Prince in shiny armor. By one of the walls there is an old
arm-chair. The only exit is through the aspenwood door to the east.

Exits.Description:
The door seems to be a very HEAVY door, carved completely from the trunk of an
Aspen tree.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: This is truly a wonderful relic of the past.  In it is a large cushion.

rooms.Name: The Kitchen of Naris
rooms.Description:
This must be the place of food and drink. You can hear the faint noise of
rats feasting on meat and bread from somewhere indeterminable. The sound makes
you feel the agony of HUNGER. The only visible exit is south to the Northern
end of the hall.

Exits.Description:
It's dark in there. But the sounds from there are unmistakable. The rats are
here to your information.
You can see the fridge from here. In it are drinks all over.
You can see the northern end of the hall.

rooms.Name: The Larder
rooms.Description:
You can see food all over. Among the heaps of food you notice HUGE rats
scuttling around, nibbling pieces off the heaps here and there.

rooms.Name: The Fridge
rooms.Description: This place is LOADED with drink, water and booze.

rooms.Name: On the stairs
rooms.Description:
You can see up and down the stairway. It seems to take forever, either going
up OR down. It's just a seemingly insurmountable climb, either way. Up is the
bedroom of Redferne, and Down leads to the Southern end of the hall.

rooms.Name: The Treasure room
rooms.Description:
This place is gloomy. A HUGE safe is cemented into the west wall. The only
visible exit is west, through the oak door.

Exits.Description: You see a tall oak door.

rooms.Name: Redferne's Bedroom
rooms.Description:
This is a snugly set bedroom with all the necessities for a romantic
evening. A large fireplace adorns the east wall, and sizzling away is the wood
that is ablaze within. The bed is enormous, covering at least HALF of this
great room. This stretches at least 140 square feet, so can you imagine the
BED? A large staircase leads down to the hall. A couple of doors open up to a
broad balcony to the south.

Exits.Description: The suns seems to shine out there, warmly and comforting.

rooms.Name: The Balcony of Redferne's Residence
rooms.Description:
You see a splendid of the most of this world. The valleys stretch as far as
the eye reaches to the south from here. Down below you can see the entrance of
this magnificent building. To the north are the doors to Redferne's Bedroom.

Exits.Description:
You see the comfortable bedroom of Naris, the mansion of Redferne the Greater
God.

You see the ground on which this castle is set. Funnily it seems to you that
it's no more than clouds.

rooms.Name: The Monster Pen
rooms.Description:
This looks like the cage in which a large carnivore is being kept. Judging
by the state the walls are in, this could very well be a large AGGRESSIVE
animal. This makes you pretty insecure, this stating your feeling about the
place quite mildly.

Exits.Description: This looks like the only exit from here.

rooms.Name: On the Huge Chain
rooms.Description:
This place has quite a good view over Midgaard. Your possibilities of
movement seems to extend only to up and down. Unless you want to let go of the
secure and seemingly unmovable chain, then those are the directions you should
take from here.

Exits.Description: Up the way you see the chain disappearing into the clouds above.
Down below you see the huge chain anchored to the ground in the Road Crossing.

rooms.Name: The Chain where it's too windy
rooms.Description:
Hanging on to the chain you figure out that there's no way of leaving down
from here. The wind pulls you from left to right and back. This seems like a
totally impossible task. The ascend is the only way ahead for you. Otherwise
you would risk death by falling to the hard ground below. DO NOT DESCEND NOW OR
YOU'LL SURELY DIE!!!!

Exits.Description: That way seems to be the only way away from here.

THAT WAY IS CERTAIN DEATH!!!! You can see the wind tearing at the chain down
below you. It swings like a furious serpent from side to side! The descend is
ABSOLUTELY out of the QUESTION.

rooms.Name: On the Great Chain of Naris
rooms.Description:
You are approximately on the middle of the treacherous Chain. One false step
and death will come and collect you quickly. The chain leads upwards and down.
No way are you going to descend now... You've only just begun your climb.
Besides it could cost you your life. Look down and you'll see why.

Exits.Description: There seems to be only one way from here and that's up.

The chain down there is swinging wildly back and forth. Going down there will
be pretty risky!

rooms.Name: The Chain
rooms.Description:
As you descend, the chain seems to absorb all weather around it, making it
swing less and less in the very powerful wind tearing at it. The Chain seems to
chuckle quietly, and as you descend further you hear a soft whisper originating
from within the Chain *ITSELF*. It says, " Welcome back some other time,
stranger. Your company is always ... hmmm ... interesting. God Speed. " The
chain extends further down through the now spreading clouds.

Exits.Description:
It seems to you that the Chain is dissolving again. Maybe it's just an
illusion, but still ... !
That way seems safe enough ... now.

rooms.Name: The Mighty Chain of Naris
rooms.Description:
This place truly a splendid view of the WHOLE COUNTRY SIDE!!! A magnificent
light shines upon you and the way up through the clouds is opened. Up there you
can now see the Mansion of Naris, Residence of the Greater God Redferne. The
chain beneath you seems to evaporate in the mustering clouds that surround you
by now.

Exits.Description:
You see the sunny top of the clouds. Beyond these, the Mansion towers before
your eyes. Beautiful!!

You see nothing but the thick clouds. They've closed completely around the
Chain.

rooms.Name: Free fall from the Chain
rooms.Description:
This is probably the third worst place to be in this entire MUD right now.
You fall . . . and fall . . . and fall . . . and HIT THE GROUND WITH SUCH A
*SPLUTCH* that you die horribly, but instantly. Bye Cruel World. You lose all
your things immediately, Sorry!!

rooms.Name: The Room that will be
rooms.Description:
This is the room that is the one that will be something when you have decided
to do something about it,now that it has become something from nothing

Exits.Description: room willbe

rooms.Name: A long tunnel
rooms.Description:
You encounter some rapids as you enter this tunnel cut out of the
mountains by the river.

rooms.Name: A long tunnel
rooms.Description: The tunnel branches off north.

rooms.Name: A long tunnel
rooms.Description: The tunnel branches off south.

rooms.Name: A long tunnel
rooms.Description: The tunnel branches off to the south.

rooms.Name: An underground lake
rooms.Description:
A underground lake opens up eastly. It looks seminatural as most have
been carved by eons of flowing water but some parts have been, improved,
chopped away by someone who did not think this lake was large enough.
Small passages lead off both south and north while the dark river takes
you westly.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The lake is jet-black and there is a constant dripping of water and lime
from above.

rooms.Name: A long narrow drainage tunnel
rooms.Description:
The tunnel descends slightly to the east to allow possible drained
water to pour easily. The tunnel walls are close and you can almost feel
the narrowing even more to the east. Westly you can hear the distant
sound of water dripping.

rooms.Name: A long narrow drainage tunnel
rooms.Description:
The tunnel descends slightly to the east and then abruptly dives down
into a brightly lit hole. This must be where all drain water go. What can
soak up such amounts of water? Westly,and slightly up the drain tunnel
continue.

rooms.Name: Cave-in
rooms.Description:
You stand at the edge of a large pile of rubble created from the last
rock slide.

Exits.Description: You can easily slide down the rocks without getting hurt.

rooms.Name: At the foot of the rubble
rooms.Description:
You are at the bottom of a large pile of rubble. A tunnel branches off
to the north and east.

rooms.Name: Cave entrance
rooms.Description:
You stand in the middle of a large and beautiful cave. A path leads
deeper into the darkness.

Exits.Description: You look down into the cave. Bones are strewn about everywhere.

rooms.Name: Giant cave
rooms.Description:
This cavern overwhelms you. The walls and ceiling seem miles away.
Bones of previous adventurers lie strewn on the cavern floor.

rooms.Name: Narrow bend
rooms.Description: The tunnel turns to the south and west.

rooms.Name: Large cave
rooms.Description:
You are standing in a large cave. Many furs are spread out on the
floor.

rooms.Name: Damp hallway
rooms.Description: The walls here are extremely damp, as well as the floor.

Exits.Description: You hear drops of water.

rooms.Name: Underground pool
rooms.Description: You are wading in a knee deep pool of lime-water.

rooms.Name: Damp hallway
rooms.Description:
The walls of the tunnel are extremely damp here. You hear the faint
sound of running water to the south.

Exits.Description: You hear drops of water.

rooms.Name: Narrow crawlway
rooms.Description:
This crawlway is just big enough for a human to crawl through or a
halfling to walk through.

Exits.Description: You smell the fragrant odor of fungus.

rooms.Name: Large cavern
rooms.Description:
You have entered a very large cavern. The rock formations would amaze
almost any dwarf.

rooms.Name: Fungus patch
rooms.Description:
As you walk through the fungus patch, you are shot at by many millions
of spores. You can hardly breathe.

Exits.Description: The fragrant smell of fungus spores continues to the east.

rooms.Name: Fungus path
rooms.Description:
As you walk along the path, millions of spores are shot at you. It is
difficult to breathe.

Exits.Description: A giant mushroom temple stands to the south.
The fragrant smell of spores continues to the west.

rooms.Name: Fungus temple
rooms.Description:
You find yourself standing inside of a giant mushroom. The inside is
decorated in the fashion of a temple.

rooms.Name: Sloping passage
rooms.Description: You follow a path sloping down from the fungus temple.

rooms.Name: Sloping passage
rooms.Description: You are on a path that gently slops up from the underground pool.

Exits.Description: You hear sounds of trickling water.

rooms.Name: The Great Eastern Desert
rooms.Description:
A vast desert stretches for miles, the sand constantly shifting around
you. A pyramid lies to the east and a snow-capped mountain range to the
west.

Exits.Description: Sand as far as the eye can see.
Sand as far as the eye can see.
Sand as far as the eye can see.

Exits.Description:

from huge blocks of stone that have been coated over with a rough sandy

you might be able to climb it.

rooms.Description:

around you. A pyramid lies to the south-west and a deep canyon to the
east. Just below you can make out a tiny ledge.

Exits.Description: Sand as far as the eye can see.
Sand as far as the eye can see.

around you. A pyramid lies to the west and a deep canyon to the east.

Exits.Description: Sand as far as the eye can see.

A rickety rope bridge stretches across the canyon... it doesn't look too
safe.

rooms.Name: A nomad camp
rooms.Description:
This small group of desert nomads has stopped for the day to rest and
refresh themselves beside this beautiful oasis. Three tents and some
camels make up the party. From within two of the tents you hear muffled
voices, obviously surprised at your visit.

Exits.Description: Some camels are tied up to a mass of stakes plugged into the ground.

You see inside one of the tents a huddled mass of people, probably
slaves.
Sand as far as the eye can see.
Sand as far as the eye can see.

rooms.Name: Inside a small tent
rooms.Description:
This is a small and simple tent with few possessions in sight. Lying
here and there are young-looking men and women, possibly slaves to the
leader of this band.

Exits.Description: You see the center of the nomad camp.

rooms.Name: Beside the camels
rooms.Description:
Here stand about ten camels, all hitched to some stakes plugged into
the ground. To the east you see a small tent while to the north you see a
larger, fancier tent.

Exits.Description:
This tent seems to be the temporary abode of the nomad leader. You make a
mental note to visit it before you leave.
In this tent there are very large men, all carrying weapons.
You see the center of the nomad camp.
Sand as far as the eye can see.

rooms.Name: The warrior's tent
rooms.Description:
This tent has a few furnishings, but mainly it holds the band's
protectors. They all stare at you coldly as you enter.

Exits.Description: Outside you see some peaceful camels.

rooms.Name: The main tent
rooms.Description:
This tent is as lavishly decorated on the inside as it is on the
outside. A fancy carpet lies on the sand and numerous baskets line the
walls.

Exits.Description: You see some peaceful camels.

rooms.Name: The main tent
rooms.Description:
This is where the leader of this band of nomads resides. He is
definitely rich as you inspect the tapestries, baskets, and a few
paintings as well.

Exits.Description: You see the entrance to this tent.

rooms.Name: The rickety rope bridge
rooms.Description:
You carefully begin to walk across the bridge, but suddenly the rope
breaks and you fall...

... and fall and fall and fall ...

                to your death on the rocks below.

rooms.Name: The wind-swept ledge
rooms.Description:
Being very careful not to lose your balance, you look around and find
that this canyon is about a half a kilometer deep. To the west is a dark
cave leading under the desert sands and above you a rope bridge spans the
gap.

Exits.Description: The desert sands blow down in your face.

rooms.Name: The cavemouth
rooms.Description:
The air in here is MUCH cooler than outside. From the west you hear
strange sounds, but can see nothing. The cave slopes down into the
darkness.

Exits.Description: Outside is lighter and very windy.

rooms.Name: The mysterious lair
rooms.Description:
You have stumbled upon the home of something. From the treasure
haphazardly strewn about and the rotting carcasses, you would guess that
this is a dragon's lair. As to what type, you can't really say. The cave
narrows out into a tunnel to the west.

rooms.Name: A wide tunnel
rooms.Description:
This tunnel seems to go on forever into the darkness. You carefully
feel your way along the walls.

rooms.Name: A narrower tunnel
rooms.Description:
The tunnel becomes very narrow and you fight to squeeze your way
through. The floor seems to level off a little.

rooms.Name: A narrow crack
rooms.Description:
This part of the tunnel is the hardest to move through as the walls
move in to meet you.

rooms.Name: A small cavern
rooms.Description:
It is dark and damp and bats hang from the ceiling. A narrow crack is
in the east wall. The floor now slopes upwards.

rooms.Name: A small shaft
rooms.Description:
From within this shaft you can see a narrow hole in the roof just
large enough for one person. Back east is the cavern.

rooms.Name: The Great Eastern Desert
rooms.Description:
A vast desert stretches for miles, the sands constantly shifting
around you. You are standing below a gigantic pyramid floating about 100
meters above the ground. To your left hangs a rope which leads straight
up to the massive structure. From here you can sense the great evil which
resides within.

Exits.Description: Sand as far as the eye can see.
Sand as far as the eye can see.
Sand as far as the eye can see.
Sand as far as the eye can see.

The rope leads up to a hole in the pyramid. A shadowy figure hovers over
the rope looking down at you.

rooms.Name: Hanging on the rope
rooms.Description:
About half way up the rope you feel it begin to shake and shudder. You
desperately try to shimmy back down the rope, but it unravels and...
SNAP!!!!!
As you plummet to the ground, you look up to see a shadowy figure in the
pyramid grinning an evil grin and brandishing a shiny dagger.

Exits.Description: A looooong way down.

rooms.Name: Lost in the Desert
rooms.Description:
Blinking to clear the sand from your eyes, you try and get some idea
of where you are. The problem is, every direction looks the same sand
as far as the eye can see, and a haze of sandy dust hanging over
everything. You have heard that people wandering in the desert
see mirages, which is undoubtably what that long stairway is, just on
the horizon, after all - who would build a stairway in the middle of
the desert?

Exits.Description: You can't see much through the desert haze.
You can't see much through the desert haze.
You can't see much through the desert haze.
You can't see much through the desert haze.

rooms.Name: South west corner of a underground lake
rooms.Description:
The underground lake continues north and east. The seminatural cave
have been carved by eons of flowing water but some parts have been,
improved, chopped away by someone who did not think this lake was large
enough.

rooms.Name: On a underground lake
rooms.Description:
The dark water lie almost still with the exception of whatever stir
you might cause. Looking around in the cave you are in you can see from
the roof that it is only seminatural as someone has been improving
transportability over this lake by removing, what you think were, certain
stone formations. The route is now open for whoever sails these dark 
waters. The lake surround you in all horizontal directions.

rooms.Name: North west corner of a underground lake
rooms.Description:
The underground lake continues south and east. The seminatural cave
have been carved by eons of flowing water but some parts have been,
improved, chopped away by someone who did not think this lake was large
enough.

rooms.Name: Up on a buoy metal construct
rooms.Description:
The metal construct is bolted into the very cave ceiling, causing the
buoy to be fixated. As you think of it, you realize that there is no
other way if you want to measure the water level. If it was floating it
would just follow the surface. A work of dwarf geniousity, be sure of it.

rooms.Name: Below a buoy
rooms.Description:
The buoy is NOT fixated to anything. How could it then measure the
water level. If it floats it just floats revealing nothing!
Around you the water is dark, but you can still see a pile of rubble
lying on the lake bed.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
A large load of stones. As you examine it closer you notice a skeletal
hand streching out from below it.

On the rather large hand, at least seen with human standards, you see a
rusty knuckle duster. Engraved on it is, still today clearly visible, the
name 'GRIFO'. Poor bugger. You leave him and his belongings be as you are
pretty sure that someone was rather displeased with him.

rooms.Name: A small quay
rooms.Description:
Apperantly this part of the underground lake is travelled by people 
that actually use this shipping route. They frequently anchor up here 
while waiting for something, perhaps their turn in line or they are just 
readying their ship for a longer journey. The cave wall is smooth and 
there are clear signs that someone has improved this part of the 
underground cave to better fit ships. Toward the north the underground 
lake stretches out its dark arms.

rooms.Name: On a underground lake
rooms.Description:
The dark water lie almost still with the exception of whatever stir
you might cause. Looking around in the cave you are in you can see from
the roof that it is only seminatural as someone has been improving
transportability over this lake by removing, what you think were, certain
stone formations. The route is now open for whoever sails these dark 
waters. The lake surround you in all horizontal directions.

rooms.Name: Next to a buoy
rooms.Description:
In the centre of the underground lake a large buoy floats. It has got
colourful circles painted around its body and on top there is a high
metal construct with some signs on, that reach up to the cave ceiling.
Around you the dark water strech out in all directions as far as you can
see.

Exits.Description: You can climb the metal construct on top of the buoy.
You can dive down into the water and examine how the buoy is fixated.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The lines are most presumably water level indicators, showing how deep
down it is to the cave ground.

The signs read :

                                *Midgaard*


*Dwarven Undermountain Harbour Town*            *Drainage*


                                  *Quay*


On the *drainage* sign someone has scrabbled down som more text.

"Griffo Orc was heere"

Obviously some kind of vandal that wanted to be know. But you never heard
of him so one could guess he never really succeded.

rooms.Name: On a underground lake
rooms.Description:
The dark water lie almost still with the exception of whatever stir
you might cause. Looking around in the cave you are in you can see from
the roof that it is only seminatural as someone has been improving 
transportability over this lake by removing, what you think were, certain 
stone formations. Now the ceiling is high enough for sailing ships 
even though there is no wind. The lake surround you in all horizontal
directions, but north, where a small channel leads off into the mountain.

rooms.Name: On a underground water channel
rooms.Description:
The water channel is wide enough only for one vessel, so you better
hope that noone bigger than you is going the opposite direction. The
channel coninue north while it seems to open up to the south.

rooms.Name: South east corner of a underground lake
rooms.Description:
The underground lake continues north and west. The seminatural cave
have been carved by eons of flowing water but some parts have been,
improved, chopped away by someone who did not think this lake was large
enough.

rooms.Name: On a underground lake
rooms.Description:
The dark water lie almost still with the exception of whatever stir
you might cause. Looking around in the cave you are in you can see from
the roof that it is only seminatural, as someone has been improving
transportability over this lake by removing, what you think were, certain
stone formations. The route is now open for whoever sails these dark
waters. The lake surround you in all horizontal directions.

rooms.Name: Northeast corner of a underground lake
rooms.Description:
The underground lake continues south and west. The seminatural cave
have been carved by eons of flowing water but some parts have been,
improved, chopped away by someone who did not think this lake was large
enough.

rooms.Name: East side of a underground lake
rooms.Description:
A small drain have been carved out, making a small tunnel that lead 
off eastly into the mountain, from the eastmost part of a underground lake
that strech out westly. The drain is probably used during the spring
flood to limit the water level of this underground basin.

rooms.Name: A water channel
rooms.Description:
The submountain water channel leads you north or south depending of
your targeted destination and of course depending on the big traffic
ships, that one has to avoid in the narrow tunnel. If one of them come 
down the channel, you are clearly a potential wallsmear. There really is 
no room to meet, so the biggest vessel goes first, or through if unlucky..

rooms.Name: A water channel
rooms.Description:
The submountain water channel leads you north or south depending of
your targeted destination and of course depending on the big traffic
ships that one has to avoid in the narrow tunnel. There really is no room
to meet, so the biggest vessel goes first.

rooms.Name: A water channel
rooms.Description:
The submountain water channel leads you east or south depending of
your targeted destination and of course depending on the big traffic
ships that one has to avoid in the narrow tunnel. There really is no room
to meet, so the biggest vessel, or the ones with the biggest fog horn,
goes first.

rooms.Name: A water channel
rooms.Description:
The submountain water channel leads you west or north depending of
your targeted destination and of course depending on the big traffic
ships that one has to avoid in the narrow tunnel. There really is no room
to meet, so what appears to be the biggest vessel, goes first.

rooms.Name: A water channel
rooms.Description:
The submountain water channel leads you north or south depending of
your targeted destination and of course depending on the big traffic
ships, that one has to avoid in the narrow tunnel. Be on your guard for 
large waves or the warning sound of a ship fog horn.

rooms.Name: A water channel
rooms.Description:
The tunnel is quite narrow and it seems that only one standard size 
cargo ship can pass along the tunnel at the time. There really is no 
room to meet, so you would better stay out of the way when a boat glides 
by. North and south is your choise of way and you should hurry before 
three is a boat coming.

rooms.Name: A water channel
rooms.Description:
The submountain water channel goes north or south in a narrow dug out 
tunnel, where there is no room for you AND a boat. So it is strongly 
suggested to keep out of the way, when the cargo ships glide by at a very 
short distance. The sound of the ships fog horns can be a signal about a 
incoming danger, but far from all use that feat.

rooms.Name: A Final room - filled with comments
rooms.Description:
Enter Comments Below:
Rooms #05-#07 was edited and #75-#99 created as a entry to zone 132.
Dwarven Undermountain Harbour Town                      -Egba.


There is no room #00, #74, #80, #81, #82
Add R4 to 50.zon file for room #85

rooms.Name: #bThe Entrance to the Kai Citadel#N
rooms.Description:
A huge citadel is outlined against the sky, overlooking the city of
Midgaard. The massive bronze doors to this fortress stand open, and you
somehow feel welcome. No guards defend this place, and the sounds that 
are normally heard in the castles of the Elite world are not heard here.
Whatever lies within, this place is at peace. Above the door you see a
huge stone archway with some writing on it. You can go south, back into
Midgaard, or north, into the citadel. You also see a #N#bplaque#N on the wall
here that may bear furthur reading.
§N

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Carved from a single piece of marble, this archway supports the south
facing wall of the citadel. Inscribed across the top of the archway is
the Kai Credo. It reads:

           "Honour, Fellowship, Courage, Respect, Loyalty."
§N

It reads:
A lot of work was put into this house, especially the extra descriptions!
If you see a work of interest such as plaque, sign, statue, anything, try
to look at it! Often, there is a detailed description attached. We, the 
builders of the Kai Fortress, hope you like it, and you are *more* then
welcome to look around and use our facilities. 
-Nymph and Rilarien
§N

rooms.Name: #bInside the Citadel#N
rooms.Description:
You are standing in a darkened hallway, massive marble pillars holding up
the arched ceiling all along the length of the hall. Carved into each pillar is
a statue, presumably of some past hero. You can follow the hallway north, or go
to one of the two rooms here. There is a small plaque on one of the pillars.

Exits.Description: The hallway to the north is dark.
You catch a glimpse of some books to the east.
You can see sunlight from here.
The doorway here is framed with massive claymores.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Stern, stalwart, deadly, Fang was the Kai of Honour and Courage. He helped 
those he deemed worthy, and had no patience for those who were incompetent.
Years of battle changed him, and he became much respected for who he was, 
as well as for his unmatched ability with the sword.

Beautiful, elegant, slender frame belying great power, Karen Eth Lanier 
was the trusted ally of Ben Kenobi and succeeded where he failed. The two 
fought many great battles side by side, for Karen is the Kai of Skill.

A slender robed figure carved in stone, with deep scars and determined 
gaze. Ben Kenobi was the Kai of respect, once beloved by his people, and 
cast aside when he lost his faith in them.

These are the semblances of the mightiest of the old Kai. Look upon them 
well, for they each symbolize a facet of what you aspire to be. The 
legendary Ben Kenobi, the vengeful Fang, and the mighty Karen Eth Lanier.

rooms.Name: #bDarius's Library#N
rooms.Description:
This dusty room's walls are lined with shelves filled with old tomes. 
There are desks and pedestals throughout the chamber, some with books in
them.  A few notable titles catch your eye.. "The Rise and Fall of the
Jedi"... "The Crimson Apocalypse"... "The Credo".... and "Arcane Arts".
Someone has been reading them and they have ornate bookmarks keeping them
at an assigned page. If you wish, you can stay here and study, or you can
leave to the west.  Occasionally the librarian Darius can be seen reading 
some ancient tome here.
§N

Exits.Description: There is fresh air this way, it must be the way out.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: You try but fail to understand the holy words.

The Credo of the Kai is written on this page:
"Courage is not the absence of fear, it is acting in spite of it. To 
accept defeat is a courageous act, but to keep on trying in spite of it, 
therin lies true greatness."

You scan the open pages and a passage catches your eye:
"And the young gods rose up and slew their elders, in the mighty war to 
end all wars, at the end of the world. And lo did one who called himself 
Fish rise above the battle and rebuild his world, claiming it for him, 
and remaking it as he wished, and he made himself its Lord. Those who did 
not side with the usurper were smitten by his hand, until none opposed 
his subjugation."

The Book Reads:
"Mighty were the Jedi, those who helped others before themselves. 
Tales of Kris, Ben, Karen and Lanceor are no longer told in the world of 
Crimson, for the Apocalypse has changed much, and the Jedi, a dying breed 
after their return, have faded into obscurity. Many traveled through the 
portal to another world and were never seen again. Others, like Karen Eth 
Lanier, who led after Ben Kenobi was slain by the gods, achieved grace 
and now are immortal. But the Jedi are no more."

rooms.Name: #bThe Kai Training Hall#N
rooms.Description:
This empty chamber has weapons lining the walls, and it obviously doubles
for an armoury. On the far wall beyond a glowing forcefield are 4 weapons,
legendary artifacts from another world. A pure white blade, a crackling black
sword, a solid mithril mace and a long war spear. The Kai also use this room to
stock spare equipment. New warriors are always welcome to look here should
they have need of beginning equipment!
§N

Exits.Description: You see the dark hallway.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
This is the mighty Sword of Glory, the weapon of the Kai. It was brought 
to this world by Ben Kenobi, and is kept here, as he is no longer worthy 
to wield such a blade.

This is the deadly Stormblade, hidden by the elves until the dragon Santa 
plundered their castles and completed their quests. When it fell into his 
hands, all who were good trembled with fear, and no-one dared oppose him.

This is the holy Mace of Disruption, brought to this world by the warrior 
maiden Kris. Thought lost, it surfaced recently and has been kept here 
ever since. Many undead creatures were blasted into oblivion at Kris's hands.

This is Vangar's Spear, wielded by the mighty general of the Crimson 
World. No-one knows how it arrived in Elite, but here it is kept, lest it 
fall into the wrong hands.

rooms.Name: #bArched Hallway#N
rooms.Description:
The large hallway continues. There are more pillars with statues carved into
them here, and there is a plaque on one support. If you wish, you can follow
the hall north or south, or you can enter one of the two doorways here to see
what lies beyond. A spiral staircase also leads up from here. §N

Exits.Description: The hallway continues to the north.
There is a large chamber to the east.
The hallway continues to the south.
There is a large chamber to the west.
There is a portal going up.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
She was Ben's teacher, his instructor, and one of the prime creation gods 
of the world of Crimson. He was also dark and self-serving, using his 
status among his peers to garner power for himself. It is hard to 
determine the gender of this statue.. it seems to change from each angle. 
Trinity has not been seen since the Apocalypse, although it is rumored he 
still lives in the world of Crimson.

A stern questor, searching wanderer, he left the realms of the gods to 
escape their hatred, and returned for the caring of a friend and the love 
of a woman. Almost a father to young Ben, he was cast aside after the 
Apolapyse, and is occasionally seen wandering the world of Elite.

A lovely angel carved in marble of startling purity and innocence. The 
smile on her lips hides the sadness she has endured. She gazes, almost 
lovingly, across the room at the statue of Terrock, her lover.

This is the room of the dead gods. The gods who once held power in the 
world of Crimson, but fell after the Apocalypse. Chani and Terrock are 
not the powers they once were, and Trinity has vanished totally.

rooms.Name: #bThe Kai Barracks#N
rooms.Description:
These are the sleeping quarters of the Kai, where they rest between their
rigorous adventures. If you need to rest, rest here, for the magic of the Kai
ensures that you cannot be harmed within this room. Indeed, some claim that
those who tend their wounds here heal much faster than anywhere else! Also,
the food you see here is for people resting here, often left by kind-hearted
Kai for less fortunate people. Please contribute! There is a map on the 
wall here, with a plaque beneath it.
§N

Exits.Description: The hallway is through this door.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
#bRoom#N   
                                      /  |   
                                     / #bCouncil#N   
                                    /   
                           #bWoR#N -- #bEoH#N  -- #bAsh#N

#bMAP KEY
-------#N

Ash - Ashen-Shugar's Room  WoR - Worship Room
EoH - End of Hall          Wil - Willow's Room
DaM - Dakkon's Maze        Atl - Atlantis's Room (register of Kai is here)
Elh - Elder Hall           Cat - Catwoman's Playroom
Dar- Darren's Room        Flg - Flagg's Room 
Zif - Zifnab's Room        ArH - Arched Hallway
InC - Inside Citidel       Ent - Entrance

Arm- Armory. NOTE: this room is for low level players only.
     High level players taking equip from this room is *HIGHLY*
     frowned on.

       Map courtesy of the Kai and the Keeper of the Citidel
§N

rooms.Name: #bHallway of the Elders#N
rooms.Description:
This long hallway is beautifully decorated, with a scarlet red carpet
covering the length. Doors line this hall, presumably leading to the private
rooms of various notable Kai. You can follow the hallway to the east or the
west, or open on of the doors here. The door to the south has the is engraved
with the name "Flagg".
§N

rooms.Name: #bThe End of the Hallway#N
rooms.Description:
The long hallway ends here, at a spiral staircase. Massive granite pillars
support the ceiling; some have speckles of obsidian in them, and they all have
ornately carved statues gracing them. There is a plaque on one pillar. You can
go through either of the doorways to the east or the west, or you can climb the
stairs to the next level of the citadel.

Exits.Description: A faint red portal shimmers here.
The room to the east is surprisingly well lit!
The hallway continues to the south.
The doorway to the west is small and you cannot see in the room.
The stairs climb in a spiral.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Once the friend of Ben Kenobi, the two grew apart, and became bitter 
enemies. Thirdstone despised Ben, and envied him, and sought to defeat 
him and take his place. Before all the people of Crimson, the young Jedi 
slew the evil Thirdstone, and drove him off with the aid of Fang. 
Thirdstone hasn't been seen in the world of Elite for over 2 decades.

A robed figure with dagger in hand, face hidden by a hood, almost solid 
obsidian. One of the most respected and powerful gods of his time, he was 
one of the first to arrive in Elite. The cause of his death is uncertain,
